title: Safety, Tolerability and Antiviral Activity of GST ‐ HG131 in Chronic Hepatitis B: A Randomized, Double‐Blind Phase IIa Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Current therapies rarely achieve a functional cure due to low rates of HBsAg clearance, the persistence of the viral replication template—covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA)—and the need for lifelong treatment. GST‐HG131 is a first‐in‐class, orally bioavailable small‐molecule inhibitor of PAPD5/7, key host factors involved in HBV mRNA stabilization and HBsAg production. We evaluated the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST‐HG131 in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) therapy in a randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled Phase IIa study. Methods This double‐blind, randomized, placebo‐controlled Phase IIa study evaluated the efficacy and safety of GST‐HG131 in 45 CHB patients. Cohorts 1 and 2 ( n = 10 each; 8 active, 2 placebo) received 30 mg or 60 mg BID for 28 days, respectively. Cohort 3 ( n = 25; 20 active, five placebo) received 30 mg BID for 12 weeks. All participants were on nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy for more than 6 months, with HBsAg between 100 and 1500 IU/mL, and serum ALT below 1× ULN. Results At Day 28, HBsAg reductions were −0.65 log 10 IU/mL in the 30 mg BID 28‐day group and −0.53 log 10 IU/mL in the 60 mg BID 28‐day group. The 30 mg BID 12‐week group showed a greater reduction of −0.89 log 10 IU/mL at the end of treatment versus placebo ( p 50% reduction in HBsAg with a maximum decrease of 1.64 log 10 IU/mL. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12‐week group achieved HBsAg below 100 IU/mL. Rebounds in HBsAg were observed following treatment discontinuation. GST‐HG131 was well tolerated, with no dose‐related toxicity or emerging safety concerns across all cohorts. Conclusion GST‐HG131, a first‐in‐class oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, demonstrated favourable safety and significant HBsAg reduction in patients with CHB. The greatest antiviral activity was observed after 12 weeks of treatment, supporting further clinical development of GST‐HG131 as a component of functional cure strategies for CHB. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06263959

title_zh: GST-HG131在慢性乙型肝炎中的安全性、耐受性和功能性治愈活性:一项随机、双盲IIa期研究
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major global health burden. Current therapies rarely achieve a functional cure due to low rates of HBsAg clearance, the persistence of the viral replication template—covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA)—and the need for lifelong treatment. GST‐HG131 is a first‐in‐class, orally bioavailable small‐molecule inhibitor of PAPD5/7, key host factors involved in HBV mRNA stabilization and HBsAg production. We evaluated the safety, tolerability and antiviral activity of GST‐HG131 in patients with CHB receiving nucleos(t)ide analogue (NUC) therapy in a randomized, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled Phase IIa study. Methods This double‐blind, randomized, placebo‐controlled Phase IIa study evaluated the efficacy and safety of GST‐HG131 in 45 CHB patients. Cohorts 1 and 2 ( n = 10 each; 8 active, 2 placebo) received 30 mg or 60 mg BID for 28 days, respectively. Cohort 3 ( n = 25; 20 active, five placebo) received 30 mg BID for 12 weeks. All participants were on nucleos(t)ide analog monotherapy for more than 6 months, with HBsAg between 100 and 1500 IU/mL, and serum ALT below 1× ULN. Results At Day 28, HBsAg reductions were −0.65 log 10 IU/mL in the 30 mg BID 28‐day group and −0.53 log 10 IU/mL in the 60 mg BID 28‐day group. The 30 mg BID 12‐week group showed a greater reduction of −0.89 log 10 IU/mL at the end of treatment versus placebo ( p 50% reduction in HBsAg with a maximum decrease of 1.64 log 10 IU/mL. Notably, 76.5% of patients in the 12‐week group achieved HBsAg below 100 IU/mL. Rebounds in HBsAg were observed following treatment discontinuation. GST‐HG131 was well tolerated, with no dose‐related toxicity or emerging safety concerns across all cohorts. Conclusion GST‐HG131, a first‐in‐class oral PAPD5/7 inhibitor, demonstrated favourable safety and significant HBsAg reduction in patients with CHB. The greatest antiviral activity was observed after 12 weeks of treatment, supporting further clinical development of GST‐HG131 as a component of functional cure strategies for CHB. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06263959
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景与目的 慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎,CHB)仍然是一个重大的全球健康负担。当前的治疗方法由于HBsAg清除率低、病毒复制模板——共价闭合环状DNA(共价闭合环状DNA)的持续存在以及需要终生治疗,很少能达到功能性治愈。GST‐HG131是一种第一类口服小分子PAPD5/7抑制剂,PAPD5/7是HBV mRNA稳定和HBsAg生成的关键因子。我们评估了GST‐HG131在使用核苷(酸)类似物(NUC)治疗的CHB患者中的安全性和耐受性及抗病毒药物活性,在一项随机、双盲、安慰剂对照的Phase IIa研究中进行了研究。方法 这是一项随机、双盲、安慰剂对照的Phase IIa研究,评估了GST‐HG131在45例CHB患者中的疗效和安全性。队列研究 1和2(每组10例;8例活性药物,2例安慰剂)分别接受30 mg或60 mg BID,共28天。队列研究 3(25例;20例活性药物,5例安慰剂)接受30 mg BID,共12周。所有参与者均接受核苷(酸)类似物单药治疗超过6个月,HBsAg在100至1500 IU/mL之间,血清ALT低于1×ULN。结果 在第28天,30 mg BID 28天组的HBsAg减少为−0.65 log10 IU/mL,60 mg BID 28天组的HBsAg减少为−0.53 log10 IU/mL。12周的30 mg BID组在治疗结束时的HBsAg减少更为显著,为−0.89 log10 IU/mL,与安慰剂组相比(p<0.05),实现了50%以上的HBsAg减少,最大减少为1.64 log10 IU/mL。值得注意的是,12周组中有76.5%的患者实现了HBsAg低于100 IU/mL。在治疗停药后观察到HBsAg反弹。GST‐HG131耐受性良好,未出现剂量相关毒性或新的安全问题。结论 GST‐HG131,一种第一类口服PAPD5/7抑制剂,在CHB患者中表现出良好的安全性和显著的HBsAg减少。抗病毒药物活性在12周的治疗后达到最大,支持GST‐HG131作为CHB治疗策略组成部分的进一步临床开发。临床试验注册 ClinicalTrials.gov标识符:NCT06263959

title: Global Underutilization of Antiviral Therapy and Survival Outcomes in Hepatitis B Virus‐Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis of 78 Studies and 68,243 Patients
abstract: Antiviral therapy with nucleos(t)ide analogues is recommended for patients with viremic hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis regardless of levels of viremia or liver enzymes. However, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is not an antiviral treatment criterion in the U.S. HBV treatment guidelines, though prior studies have reported improved survival with antiviral treatment in HBV-related HCC. To inform guidelines, we estimated antiviral treatment rates and their association with survival and HCC recurrence rates in HBV-related HCC. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2006 and 2024 that reported antiviral treatment, survival, and/or HCC recurrence rates in adults with HBV-related HCC, following PRISMA guidelines. Random-effects models pooled study estimates. Of the initial 4556 studies, 178 underwent full-text review, and 78 (68,243 patients) were analysed. The pooled antiviral treatment rate (52 studies, 41,345 patients) was 53.1%. In studies reporting pre-HCC antiviral initiation, 17.2% of HBV-related HCC patients received therapy before diagnosis. Treated (vs untreated) patients had higher 3- and 5-year OS (80.4% vs. 46.8%, both p < 0.01). Five-year OS was 78.0% vs. 56.4% in inactive HCC (p < 0.01) and 48.2% vs. 22.6% in active HCC (p = 0.14). Antiviral therapy remained independently associated with improved 5-year OS in multivariable meta-regression. There was no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates. Antiviral therapy is associated with improved long-term survival but remains underutilized in HBV-related HCC. These findings highlight a critical gap in care and underscore the need for earlier and more consistent antiviral initiation in patients with HBV-related HCC.

title_zh: 全球抗病毒药物疗法在乙型肝炎病毒相关肝细胞癌中的应用不足及其生存结局:一项纳入78项研究和68,243名患者的系统综述和荟萃分析
source_body_en: Antiviral therapy with nucleos(t)ide analogues is recommended for patients with viremic hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis regardless of levels of viremia or liver enzymes. However, hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is not an antiviral treatment criterion in the U.S. HBV treatment guidelines, though prior studies have reported improved survival with antiviral treatment in HBV-related HCC. To inform guidelines, we estimated antiviral treatment rates and their association with survival and HCC recurrence rates in HBV-related HCC. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published between 2006 and 2024 that reported antiviral treatment, survival, and/or HCC recurrence rates in adults with HBV-related HCC, following PRISMA guidelines. Random-effects models pooled study estimates. Of the initial 4556 studies, 178 underwent full-text review, and 78 (68,243 patients) were analysed. The pooled antiviral treatment rate (52 studies, 41,345 patients) was 53.1%. In studies reporting pre-HCC antiviral initiation, 17.2% of HBV-related HCC patients received therapy before diagnosis. Treated (vs untreated) patients had higher 3- and 5-year OS (80.4% vs. 46.8%, both p < 0.01). Five-year OS was 78.0% vs. 56.4% in inactive HCC (p < 0.01) and 48.2% vs. 22.6% in active HCC (p = 0.14). Antiviral therapy remained independently associated with improved 5-year OS in multivariable meta-regression. There was no significant difference in HCC recurrence rates. Antiviral therapy is associated with improved long-term survival but remains underutilized in HBV-related HCC. These findings highlight a critical gap in care and underscore the need for earlier and more consistent antiviral initiation in patients with HBV-related HCC.
abstract_zh: 使用核苷(酸)类似物进行抗病毒药物治疗被推荐用于所有具有病毒血症的乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)相关肝硬化的患者,无论其病毒载量或肝酶水平如何。然而,肝细胞癌(HCC)并不是美国HBV 治疗指南中的治疗标准。尽管之前的研究报告指出,在HBV相关HCC患者中,抗病毒药物治疗与改善生存率相关,但目前仍缺乏明确的指南。为了指导指南制定,我们估计了抗病毒药物治疗率及其与生存率和HCC复发率之间的关联。我们按照PRISMA指南,对2006年至2024年间发表的、报告了HBV相关HCC成人患者抗病毒药物治疗率、生存率和/或HCC复发率的研究进行了系统综述和荟萃分析。使用随机效应模型汇总研究估计值。初始共有4556项研究,其中178项进行了全文审查,最终分析了78项(共68,243名患者)。汇总的抗病毒药物治疗率(52项研究,41,345名患者)为53.1%。在报告了HCC前抗病毒药物治疗启动的研究中,17.2%的HBV相关HCC患者在HCC发生前接受了治疗。接受治疗(与未接受治疗相比)的患者3年和5年总生存率(OS)更高(80.4% vs. 46.8%,两者p < 0.01)。在非活动性HCC研究中,5年OS为78.0% vs. 56.4%(p < 0.01),而在活动性HCC研究中,5年OS为48.2% vs. 22.6%(p = 0.14)。在多变量荟萃回归分析中,抗病毒药物治疗仍与改善5年OS独立相关。HCC复发率没有显著差异。抗病毒药物治疗与改善长期生存率相关,但在HBV相关HCC中仍被低估使用。这些发现突显了护理中的关键差距,并强调了在HBV相关HCC患者中更早和更一致地启动抗病毒药物治疗的必要性。

title: Hepatitis B and C Virus Among Prisoners in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: ObjectiveTo estimate the pooled prevalence and identify transmission drivers of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections among incarcerated populations in sub-Saharan Africa.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following a search encompassing Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and free-text terms from database inception through February 2025. Data were synthesized from 26 studies involving 77,760 prisoners across sub-Saharan Africa. A random-effects model was used to calculate pooled prevalence estimates, assess regional variation, and evaluate odds ratios (OR) for potential transmission risk factors.ResultsThe overall pooled prevalence was 13.0% for HBV and 8.0% for HCV among prisoners. Significant regional disparities were observed, with West Africa presenting the highest HBV burden (16.3%) and East Africa showing the highest HCV burden (8.8%). Key independent predictors of infection included sharing sharp objects (OR, 1.98), tattooing (OR, 1.92), and intravenous drug use (OR, 1.38).ConclusionIncarcerated populations in sub-Saharan Africa experience a high burden of viral hepatitis driven by parenteral exposure and high-risk sexual interactions. Addressing these gaps requires targeted screening, comprehensive harm reduction, condom provision, and integrating prison health services into national elimination strategies.
journal: Journal of the International Association of Providers of AIDS Care

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence and identify transmission drivers of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections among incarcerated populations in sub-Saharan Africa. The evidence base included 26 studies with 77,760 prisoners, and a random-effects model was used to calculate pooled prevalence and assess risk factors. The overall pooled prevalence was 13.0% for HBV and 8.0% for HCV, with significant regional disparities observed. West Africa had the highest HBV burden (16.3%), while East Africa had the highest HCV burden (8.8%). Key risk factors included sharing sharp objects, tattooing, and intravenous drug use. The review highlights the need for targeted screening, harm reduction, and integration of prison health services into national strategies to address the high burden of viral hepatitis in this population.

title: Evaluating the potential of treatment options for chronic hepatitis B
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a leading cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide, but long-term or even lifelong viral suppression with nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) seldom clears hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), so-called 'functional cure.' In recent years, a shift in treatment strategy from viral suppression toward cure has emerged, catalyzed by three revised international hepatitis B guidelines (2025-2026) and the first-in-class phase 3 evidence that a finite antiviral therapy, the antisense oligonucleotide bepirovirsen, can achieve a functional cure in about one in five NA-suppressed CHB patients with baseline HBsAg below 3000 IU/mL. AREAS COVERED: We evaluated the spectrum of established and emerging treatment options for CHB, organized around quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) as the axis for selecting and sequencing therapy. Coverage spans backbone NAs and pegylated interferon-α, an HBsAg-guided roadmap, finite NA therapy and off-treatment outcomes, bepirovirsen, other virus-targeting and immunomodulatory agents, and genome-directed covalently closed circular DNA silencing and editing. EXPERT OPINION: Bepirovirsen's approaching approval is an inflection point. qHBsAg should guide personalized, sequential therapy, with partial cure (HBsAg < 100 IU/mL) as a potential intermediate target when functional cure is unlikely. Durability, standardized biomarkers, rational combination design, metabolic co-management and equitable access are the priorities; a sterilizing cure remains distant.

title: Finite Versus Indefinite Nucleos(t)ide Analogue Therapy in HBeAg‐Negative Chronic Hepatitis B: Meta‐Analysis of Randomized Trials.
abstract: Continuous nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) effectively maintains viral suppression but rarely results in functional cure. Finite NA therapy has been proposed to increase rates of HBsAg loss; however, international guidelines provide conflicting recommendations. This study compares the efficacy and safety of finite versus continuous NA therapy in HBeAg-negative adults using randomized controlled trials. We included parallel-group randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) cessation versus continuation in non-cirrhotic, virally suppressed HBeAg-negative adults. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed risk of bias using Cochrane RoB 2. Random-effects Mantel-Haenszel meta-analyses with Hartung-Knapp adjustment and Paule-Mandel estimation were used to pool risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Certainty of evidence was assessed using the GRADE approach. Four RCTs (n = 357) met inclusion criteria. Discontinuation increased HBsAg loss vs. continuation (RR 5.02, 95% CI: 0.47-53.47; I2 = 21.8%; low certainty), corresponding to ~53 additional losses per 1000 patients. However, finite therapy markedly increased virologic relapse (RR 23.09) and retreatment (RR 21.94) while reducing sustained off-therapy virologic response (RR 0.46). Post-cessation ALT flares were frequent but self-limited or resolved with retreatment. No hepatic decompensation or serious adverse events occurred. In monitored, non-cirrhotic adults, finite NA therapy may increase the probability of HBsAg loss despite predictable relapse and retreatment. With no evidence of severe harm, these findings support finite therapy as a selective, patient-centered strategy toward functional cure in expert centers.

title: Superior Efficacy of Besifovir in Reducing Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk Compared to Tenofovir in Chronic Hepatitis B Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Besifovir dipivoxil maleate (BSV) is a novel therapeutic option for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB). However, its long-term effectiveness in reducing the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Korean Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service database from 2018 to 2022. A total of 32,383 patients with CHB were included (BSV, n = 2,358; tenofovir disoproxil fumarate [TDF], n = 30,025). Propensity score matching was conducted at a 1:3 ratio to minimize selection bias. The primary outcome was the incidence of HCC, with cirrhosis development as the secondary endpoint. RESULTS: In the overall population, 57 cases of HCC were reported in the BSV group (2,358 individuals, 5,918 person-years), while 1,268 cases of HCC were reported in the TDF group (30,025 individuals, 83,587 person-years). After propensity score matching, the incidence of HCC was significantly lower in the BSV group (9.63 per 1,000 person-years; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.43-12.49) than in the TDF group (15.36 per 1,000 person-years; 95% CI, 13.72-17.18), with an incidence rate ratio of 1.59 (P = 0.001). This protective effect remained consistent in both cirrhotic (hazard ratio [HR], 1.609; P = 0.028) and non-cirrhotic subgroups (HR, 1.831; P = 0.002). CONCLUSION: BSV treatment demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing the risk of HCC compared to TDF, regardless of baseline cirrhosis status. These findings suggest that BSV may provide enhanced protection against HCC in patients with CHB.

title_zh: Besifovir在降低慢性乙型肝炎(慢性乙型肝炎)患者肝细胞癌风险方面相较于Tenofovir的优越效果:一项全国范围的队列研究研究。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Besifovir dipivoxil maleate (BSV) is a novel therapeutic option for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB). However, its long-term effectiveness in reducing the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Korean Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service database from 2018 to 2022. A total of 32,383 patients with CHB were included (BSV, n = 2,358; tenofovir disoproxil fumarate [TDF], n = 30,025). Propensity score matching was conducted at a 1:3 ratio to minimize selection bias. The primary outcome was the incidence of HCC, with cirrhosis development as the secondary endpoint. RESULTS: In the overall population, 57 cases of HCC were reported in the BSV group (2,358 individuals, 5,918 person-years), while 1,268 cases of HCC were reported in the TDF group (30,025 individuals, 83,587 person-years). After propensity score matching, the incidence of HCC was significantly lower in the BSV group (9.63 per 1,000 person-years; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.43-12.49) than in the TDF group (15.36 per 1,000 person-years; 95% CI, 13.72-17.18), with an incidence rate ratio of 1.59 (P = 0.001). This protective effect remained consistent in both cirrhotic (hazard ratio [HR], 1.609; P = 0.028) and non-cirrhotic subgroups (HR, 1.831; P = 0.002). CONCLUSION: BSV treatment demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing the risk of HCC compared to TDF, regardless of baseline cirrhosis status. These findings suggest that BSV may provide enhanced protection against HCC in patients with CHB.
abstract_zh: 背景:Besifovir二甲基马来酸盐(BSV)是慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)的一种新型治疗选择。然而,其在降低肝细胞癌(HCC)风险方面的长期效果仍不清楚。方法:我们使用韩国健康保险审查与评估服务数据库,从2018年至2022年进行了一项回顾性队列研究。共纳入32,383名CHB患者(BSV组,n = 2,358;替诺福韦二甲基苯甲酸酯[TDF]组,n = 30,025)。采用1:3的倾向评分匹配方法以减少选择偏倚。主要结局是HCC的发病率,而肝硬化的发展作为次要终点。结果:在总体人群中,BSV组报告了57例HCC(2,358人,5,918人年),而TDF组报告了1,268例HCC(30,025人,83,587人年)。倾向评分匹配后,BSV组的HCC发病率显著低于TDF组(BSV组为9.63例每1,000人年;95%置信区间[CI]为7.43-12.49),而TDF组为15.36例每1,000人年(95% CI为13.72-17.18),发病率比为1.59(P = 0.001)。这种保护作用在肝硬化(风险比[HR]为1.609;P = 0.028)和非肝硬化亚组(HR为1.831;P = 0.002)中均保持一致。结论:无论基线肝硬化状态如何,BSV在降低HCC风险方面均显示出优于TDF的疗效。这些发现表明,BSV可能为慢性乙型肝炎患者提供更强的HCC防护作用。

title: Burden of liver fibrosis and steatosis coexisting with hepatitis B or C infection in China: a population-based study from the 2020 National Serological Survey.
abstract: Background The burden of liver fibrosis and steatosis coexisting with hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections in China remains to be quantified. Objective To estimate the prevalence of HBV or HCV infection with liver fibrosis and steatosis to inform national elimination strategies. Design This study was conducted among individuals aged 15–69 years in the 2020 National Serological Survey of Viral Hepatitis in China. Among participants with HBV or HCV infection, liver fibrosis and steatosis were assessed using vibration-controlled transient elastography. Weighted prevalence and population estimates of HBV or HCV infection coexisting with liver fibrosis and steatosis were calculated. Results Among 69 351 participants, 4236 had HBV infection and 122 had HCV infection. The weighted population prevalence of HBV and HCV infection with ≥F2 fibrosis was 0.63% (95% CI 0.52% to 0.77%) and 0.05% (95% CI 0.03% to 0.08%), accounting for an estimated 6.08 million and 0.48 million individuals in China, respectively. The corresponding prevalence of steatosis was 1.82% (95% CI 1.56% to 2.13%) and 0.06% (95% CI 0.04% to 0.10%), accounting for an estimated 17.30 million and 0.61 million individuals respectively. Diagnosis rates were 59.78% for HBV infection and 38.02% for HCV infection, and treatment rates were 7.60% and 48.66% respectively. Conclusion China continues to face a substantial burden of advanced liver disease among people with viral hepatitis, further compounded by the high prevalence of liver steatosis. Proactive case-finding and linkage to care are essential to achieving elimination of viral hepatitis as a public health threat.

abstract_zh: 背景:在中国,肝纤维化和脂肪变性共存于乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)和丙型肝炎病毒(HCV)感染中的负担尚未量化。目的:估计HBV或HCV感染伴肝纤维化和脂肪变性的患病率,以为国家消除策略提供信息。设计:本研究在2020年中国病毒性肝炎全国血清学调查中,对年龄15–69岁的个体进行。对HBV或HCV感染的参与者,使用振动控制瞬时弹性成像评估肝纤维化和脂肪变性。计算了HBV或HCV感染共存肝纤维化和脂肪变性的加权患病率及人口估计。结果:在69 351名参与者中,4236例为HBV感染,122例为HCV感染。HBV和HCV感染伴≥F2纤维化的加权人口患病率分别为0.63%(95% CI 0.52%至0.77%)和0.05%(95% CI 0.03%至0.08%),对应估计的6.08 million和0.48 million个体。相应的脂肪变性患病率为1.82%(95% CI 1.56%至2.13%)和0.06%(95% CI 0.04%至0.10%),对应估计的17.30 million和0.61 million个体。诊断率分别为HBV感染的59.78%和HCV感染的38.02%,治疗率分别为7.60%和48.66%。结论:中国继续面临病毒性肝炎患者中大量晚期肝病负担,且肝脂肪变性的高患病率进一步加重。积极的病例发现和护理链接对于实现将病毒性肝炎消除为公共卫生威胁至关重要。

title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Hepatitis B and/or C Virus Infections among Medical Waste Handlers in Ethiopia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
abstract: Health systems around the world are severely impacted by hepatitis B Virus and hepatitis C Virus, particularly in low- and middle-income nations. These viruses are still more common in Ethiopia even with preventive efforts including the hepatitis B vaccine, universal precautions, and occupational safety procedures. There is little information available on their frequency and related variables among Ethiopian medical waste handlers. The purpose of this meta-analysis and systematic review was to ascertain the prevalence of hepatitis B and/or C in this population as well as its contributing factors. Different databases, including PubMed, Science Direct, Cochrane, Hinari, Google Scholar, grey literature, and articles from different university repository sites, were examined in order to locate available publications. Five studies with a total sample size of 1,211 participants were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis. The data was extracted and sorted using Microsoft Excel version 13 before being sent to STATA/MP 17.0 for analysis. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used to assess each study’s quality. The pooled prevalence of the hepatitis B and C virus was examined using a Der Simonian random-effects model with a 95% confidence interval. The Egger’s test and I 2 were used to evaluate publication bias and heterogeneity. The possible cause of heterogeneity was assessed using both subgroup analysis and meta-regression. P-values less than 0.05 were considered statistically significant. The pooled prevalence of hepatitis B and/or C viruses among Ethiopian medical waste handlers was 13% (95% CI: 5–21%), according to the findings of this comprehensive study and meta-analysis. Significant heterogeneity is shown in the Galbraith plot, with I 2 = 96.21% ( p < 0.001). The prevalence of hepatitis B and/or C viruses was 11.3%, according to studies conducted until the year 2020. However, studies included less than 260 participants found that the prevalence of the hepatitis B and/or C virus was 14.90%. This study found that having multiple sexual partners and prior exposure to sharp objects were associated with Hepatitis B Virus and/or Hepatitis C Virus infection among medical waste handlers. These findings highlight the role of behavioral and occupational factors in hepatitis transmission. Therefore, reducing infection risk requires promoting safe sexual practices and strengthening infection prevention and control measures in healthcare settings.

abstract_zh: 全球卫生系统正受到乙型肝炎病毒和乙型肝炎病毒的严重冲击,尤其是在低收入和中等收入国家。即使有包括乙型肝炎病毒疫苗、普遍预防措施和职业安全程序在内的预防措施,这些病毒在埃塞俄比亚仍然较为常见。目前关于埃塞俄比亚医疗废物处理人员中这些病毒的流行率及其相关变量的信息仍然有限。本项系统综述和荟萃分析的目的是确定该人群中乙型和/或丙型肝炎的患病率及其影响因素。为了寻找相关文献,我们查阅了包括PubMed、Science Direct、Cochrane、Hinari、Google Scholar、灰色文献以及不同大学文献库在内的多个数据库。本系统综述和荟萃分析共纳入了五项研究,总样本量为1,211名参与者。数据使用Microsoft Excel版本13进行提取和整理,然后导入STATA/MP 17.0进行分析。采用Newcastle-Ottawa量表评估每项研究的质量。使用Der Simonian随机效应模型,结合95%置信区间,分析了乙型和丙型肝炎病毒的综合患病率。采用Egger检验和I 2检验评估发表偏倚和异质性。通过亚组分析和元回归评估异质性的可能原因。P值小于0.05被认为具有统计学意义。根据这项全面的研究和荟萃分析,埃塞俄比亚医疗废物处理人员中乙型和/或丙型肝炎病毒的综合患病率为13%(95% CI:5–21%)。Galbraith图显示存在显著异质性,I 2 = 96.21%(p < 0.001)。截至2020年的研究显示,乙型和/或丙型肝炎病毒的患病率为11.3%。然而,样本量少于260的研究发现,乙型和/或丙型肝炎病毒的患病率为14.90%。本研究发现,拥有多个性伴侣和之前接触尖锐物体与医疗废物处理人员中乙型肝炎病毒和/或丙型肝炎病毒的感染有关。这些发现突显了行为和职业因素在肝炎传播中的作用。因此,降低感染风险需要推广安全的性行为实践,并加强医疗保健环境中的感染预防和控制措施。

title: Realizing personalized prediction for the reversal of chronic hepatitis B-associated liver fibrosis through machine learning
abstract: Although long-term antiviral therapy can reverse liver fibrosis in a considerable proportion of patients with chronic hepatitis B, treatment response differs markedly among individuals, and reliable methods for predicting who will benefit remain lacking. Conventional clinical tools such as liver stiffness measurement and the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index were originally dewsigned for cross-sectional staging rather than longitudinal prediction, and their ability to capture the dynamic process of fibrosis reversal is limited. In this opinion review, we discuss how machine learning (ML) may help address this unmet need. We focus on three areas where ML has shown early but encouraging results: Quantitative analysis of images using ML, integration of pathological and clinical data through multimodal models, and dynamic prediction of treatment response based on serial measurements during antiviral therapy. In our view, the greatest value of ML lies not in replacing existing assessment tools but in complementing them, particularly through the early identification of patients who are unlikely to achieve fibrosis reversal with antiviral therapy alone. However, we also caution that most current models have been developed from small, single-center retrospective cohorts, and their clinical adoption will require prospective multi-center validation, improved model interpretability, and adherence to standardized reporting frameworks.

abstract_zh: 尽管长期抗病毒药物治疗可以逆转慢性乙型肝炎患者的肝纤维化,但个体对治疗的反应差异显著,目前仍缺乏可靠的预测方法。传统的临床工具如肝硬度测量和天门冬氨酸氨基转移酶与血小板比值指数最初设计用于横断面分期,而非纵向预测,其捕捉纤维化逆转动态过程的能力有限。在本观点综述中,我们讨论了机器学习(ML)如何帮助解决这一未满足的需求。我们重点关注了机器学习在三个方面的早期但有希望的结果:利用机器学习进行图像的定量分析、通过多模态模型整合病理和临床数据,以及基于抗病毒药物治疗期间的连续测量动态预测治疗反应。我们认为,机器学习的最大价值并不在于取代现有评估工具,而在于补充它们,特别是在早期识别那些仅通过抗病毒药物治疗难以实现纤维化逆转的患者方面。然而,我们也提醒,目前大多数模型都是基于小规模、单中心的回顾性队列研究开发的,其临床应用需要前瞻性多中心验证、提高模型的可解释性以及遵循标准化的报告框架。

title: The long noncoding RNA MAPKAPK5-AS1 promotes the formation of hepatitis B virus cccDNA by modulating the expression of NABP1
abstract: Cellular long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have been shown to participate in diverse biological pathways, including the regulation of virus infections. However, their functions in the hepatitis B virus (HBV) life cycle still need to be explored. Here, we conducted a loss-of-function screen targeting 1779 human lncRNAs and identified 19 lncRNAs associated with HBV infection. One lncRNA, named MAPKAPK5-AS1 (lnc-MAAS), was identified as a host factor required for HBV infection. Our data suggest that lnc-MAAS is involved in the conversion of HBV relaxed circular DNA into covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA). Furthermore, mechanistic experiments revealed that lnc-MAAS affects cccDNA formation by modulating the expression of nucleic acid binding protein 1 (NABP1). Together, our findings shed light on the roles of host lnc-MAAS and NABP1 in HBV cccDNA formation, which may contribute to the development of novel anti-HBV therapeutics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the role of host long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in the hepatitis B virus (HBV) life cycle, addressing the need to understand the mechanisms underlying HBV infection and cccDNA formation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A loss-of-function screen targeting 1779 human lncRNAs was conducted to identify host factors involved in HBV infection, focusing on the HBV life cycle in human cells.
analysis.methods: The study employed a loss-of-function screen to identify lncRNAs associated with HBV infection, followed by mechanistic experiments to elucidate the role of a specific lncRNA, lnc-MAAS, in cccDNA formation.
analysis.main_results: The study identified lnc-MAAS as a host factor required for HBV infection and found that it affects cccDNA formation by modulating the expression of NABP1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that lnc-MAAS plays a crucial role in HBV cccDNA formation through the regulation of NABP1 expression, providing new insights into the mechanisms of HBV infection and potentially contributing to the development of novel anti-HBV therapeutics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study’s findings could inform the development of novel anti-HBV therapeutics by targeting lnc-MAAS and NABP1, which may help in the management of chronic hepatitis B and related complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s limitations include the use of a loss-of-function screen, which may not fully capture the complexity of the HBV life cycle, and the need for further validation of the findings in clinical settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study identified lnc-MAAS as a host factor required for HBV infection and found that it modulates NABP1 expression to affect cccDNA formation, providing new insights for potential anti-HBV therapeutics.

title: Effect of Hepatitis B virus X T118N mutant protein in HepG2 cell cycle and apoptosis regulation
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) belongs to Hepadnaviridae family and caused liver infection. HBV infection can develop into hepatocellular carcinoma, one of which is due to presence of HBV X protein (HBx). Some mutations are known to be associated with development of liver carcinoma, for instance HBx K130M/V131I (HBx_KV). In Indonesia, HBx T118N (HBx_T) has been found at similar frequency as the HBx_KV. This study aims to examine the effect of HBx T118N mutant on cell cycle and apoptosis regulation. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this study, analysis of CyclinE, p21, Bax, and Bcl-2 gene expression was performed using RT-qPCR. Cell cycle and apoptosis analysis was done using flowcytometry with PI and Annexin V-PI staining, respectively. Caspase 3 activity assay was performed using CaspACETM Colorimetric Assay Kit. The presence of HBx_T mutant increased CyclinE expression at 72 h post transfection, similarly to HBx_KV. Both Bax and Bcl-2 mRNA level were also increased HepG2 cells expressing HBx_T in comparison to HBx_KV expression at 72 h post transfection. HBx_T expression in HepG2 cells at 48 h post transfection caused increase of AnnexinV+/PI- and AnnexinV+/PI+ cell populations, as compared to HBx_wt expression. CONCLUSIONS: Our data suggests that HBx_T influences cell cycle and apoptosis regulation in slightly different mechanism to HBx_KV. Further investigations are still required to understand HBx_T mutant involvement in development of chronic liver disease and liver cirrhosis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to examine the effect of HBx T118N mutant on cell cycle and apoptosis regulation in HepG2 cells, addressing the need to understand the role of this specific HBV mutation in liver disease development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used HepG2 cells and analyzed the effect of HBx T118N mutant protein on cell cycle and apoptosis regulation through gene expression analysis and flow cytometry.

title_zh: 乙型肝炎病毒 X T118N突变蛋白对HepG2细胞周期和凋亡调控的影响
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) belongs to Hepadnaviridae family and caused liver infection. HBV infection can develop into hepatocellular carcinoma, one of which is due to presence of HBV X protein (HBx). Some mutations are known to be associated with development of liver carcinoma, for instance HBx K130M/V131I (HBx_KV). In Indonesia, HBx T118N (HBx_T) has been found at similar frequency as the HBx_KV. This study aims to examine the effect of HBx T118N mutant on cell cycle and apoptosis regulation. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this study, analysis of CyclinE, p21, Bax, and Bcl-2 gene expression was performed using RT-qPCR. Cell cycle and apoptosis analysis was done using flowcytometry with PI and Annexin V-PI staining, respectively. Caspase 3 activity assay was performed using CaspACETM Colorimetric Assay Kit. The presence of HBx_T mutant increased CyclinE expression at 72 h post transfection, similarly to HBx_KV. Both Bax and Bcl-2 mRNA level were also increased HepG2 cells expressing HBx_T in comparison to HBx_KV expression at 72 h post transfection. HBx_T expression in HepG2 cells at 48 h post transfection caused increase of AnnexinV+/PI- and AnnexinV+/PI+ cell populations, as compared to HBx_wt expression. CONCLUSIONS: Our data suggests that HBx_T influences cell cycle and apoptosis regulation in slightly different mechanism to HBx_KV. Further investigations are still required to understand HBx_T mutant involvement in development of chronic liver disease and liver cirrhosis.
abstract_zh: 背景:乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)属于Hepadnaviridae科,可引起肝感染。HBV感染可发展为肝细胞癌,其中部分原因是由于HBV X蛋白(HBx)的存在。一些突变已被证实与肝癌的发生有关,例如HBx K130M/V131I(HBx_KV)。在印度尼西亚,HBx T118N(HBx_T)的出现频率与HBx_KV相似。本研究旨在探讨HBx_T突变蛋白对HepG2细胞周期和凋亡调控的影响。方法和结果:本研究使用RT-qPCR分析CyclinE、p21、Bax和Bcl-2基因的表达。细胞周期和凋亡分析通过流式细胞术进行,分别使用PI和Annexin V-PI染色。Caspase 3活性检测使用CaspACETM比色法试剂盒。HBx_T突变蛋白在转染后72小时增加了CyclinE的表达,与HBx_KV类似。在转染后72小时,与HBx_KV相比,表达HBx_T的HepG2细胞中Bax和Bcl-2 mRNA水平也有所增加。HBx_T在HepG2细胞中于转染后48小时表达时,导致AnnexinV+/PI-和AnnexinV+/PI+细胞群体的增加,与HBx野生型表达相比。结论:我们的数据表明,HBx_T对细胞周期和凋亡调控的影响机制与HBx_KV略有不同。仍需进一步研究以了解HBx_T突变在慢性肝病和肝硬化发展中的作用。

title: Hepatic Steatosis in People With Chronic Hepatitis B in Africa: Prevalence, Correlates, and Clinical Significance.
abstract: To address data gaps around metabolic liver disease in Africa, within the Hepatitis B in Africa Collaborative Network (HEPSANET), we evaluated participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection (CHB) for steatotic liver disease (SLD) using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Using multivariable logistic regression, we identified sociodemographic, anthropometric, and clinical associations with SLD (CAP ≥ 248 dB/m), and evaluated whether SLD severity was independently associated with fibrosis. Short-term impacts of SLD on mortality were also assessed with Cox proportional hazards analysis. We also evaluated the diagnostic performance of B-mode ultrasound for SLD, with CAP as reference. Across 6 countries and 1601 participants (age range, 12-80 years; 39.5% female; 4% with diabetes; 11% unhealthy alcohol use; median body mass index, 24.4), 421 (26.3%) had SLD; 219 (13.7%) had severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). Older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV-negative status were associated with SLD. After adjusting for age, sex, HIV status, HBV treatment, and country, severe steatosis, but not mild and moderate forms (i.e., 248-279 dB/m), was associated with a 8.4% (95%, 1.9%-14.9%) increased probability of fibrosis. Over limited follow-up (median 2.69 years) and small number of deaths, SLD was not associated with all-cause or liver-related mortality. B-mode ultrasound had low sensitivity for SLD, overall or when severe, but specificity was 95%. In conclusion, SLD was common in people with CHB in Africa and its severe form was associated with liver fibrosis. These data support screening for metabolic comorbidities as part of HBV care and treatment in Africa.
authors: Hepatitis B in Africa Collaborative Network (HEPSANET)

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address data gaps on metabolic liver disease in Africa by evaluating participants with chronic hepatitis B virus infection for steatotic liver disease using transient elastography with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). The research was conducted across six countries involving 1601 participants, with 421 (26.3%) found to have SLD and 219 (13.7%) with severe steatosis (CAP ≥ 280 dB/m). The study identified sociodemographic, anthropometric, and clinical factors associated with SLD, including older age, male sex, overweight and obesity, and HIV-negative status. After adjusting for various factors, severe steatosis was linked to an increased probability of fibrosis. However, SLD was not associated with mortality during limited follow-up. The findings highlight the importance of screening for metabolic comorbidities in HBV care and suggest that severe steatosis may be a marker for fibrosis. The study's limitations include its short follow-up period and small number of deaths, which may affect the strength of conclusions about mortality.

title: Ultrasound findings across liver fibrosis stages defined by transient elastography in patients with chronic hepatitis B in Georgia
abstract: PURPOSE: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major cause of chronic liver disease and may progress to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aimed to evaluate conventional abdominal ultrasound (US) findings across liver fibrosis stages defined by transient elastography (TE) in patients with CHB. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 232 adults with CHB were included. Conventional abdominal US and TE data were available for 231 patients. US findings were evaluated in relation to liver fibrosis stages defined by TE-derived liver stiffness measurements. Differences in liver stiffness according to US findings were assessed using the independent-samples t-test. RESULTS: Patients with heterogeneous liver echotexture had significantly higher liver stiffness than those with normal liver echotexture (8.71 ± 6.89 vs. 5.65 ± 1.30 kPa; mean difference, 3.06 kPa; 95% CI 1.78-4.34 kPa; p < 0.001). Patients with splenomegaly had significantly higher liver stiffness than those without splenomegaly (17.31 ± 15.18 vs. 6.55 ± 2.82 kPa; mean difference, 10.77 kPa; 95% CI 2.00-19.54 kPa; p = 0.020). Among the 231 patients, 71.9% were classified as F0-F1, 21.6% as F2-F3, and 6.5% as F4. Four patients were diagnosed with HCC, including three with cirrhosis (F4) and one with F0-F1 fibrosis. CONCLUSIONS: Conventional abdominal US findings, particularly heterogeneous liver echotexture and splenomegaly, were associated with higher liver stiffness in patients with CHB. These findings support the complementary role of conventional abdominal US in the comprehensive non-invasive evaluation of patients with CHB.

title_zh: 在佐治亚州慢性乙型肝炎患者中,根据瞬时弹性成像定义的肝纤维化阶段的超声检查发现
source_body_en: PURPOSE: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) remains a major cause of chronic liver disease and may progress to liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aimed to evaluate conventional abdominal ultrasound (US) findings across liver fibrosis stages defined by transient elastography (TE) in patients with CHB. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 232 adults with CHB were included. Conventional abdominal US and TE data were available for 231 patients. US findings were evaluated in relation to liver fibrosis stages defined by TE-derived liver stiffness measurements. Differences in liver stiffness according to US findings were assessed using the independent-samples t-test. RESULTS: Patients with heterogeneous liver echotexture had significantly higher liver stiffness than those with normal liver echotexture (8.71 ± 6.89 vs. 5.65 ± 1.30 kPa; mean difference, 3.06 kPa; 95% CI 1.78-4.34 kPa; p < 0.001). Patients with splenomegaly had significantly higher liver stiffness than those without splenomegaly (17.31 ± 15.18 vs. 6.55 ± 2.82 kPa; mean difference, 10.77 kPa; 95% CI 2.00-19.54 kPa; p = 0.020). Among the 231 patients, 71.9% were classified as F0-F1, 21.6% as F2-F3, and 6.5% as F4. Four patients were diagnosed with HCC, including three with cirrhosis (F4) and one with F0-F1 fibrosis. CONCLUSIONS: Conventional abdominal US findings, particularly heterogeneous liver echotexture and splenomegaly, were associated with higher liver stiffness in patients with CHB. These findings support the complementary role of conventional abdominal US in the comprehensive non-invasive evaluation of patients with CHB.
abstract_zh: 目的:慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)仍是慢性肝病的主要原因之一,可能进展为肝纤维化、肝硬化和肝细胞癌(HCC)。本研究旨在评估慢性乙型肝炎患者中根据瞬时弹性成像(TE)定义的肝纤维化阶段的常规腹部超声(US)发现。方法:本研究为横断面研究,纳入了232名慢性乙型肝炎患者。231名患者的常规腹部超声和瞬时弹性成像数据可用。超声发现与根据TE得出的肝硬度测量定义的肝纤维化阶段进行了评估。使用独立样本t检验评估根据超声发现的肝硬度差异。结果:肝回声纹理异质性的患者肝硬度显著高于肝回声纹理正常的患者(8.71 ± 6.89 vs. 5.65 ± 1.30 kPa;平均差异3.06 kPa;95% CI 1.78-4.34 kPa;p < 0.001)。脾肿大的患者肝硬度显著高于无脾肿大的患者(17.31 ± 15.18 vs. 6.55 ± 2.82 kPa;平均差异10.77 kPa;95% CI 2.00-19.54 kPa;p = 0.020)。在231名患者中,71.9%被归类为F0-F1,21.6%为F2-F3,6.5%为F4。4名患者被诊断为HCC,其中3名伴有肝硬化(F4),1名伴有F0-F1纤维化。结论:慢性乙型肝炎患者的常规腹部超声发现,特别是肝回声纹理异质性和脾肿大,与较高的肝硬度相关。这些发现支持常规腹部超声在慢性乙型肝炎患者全面无创评估中的补充作用。

title: Becoming Physically Active and Risks of Mortality and Liver-Related Events in Adults With Chronic Hepatitis B: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
abstract: Physical activity (PA) confers several health benefits; however, whether increasing PA among physically inactive adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is associated with lower risks of adverse clinical outcomes remains unclear. We used the nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database. We included 318,131 adults with CHB who were physically inactive at the initial health screening (Exam 1) and completed a subsequent screening within 4 years (Exam 2). Among them, 58,703 initiated moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA), defined as vigorous activity ≥ 20 min/day on ≥ 3 days/week or moderate activity ≥ 30 min/day on ≥ 5 days/week. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcomes were liver-related events (hepatic decompensation, liver transplantation, hepatocellular carcinoma [HCC]) and HCC. Multivariable Cox and Fine-Grey competing-risk models were adjusted for demographic, clinical, and behavioural factors. During a median 7.9-year follow-up (IQR, 5.2-9.5), 7609 deaths occurred. MVPA initiation was associated with lower all-cause mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.94), a lower risk of liver-related events (subdistribution HR [subHR], 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97), and, more modestly, of HCC (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99) compared with those remaining inactive. The association was more pronounced in older adults, women, never smokers, non-drinkers, and untreated participants (all p for interaction ≤ 0.03). Initiating MVPA among physically inactive adults with CHB was associated with lower risks of mortality and liver-related outcomes. These findings provide large-scale epidemiological evidence supporting further evaluation of PA promotion in physically inactive patients with CHB.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between initiating moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and reduced risks of mortality and liver-related events in adults with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Using the nationwide Korean National Health Insurance database, the researchers followed 318,131 physically inactive adults with CHB over a median of 7.9 years. They found that MVPA initiation was linked to lower all-cause mortality (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.84-0.94), reduced liver-related events (subHR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.92-0.97), and a modest decrease in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk (subHR, 0.95; 95% CI, 0.91-0.99) compared to those who remained inactive. The associations were stronger in specific subgroups, including older adults, women, and untreated participants. The study highlights the potential public health significance of promoting physical activity in CHB patients, though it does not provide direct causal evidence.

title: Risk factors for postpartum alanine aminotransferase elevation in women with chronic hepatitis B infection: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Postpartum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) elevation is common in women with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection and may adversely affect maternal recovery and long-term disease outcomes. However, the risk factors associated with postpartum ALT elevation remain inconsistent across studies. Methods We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines; the registration number is CRD420251208005. PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), and WanFang databases were searched from their inception to 1 January 2026. Results A total of 17 cohort studies involving 6,876 women with CHB were included. The meta-analysis demonstrated that hepatitis B e-antigen (HBeAg) positivity (odds ratio [OR] = 3.03; 95% CI [1.91–4.81]), higher baseline hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA levels (OR = 1.39; 95% CI [1.04–1.86]), and elevated antepartum ALT levels were significantly associated with postpartum ALT elevation. A subgroup analysis revealed that antepartum ALT elevation, defined as a categorical variable (ALT >1 ULN), showed a strong association with postpartum ALT elevation (OR = 5.54, 95% CI 3.78–8.12), whereas continuous ALT increase showed a smaller effect size. Increasing maternal age was associated with a reduced risk of postpartum ALT elevation (OR = 0.93, 95% CI 0.87–0.99). Conclusion HBeAg positivity, high baseline HBV DNA levels, and elevated antepartum ALT levels are key risk factors for postpartum ALT elevation in women with CHB. Additionally, younger maternal age may confer increased susceptibility. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251208005 , Identifier: CRD420251208005.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify risk factors for postpartum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) elevation in women with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection. The study included 17 cohort studies involving 6,876 women with CHB. Key findings indicated that HBeAg positivity, higher baseline HBV DNA levels, and elevated antepartum ALT levels were significantly associated with postpartum ALT elevation. Subgroup analysis showed that antepartum ALT elevation, defined as ALT >1 ULN, had a strong association with postpartum ALT elevation, while continuous ALT increase showed a smaller effect. Increasing maternal age was associated with a reduced risk of postpartum ALT elevation. The review highlights the importance of monitoring antepartum ALT levels and managing HBeAg positivity and HBV DNA levels in women with CHB during pregnancy and postpartum periods. The findings suggest that younger maternal age may increase susceptibility to postpartum ALT elevation.

The meta-analysis demonstrated that hepatitis B e-antigen (HBeAg) positivity (odds ratio [OR] = 3.03; 95% CI [1.91–4.81]), higher baseline hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA levels (OR = 1.39; 95% CI [1.04–1.86]), and elevated antepartum ALT levels were significantly associated with postpartum ALT elevation. A subgroup analysis revealed that antepartum ALT elevation, defined as a categorical variable (ALT >1 ULN), showed a strong association with postpartum ALT elevation (OR = 5.54, 95% CI 3.78–8.12), whereas continuous ALT increase showed a smaller effect size. Increasing maternal age was associated with a reduced risk of postpartum ALT elevation (OR = 0.93, 95% CI 0.87–0.99). Conclusion HBeAg positivity, high baseline HBV DNA levels, and elevated antepartum ALT levels are key risk factors for postpartum ALT elevation in women with CHB. Additionally, younger maternal age may confer increased susceptibility. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251208005 , Identifier: CRD420251208005.

title: A comprehensive evaluation on the impact of MASLD on the prognosis of chronic hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma following hepatectomy: results from retrospective multicenter cohort study and meta-analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prognosis after radical hepatectomy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is poor. Comorbidity of CHB and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has grown increasingly common, with MASLD further modifying the hepatic microenvironment beyond HBV-induced injury. However, its impact on postoperative prognosis remains unclear. METHODS: Combining a retrospective study with meta-analysis, this study systematically compared prognostic differences and influencing factors in 424 hepatectomy patients (MASLD-CHB-HCC group vs. CHB-HCC group) from multiple centers. Additionally, a meta-analysis involving 6653 patients was performed to further verify the prognostic effect of MASLD. RESULTS: In this retrospective cohort study, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group showed significantly superior overall survival (OS) (p = 0.041) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) (p = 0.028) compared with the CHB-HCC group, with statistically significant differences. However, after performing propensity score matching (PSM) screening, no statistical differences were observed in OS (p = 0.220) and RFS (p = 0.190) between the two groups. This result is consistent with our meta-analysis conclusion. Cox regression analysis demonstrated that higher body mass index (BMI) was an independent factor associated with favorable survival. In subgroup analyses stratified by different BMI cutoffs, among non-lean patients, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group achieved better OS (BMI ≥ 23 subgroup: p < 0.001; BMI ≥ 25 subgroup: p < 0.001) and RFS (BMI ≥ 23 subgroup: p < 0.001; BMI ≥ 25 subgroup: p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: MASLD exerts differential impacts on survival prognosis in patients with CHB-HCC, with divergent effects observed between lean and non-lean subgroups stratified by BMI.

analysis.scope_and_question: This study evaluates the impact of MASLD on the prognosis of chronic hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) following hepatectomy. The central question is whether MASLD modifies postoperative outcomes in patients with CHB-HCC.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study combines a retrospective multicenter cohort study with a meta-analysis. It included 424 patients from multiple centers and a meta-analysis involving 6653 patients. Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to adjust for confounding factors, and Cox regression analysis was performed to identify independent prognostic factors.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that the MASLD-CHB-HCC group showed significantly better overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) compared to the CHB-HCC group in the retrospective cohort study. However, after PSM, no significant differences were observed. Subgroup analyses revealed that among non-lean patients, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group had better OS and RFS, particularly in BMI ≥ 23 and BMI ≥ 25 subgroups. The meta-analysis confirmed these findings, indicating that MASLD has differential impacts on survival prognosis in CHB-HCC patients.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights conflicting findings between the initial analysis and the PSM-adjusted results, suggesting potential confounding factors. Additionally, the differential effects of MASLD on survival were observed only in non-lean subgroups, indicating a need for further research to understand the mechanisms behind these differences.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on understanding the mechanisms by which MASLD affects survival in CHB-HCC patients, particularly in non-lean subgroups. There is a need for larger, prospective studies to validate these findings and explore the role of BMI in mediating the impact of MASLD on prognosis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the impact of MASLD on the prognosis of chronic hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) following hepatectomy. A retrospective multicenter cohort study and meta-analysis were conducted, involving 424 and 6653 patients, respectively. Initial findings suggested that MASLD-CHB-HCC patients had better overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) compared to CHB-HCC patients, but these differences disappeared after propensity score matching (PSM). Subgroup analyses revealed that non-lean patients with MASLD-CHB-HCC had significantly improved OS and RFS, particularly in BMI ≥ 23 and ≥ 25 groups. The meta-analysis supported these results, indicating that MASLD has differential effects on survival outcomes in CHB-HCC patients. The study underscores the need for further research to clarify the mechanisms behind these differences and to explore the role of BMI in influencing prognosis.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本研究结合回顾性多中心队列研究研究与荟萃分析。纳入了来自多中心的424例患者以及包含6653例患者的荟萃分析。使用倾向评分匹配(PSM)调整混杂因素,并进行了Cox回归分析以识别独立预后因素。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,在回顾性队列研究研究中,MASLD-CHB-HCC组的总体生存率(OS)和无复发生存率(RFS)显著优于CHB-HCC组。然而,在PSM调整后,两组之间无显著差异。亚组分析显示,在非瘦体型患者中,MASLD-CHB-HCC组的OS和RFS均更好,尤其是在BMI ≥ 23和BMI ≥ 25的亚组中。荟萃分析证实了这些发现,表明MASLD对CHB-HCC患者的生存预后具有差异性影响。

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应重点探讨MASLD如何影响CHB-HCC患者的生存,特别是在非瘦体型亚组中。需要进行更大规模的前瞻性研究以验证这些发现,并进一步探索BMI在MASLD对预后影响中的中介作用。

analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that the MASLD-CHB-HCC group showed significantly better overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) compared to the CHB-HCC group in the retrospective cohort study. However, after PSM, no significant differences were observed. Subgroup analyses revealed that among non-lean patients, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group had better OS and RFS, particularly in BMI ≥ 23 and BMI ≥ 25 subgroups. The meta-analysis confirmed these findings, indicating that MASLD has differential impacts on survival prognosis in CHB-HCC patients.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights conflicting findings between the initial analysis and the PSM-adjusted results, suggesting potential confounding factors. Additionally, the differential effects of MASLD on survival were observed only in non-lean subgroups, indicating a need for further research to understand the mechanisms behind these differences.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should focus on understanding the mechanisms by which MASLD affects survival in CHB-HCC patients, particularly in non-lean subgroups. There is a need for larger, prospective studies to validate these findings and explore the role of BMI in mediating the impact of MASLD on prognosis.

title_zh: MASLD对慢性乙型肝炎相关肝细胞癌肝切除术后预后影响的综合评估:来自回顾性多中心队列研究研究和荟萃分析的结果
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Prognosis after radical hepatectomy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is poor. Comorbidity of CHB and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has grown increasingly common, with MASLD further modifying the hepatic microenvironment beyond HBV-induced injury. However, its impact on postoperative prognosis remains unclear. METHODS: Combining a retrospective study with meta-analysis, this study systematically compared prognostic differences and influencing factors in 424 hepatectomy patients (MASLD-CHB-HCC group vs. CHB-HCC group) from multiple centers. Additionally, a meta-analysis involving 6653 patients was performed to further verify the prognostic effect of MASLD. RESULTS: In this retrospective cohort study, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group showed significantly superior overall survival (OS) (p = 0.041) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) (p = 0.028) compared with the CHB-HCC group, with statistically significant differences. However, after performing propensity score matching (PSM) screening, no statistical differences were observed in OS (p = 0.220) and RFS (p = 0.190) between the two groups. This result is consistent with our meta-analysis conclusion. Cox regression analysis demonstrated that higher body mass index (BMI) was an independent factor associated with favorable survival. In subgroup analyses stratified by different BMI cutoffs, among non-lean patients, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group achieved better OS (BMI ≥ 23 subgroup: p < 0.001; BMI ≥ 25 subgroup: p < 0.001) and RFS (BMI ≥ 23 subgroup: p < 0.001; BMI ≥ 25 subgroup: p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: MASLD exerts differential impacts on survival prognosis in patients with CHB-HCC, with divergent effects observed between lean and non-lean subgroups stratified by BMI.
abstract_zh: 背景:慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)相关肝细胞癌(HCC)患者在进行根治性肝切除术后预后较差。CHB与代谢相关脂肪性肝病(MASLD)的共病现象日益普遍,MASLD进一步改变了HBV诱导的肝微环境。然而,其对术后预后的影响尚不明确。方法:本研究结合回顾性研究与荟萃分析,系统比较了来自多中心的424例肝切除患者(MASLD-CHB-HCC组与CHB-HCC组)的预后差异及影响因素。此外,还进行了包含6653例患者的荟萃分析,以进一步验证MASLD的预后效应。结果:在本回顾性队列研究研究中,MASLD-CHB-HCC组的总体生存率(OS)(p = 0.041)和无复发生存率(RFS)(p = 0.028)显著优于CHB-HCC组,差异具有统计学意义。然而,在进行倾向评分匹配(PSM)筛选后,两组之间的OS(p = 0.220)和RFS(p = 0.190)无显著统计学差异。这一结果与我们的荟萃分析结论一致。Cox回归分析显示,较高的身体质量指数(BMI)是与良好生存相关的独立因素。在按不同BMI截断值分层的亚组分析中,对于非瘦体型患者,MASLD-CHB-HCC组在OS(BMI ≥ 23亚组:p < 0.001;BMI ≥ 25亚组:p < 0.001)和RFS(BMI ≥ 23亚组:p < 0.001;BMI ≥ 25亚组:p < 0.001)方面均表现更好。结论:MASLD对CHB-HCC患者的生存预后具有差异性影响,在按BMI分层的瘦体型和非瘦体型亚组中观察到不同的效果。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本研究评估MASLD对慢性乙型肝炎相关肝细胞癌(HCC)患者肝切除术后预后的影响。核心问题是MASLD是否会影响CHB-HCC患者的术后结果。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本研究结合回顾性多中心队列研究研究与荟萃分析。纳入了来自多中心的424例患者以及包含6653例患者的荟萃分析。使用倾向评分匹配(PSM)调整混杂因素,并进行了Cox回归分析以识别独立预后因素。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,在回顾性队列研究研究中,MASLD-CHB-HCC组的总体生存率(OS)和无复发生存率(RFS)显著优于CHB-HCC组。然而,在PSM调整后,两组之间无显著差异。亚组分析显示,在非瘦体型患者中,MASLD-CHB-HCC组的OS和RFS均更好,尤其是在BMI ≥ 23和BMI ≥ 25的亚组中。荟萃分析证实了这些发现,表明MASLD对CHB-HCC患者的生存预后具有差异性影响。

analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应重点探讨MASLD如何影响CHB-HCC患者的生存,特别是在非瘦体型亚组中。需要进行更大规模的前瞻性研究以验证这些发现,并进一步探索BMI在MASLD对预后影响中的中介作用。

title: Concomitant Liver Steatosis in Chronic Hepatitis B Virus Infection Is Linked to a Distinct Cytokine Profile and Reduced Viral Load.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection frequently coexists with hepatic steatosis, which may promote liver disease progression and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development. However, the effects of liver steatosis on antiviral immune responses and viral load remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We investigated cytokine and chemokine patterns in plasma samples of 66 treatment-naive patients with chronic HBV infection in the absence or presence of liver steatosis. In addition, viral load and aminotransferase levels were assessed in blood samples. RESULTS: Patients with HBV infection and liver steatosis revealed a lower viral load than patients without liver steatosis. Despite a reduced viral load, liver steatosis was associated with reduced plasma levels of several cytokines and chemokines including interleukin (IL)-2, IL-9, IL-15, IL-18, CCL2, CCL4, and CXCL10, as well as with reduced aminotransferase levels. In contrast, other cytokines, such as IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-7, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12, IL-17, and tumor necrosis factor-α, did not significantly differ between the two patient groups. CONCLUSIONS: In chronic HBV infection, concomitant liver steatosis is associated with lower viral load but a dampened systemic cytokine and chemokine response suggesting an impaired immune response that may influence disease progression and HCC risk independently of viral load.

title_zh: 慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染并发的肝脂肪变与独特的细胞因子谱及病毒载量降低相关。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection frequently coexists with hepatic steatosis, which may promote liver disease progression and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development. However, the effects of liver steatosis on antiviral immune responses and viral load remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We investigated cytokine and chemokine patterns in plasma samples of 66 treatment-naive patients with chronic HBV infection in the absence or presence of liver steatosis. In addition, viral load and aminotransferase levels were assessed in blood samples. RESULTS: Patients with HBV infection and liver steatosis revealed a lower viral load than patients without liver steatosis. Despite a reduced viral load, liver steatosis was associated with reduced plasma levels of several cytokines and chemokines including interleukin (IL)-2, IL-9, IL-15, IL-18, CCL2, CCL4, and CXCL10, as well as with reduced aminotransferase levels. In contrast, other cytokines, such as IL-4, IL-5, IL-6, IL-7, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12, IL-17, and tumor necrosis factor-α, did not significantly differ between the two patient groups. CONCLUSIONS: In chronic HBV infection, concomitant liver steatosis is associated with lower viral load but a dampened systemic cytokine and chemokine response suggesting an impaired immune response that may influence disease progression and HCC risk independently of viral load.
abstract_zh: 背景:慢性乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)感染常与肝脂肪变并存,这可能促进肝病进展和肝细胞癌(HCC)的发生。然而,肝脂肪变对抗病毒药物 免疫应答及病毒载量的影响仍不完全清楚。方法:我们研究了66名慢性HBV感染且未接受治疗治疗的患者在存在或不存在肝脂肪变情况下的血浆样本中的细胞因子和趋化因子模式,并评估了血液样本中的病毒载量和氨基转移酶水平。结果:HBV感染合并肝脂肪变的患者表现出比无肝脂肪变的患者更低的病毒载量。尽管病毒载量降低,肝脂肪变与几种细胞因子和趋化因子的血浆水平降低相关,包括白细胞介素(IL)-2、IL-9、IL-15、IL-18、CCL2、CCL4和CXCL10,以及与氨基转移酶水平降低相关。相反,其他细胞因子,如IL-4、IL-5、IL-6、IL-7、IL-8、IL-10、IL-12、IL-17和肿瘤坏死因子-α,在两组患者之间没有显著差异。结论:在慢性HBV感染中,肝脂肪变与较低的病毒载量相关,但与系统性细胞因子和趋化因子反应减弱有关,这表明免疫应答可能受损,这种损害可能独立于病毒载量影响疾病进展和HCC风险。

title: Prevalence and determinants of hepatitis B vaccination uptake among pregnant women in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Despite more than two decades of hepatitis B vaccination implementation across sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains hyperendemic in the region, with vertical transmission an important route of infection. However, there is a lack of regional evidence on HBV vaccination uptake among pregnant women, a priority population in HBV prevention. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the prevalence of HBV vaccination uptake and identify its determinants among pregnant women in SSA. DESIGN: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. DATA SOURCES: Following prospective registration (PROSPERO), we searched MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and Scopus for peer-reviewed studies published up to August 2026, supplemented by African Journals Online and Google Scholar. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR SELECTING STUDIES: Observational studies reporting HBV vaccination uptake among pregnant women in SSA countries were included. DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and assessed methodological quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist for analytical cross-sectional studies. A random-effects meta-analysis was performed to estimate pooled prevalence. Subgroup and meta-regression sensitivity analyses explored sources of heterogeneity and robustness of findings. Determinants of vaccination uptake were synthesised narratively. RESULTS: Of 1041 records screened, 21 studies involving 15 804 pregnant women from seven SSA countries were included. The pooled prevalence of HBV vaccination uptake was 18% (95% CI 14% to 21%) with substantial heterogeneity (I2=99.2%) observed. Studies from West Africa (12; n=8062) reported higher vaccine uptake (24%, 95% CI 17% to 31%; p<0.001). Available studies identified socioeconomic, behavioural and healthcare-related factors associated with uptake, though evidence was limited. Evidence of small-study effects or potential publication bias was observed (Egger’s test, p<0.001). The overall certainty of evidence was considered very low using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, reflecting serious concerns regarding inconsistency, risk of bias and small-study effects. CONCLUSIONS: HBV vaccination uptake among pregnant women in SSA remains suboptimal and represents an important unmet need for preventing vertical transmission. Targeted, context-specific interventions to improve awareness, access and integration of vaccination into antenatal care services are needed to enhance uptake. Future research should examine barriers and evaluate interventions to increase vaccination coverage in this priority population. PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251120357.

abstract_zh: OBJECTIVE: 尽管撒哈拉以南非洲(SSA)地区已实施乙型肝炎病毒疫苗接种超过二十年,乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)仍在此地区高度流行,垂直传播是重要的感染途径。然而,关于孕妇中HBV疫苗接种接受情况的区域证据仍然缺乏,孕妇是HBV预防的重点人群。本系统综述和元分析旨在估计HBV疫苗接种接受情况的总体水平,并确定撒哈拉以南非洲孕妇中该疫苗接种的决定因素。DESIGN: 本研究遵循首选报告项目清单(PRISMA)指南进行系统综述和随机效应元分析。DATA SOURCES: 在前瞻性注册(PROSPERO)后,我们搜索了MEDLINE、Embase、Web of Science和Scopus数据库,获取截至2026年8月发表的同行评审研究,并补充了非洲期刊在线和Google Scholar。ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR SELECTING STUDIES: 包括报告撒哈拉以南非洲国家孕妇中HBV疫苗接种接受情况的观察性研究。DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: 两名评审员独立筛选研究、提取数据并使用Joanna Briggs研究所的分析横断面研究检查表评估方法学质量。采用随机效应元分析来估计总体接受情况。亚组分析和元回归敏感性分析用于探索异质性的来源和结果的稳健性。疫苗接种接受情况的决定因素通过叙述性综合进行分析。RESULTS: 在筛选的1041条记录中,纳入了来自七个撒哈拉以南非洲国家、涉及15,804名孕妇的21项研究。HBV疫苗接种的总体接受率为18%(95% CI 14%至21%),观察到显著的异质性(I2=99.2%)。西非的研究(12项;n=8062)报告了更高的疫苗接种接受率(24%,95% CI 17%至31%;p<0.001)。现有研究确定了与疫苗接种接受相关的社会经济、行为和医疗保健因素,但证据有限。观察到小研究效应或潜在发表偏倚的证据(Egger’s检验,p<0.001)。使用推荐评估、发展和评价(GRADE)方法评估证据的整体确定性,认为其非常低,反映了对不一致性、偏倚风险和小研究效应的严重关注。CONCLUSIONS: 撒哈拉以南非洲孕妇中HBV疫苗接种接受情况仍然不足,是预防垂直传播的重要未满足需求。需要有针对性、因地制宜的干预措施,以提高意识、获取和将疫苗接种纳入产前护理服务,从而提高接种率。未来的研究应探讨障碍并评估干预措施,以增加该重点人群的疫苗接种覆盖率。PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251120357.

title: Natural History and Clinical Outcomes of HBeAg-Negative Chronic Hepatitis B Patients in the “Grey Zone”: A Longitudinal Cohort Study
abstract: Introduction and Objectives: Up to one-third of treatment-naïve, HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients with normal ALT do not meet the strict criteria for the inactive carrier (IC) phase, falling into a “Grey Zone” (GZIC). We aimed to delineate the longitudinal outcomes of GZIC patients compared with strictly defined IC patients. Patients and Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 386 HBeAg-negative, ALT-normal CHB patients (125 GZIC, 261 IC). Endpoints included phase transition to immune-active stages, antiviral initiation, and end-stage liver disease (cirrhosis or hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)). Cumulative incidence was assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis. Results: Over a median follow-up of 4.5 years, the GZIC cohort exhibited significantly higher cumulative incidence of phase transition (36.8% vs. 13.8%, p < 0.001), antiviral initiation (37.6% vs. 18.8%, p = 0.00014), and end-stage liver disease (4.8% vs. 1.5%, p = 0.049) compared with the IC cohort. All incident HCC cases occurred exclusively in the GZIC group. Multivariate analysis identified baseline GZIC status, male sex, and elevated AFP as independent risk factors. A lower ALT cutoff of 24.5 U/L was superior to 40 U/L in predicting phase transition (p < 0.01). Sex-stratified analyses confirmed that GZIC remained an independent risk factor for phase transition in both male and female patients (both p < 0.05). Conclusions: The GZIC phase is not a benign state. Compared with true inactive carriers, GZIC patients face a significantly elevated risk of progression and liver-related complications, supporting proactive surveillance and timely antiviral intervention.

title: Donor–recipient Hepatitis B serological patterns and post-transplant HBV events in pediatric living donor liver transplantation: a single-center retrospective cohort with a nested case series
abstract: Background The combined effects of donor hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc) status and recipient pre-transplant hepatitis B surface antibody (anti-HBs) levels on post-transplant HBV events remain unclear in pediatric living donor liver transplantation (LDLT). Methods We retrospectively analyzed pediatric LDLT recipients transplanted between May 2018 and June 2023. The primary outcome was the first post-transplant hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive result, with death treated as a competing event. Recipients were stratified by donor anti-HBc status and recipient anti-HBs level (≥100 vs <100 mIU/mL). Antiviral prophylaxis with entecavir (0.015 mg/kg once daily) was given only to recipients of anti-HBc-positive grafts, and hepatitis B immune globulin was not used. Cumulative incidence was compared using Gray’s test, and associated factors were evaluated using Fine–Gray regression. Results Among 229 recipients, 14 (6.1%) developed HBV events. Events occurred in 0 of 97 recipients with an anti-HBc-negative donor and anti-HBs ≥100 mIU/mL (G1), 3 of 67 with an anti-HBc-negative donor and anti-HBs <100 mIU/mL (G2), 2 of 29 with an anti-HBc-positive donor and anti-HBs ≥100 mIU/mL (G3), and 9 of 36 with an anti-HBc-positive donor and anti-HBs <100 mIU/mL (G4); the corresponding 5-year cumulative incidences were 0%, 4.5%, 6.9% and 25.0% (global Gray’s test, P<0.001). Donor anti-HBc positivity (sHR, 8.28; 95% CI, 2.27–30.28; P = 0.001) and recipient anti-HBs <100 mIU/mL (sHR, 6.02; 95% CI, 1.32–27.55; P = 0.021) were independently associated with HBV events, although the wide confidence intervals reflect the small number of events (n = 14) and the magnitude of these estimates should be interpreted with caution. Conclusions Donor anti-HBc positivity and low recipient pre-transplant anti-HBs were independently associated with post-transplant HBV events after pediatric LDLT. Combined donor–recipient serological stratification identified a clear risk gradient and may support risk-adapted HBV surveillance and prevention.

title: Hepatitis D virus infection in persons with HIV and hepatitis B virus across Europe : A cross‐sectional analysis of the HDV‐Europe cohort
abstract: Abstract Introduction Infection with hepatitis D virus (HDV) is known to accelerate the progression of liver disease and is associated with mortality in individuals with HIV and hepatitis B virus (HBV). However, little is known about current HDV epidemiology, including HDV‐testing practices and prevalence, in this population in Europe. Methods We conducted a cross‐sectional study of clinical cohorts across Europe (Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Spain, Switzerland and United Kingdom). Included individuals were those living with HIV, ever hepatitis B surface antigen positive, aged ≥18 years and actively in care on December 31, 2023. We calculated the percentage of individuals tested for HDV, prevalence of individuals who ever had anti‐HDV positive serology (i.e., past/current infection) and the prevalence of individuals whose last HDV RNA result was positive (i.e., active infection). Results A total of 2970 individuals were included. Anti‐HDV antibody results were available in 2189 (73.7%). Of them, 261 (12.0%) had past/current HDV infection, ranging between 3.8% in the United Kingdom and 27.3% in Poland. Among the 261 individuals with an anti‐HDV‐positive result, 162 (62.1%) had been tested for HDV RNA. Of them, 92 (56.8%) had active HDV infection. Of the overall population with available data, active HDV infection was observed in 4.4% ( n = 92/2077), ranging between 0.9% in the Netherlands and 11.0% in Italy. Conclusions In Europe, about one‐eighth of individuals with HIV/HBV in care have evidence of past/current HDV infection, in whom half have active HDV infection. Nevertheless, these results come from a setting where one‐quarter have yet to be tested for anti‐HDV antibodies.

title: Sigmoid colon mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma complicated with hepatitis B virus infection: a case report
abstract: Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) lymphoma is a low-grade malignant extranodal marginal zone B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, which most commonly originates in the stomach. Primary colorectal MALT lymphoma is rare clinically, and there are currently no unified diagnostic and therapeutic criteria. Besides, the association between chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and sigmoid colon MALT lymphoma remains unclear. Herein, we report a 69-year-old male patient with primary sigmoid colon MALT lymphoma complicated with HBV infection. The patient was admitted due to a colorectal mass detected during physical examination, without typical gastrointestinal symptoms. Primary sigmoid colon MALT lymphoma was confirmed by colonoscopic biopsy, immunohistochemistry, gene rearrangement analysis and PET-CT. The patient did not receive targeted anti-tumor therapy, and instead received basic management including anti-HBV treatment combined with regular follow-up. After two years of standardized follow-up, the primary lesion in the sigmoid colon resolved, with no disease progression or recurrence. This case suggests that for asymptomatic localized primary sigmoid colon MALT lymphoma, the management strategy of targeted therapy for chronic infection such as HBV infection combined with intensive monitoring and regular follow-up merits further discussion.

title: Interferon-λ receptor positive monocytes/macrophages orchestrate a pro-fibrotic immune environment in hepatitis B virus-related liver fibrosis.
abstract: Interferon-λ receptor (IFNLR), a heterodimer composed of IFNLR1 and IL-10Rβ, mediates IFN-λ-driven fibrotic effects. This study investigated the involvement of IFNLR1+ monocytes/macrophages in orchestrating pro-fibrotic immune microenvironment. Flow cytometric analysis of peripheral blood showed that IFNLR1+ monocytes were elevated in patients with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection (CHI) and patients with HBV-related liver cirrhosis (LC), compared with healthy controls (HC). These cells also displayed a CCR2hiCCR5hiCX3CR1hiCD86hiHLA-DRhiCD163hiMERTKhi phenotype with an IL-10hiTNF-αhi cytokine profile. Hepatic fibrosis was induced in wild-type and Ifnlr1-knockout (Ifnlr1-/-) mice using carbon tetrachloride and recombinant adeno-associated virus 8-1.3HBV. Ifnlr1 deficiency down-regulated CCR2 and CCR5 expression on monocytes/macrophages, attenuated collagen deposition, but enhanced HBV-DNA replication. In vitro, bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) were co-cultured with hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) or naive CD4+ T cells to assess the functional impact of IFNLR1+ macrophages. Concurrently, the involvement of lipid metabolism in IFN-λ/IFNLR1-mediated macrophage regulation was examined using liver X receptor (LXR) agonists/antagonists. Ifnlr1-/- BMDMs exhibited a diminished capacity to activate HSCs and drive regulatory T cells differentiation. Mechanistically, IFN-λ-IFNLR1 signaling suppressed LXR-dependent lipid metabolism, thereby promoting tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α and IL-1β production, and LXR pathway inhibition favored M1-macrophage polarization. Collectively, IFNLR1 identifies a pro-fibrotic and immunoregulatory monocyte/macrophage subset. Targeting IFNLR1-LXR axis may represent promising anti-fibrotic strategies for HBV-related liver fibrosis.

title: Toll-like Receptor 7 and Interferon-α Synergy Establishes a Positive Feedback Loop to Potentiate Antiviral Immunity in Chronic Hepatitis B.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Current therapies for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) rarely achieve functional cure, underscoring the need for novel immunotherapies. Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7), a key innate immune sensor, has emerged as a major drug development focus. This study aims to characterize stage-specific TLR7 expression and functions in CHB, investigate its association with antiviral therapy response, and evaluate synergistic effects of TLR7 activation combined with interferon-α (IFN-α). METHODS: We conducted cross-sectional and longitudinal clinical analyses of CHB patients, complemented by in vitro functional assays using peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and purified B cells, and an in vivo HBV mouse model. RESULTS: TLR7 expression in PBMCs was downregulated in immunotolerant and inactive carriers but elevated in immune-active (IA) patients, positively correlated with serum ALT. TLR7 activation induced IFN-α-mediated HBV suppression, with IA patient-derived PBMCs exhibiting enhanced antiviral activity. Notably, IFN-α dose-dependently upregulated TLR7 expression, revealing a positive feedback loop between TLR7 and IFN-α. Clinically, sustained TLR7 upregulation during pegylated IFN-α therapy predicted virological response. As the primary TLR7-expressing subset, B cells exhibited enhanced proliferation, activation, cytokine production, and antibody secretion upon combined TLR7 ligand (TLR7-L)/IFN-α stimulation. In an HBV mouse model, TLR7-L/IFN-α combination therapy synergistically suppressed HBsAg and enhanced CD8+ T cell functionality. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies a candidate self-reinforcing TLR7-IFN-α positive feedback loop in CHB that exhibits stage-specific dynamics and predicts treatment response. The synergistic effects of TLR7 and IFN-α support a threshold model of immune activation and provide a mechanistic rationale for combination immunotherapies aiming for functional cure.

title: Gut-liver axis dysregulation and restoration in decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis: rationale and research progress of fecal microbiota transplantation
abstract: Decompensated hepatitis B virus (HBV) related cirrhosis is associated with high mortality and a wide range of complications. Current antiviral and symptomatic treatments fail to reverse core pathological alterations, including disruption of the gut microbial ecosystem. Gut-liver axis imbalance represents a central hub in disease progression. Gut dysbiosis compromises the intestinal mucosal barrier, leading to endotoxin translocation into the bloodstream, which in turn exacerbates hepatic inflammation and fibrosis, thereby establishing a vicious cycle. This review synthesizes the key mechanisms, clinical efficacy, administration routes, and safety profile of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in this disease. It also identifies current technical bottlenecks and research gaps in FMT application and discusses future directions toward precision based and standardized clinical translation of this therapeutic approach.
