title: Persistence of antibody to hepatitis b surface antigen and reported post-vaccination symptoms in young children with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency: a comparative cross-sectional study
abstract: We compared persistence of antibody to hepatitis B surface antigen (anti-HBs) and retrospectively reported post-vaccination symptoms between young children with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency and healthy controls. This comparative cross-sectional study was conducted in Heyuan, China, from March 2024 to January 2025. G6PD deficiency was enzymatically confirmed. Controls were frequency-matched by sex, with body mass index used for group-level balancing. Vaccination histories were obtained from records; parents retrospectively reported six common symptoms within 30 days after each hepatitis B vaccine dose. Anti-HBs was measured at enrolment. Primary persistence analyses included children sampled at least 6 months after dose 3. Risk differences and risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. Modified Poisson and linear regression used robust standard errors and adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, time since dose 3, and vaccine product. The study included 505 children (55 with G6PD deficiency; 450 controls); 98.2% were aged 1–4 years. The mean interval from dose 3 to sampling was approximately 30 months. Primary analyses included 54 and 438 children, respectively. Seroprotection (anti-HBs ≥10 mIU/mL) was 87.0% versus 82.2% (risk difference, 4.8 percentage points; 95% CI, −7.1 to 12.4; adjusted risk ratio, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.96–1.19). The adjusted association between G6PD deficiency and log2(anti-HBs concentration+1) was not statistically significant (β = −0.04; 95% CI, −0.68 to 0.59; P = 0.90). At least one symptom was reported in 5/55 (9.1%) versus 19/450 (4.2%) children (P = 0.17). No statistically detectable differences in anti-HBs seroprotection, antibody concentrations, or retrospectively reported common post-vaccination symptoms were observed. These findings do not establish equivalence. The long recall interval and lack of systematic ascertainment of hemolysis-related and serious clinical outcomes preclude conclusions regarding G6PD-specific vaccine safety. Larger prospective multicentre cohorts incorporating genotype, quantitative G6PD activity, standardized serological follow-up, and active safety surveillance are needed.

title: Immunomodulation and Molecular Diagnostic Aspects in Individuals with Hepatitis B Virus Infection
abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a major global health issue associated with severe liver complications. Outcomes depend on the immune response, which can sometimes fail, and are associated with chronic disease. Improved diagnostics and understanding of immune markers are crucial for more effective management and treatment of HBV infection. Aims: The study aimed to investigate the association between the HBV viral load, viral antigens, including Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), Hepatitis B core antigen (HBcAg), Hepatitis B enveloped antigen (HBeAg), and pro-inflammatory cytokines, including Human Interferon γ (INF-γ), Human Tumour Necrosis Factor α (TNF-α), Soluble Human Leukocyte Antigen class I (sHLA-A), an antigen-presenting molecule, and Human soluble Cluster of Differentiation 8 (sCD8), a soluble T-cell activation marker. This study provides additional regional information on the associations between virological and immunological parameters in patients with HBV infection from the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. Methodology: The study was a case-control study conducted on 120 individuals in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, comprising 60 patients with HBV infection and 60 healthy controls. The investigation included both sexes aged 25 to 74 years, during the period from March to July 2025. RT-PCR was used to assess viral load, and ELISA was used to evaluate immunological markers. Results: According to the study findings, Patients with HBV infection exhibited significantly higher immunological markers than healthy controls (p < 0.0001). Significant positive correlations were observed in the study between viral load and HBeAg (r=0.9051), as well as inflammatory cytokines IFN-γ (r=0.9189), TNF-α (r=0.832), sCD8 (r=0.888), and HLA-A (r=0.801). The obtained results demonstrated significant positive correlations between viral load and immune activation markers. Conclusion: Overall, the current study demonstrated significant positive correlations among viral load, viral antigens, and immunological markers in patients with chronic HBV infection and provides additional evidence of the immunological characteristics.

title: Perspectives on primary care management of chronic hepatitis B in refugees: findings from qualitative interviews with healthcare providers in Melbourne, Victoria.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In Australia, healthcare providers face significant challenges in meeting the niche health needs of refugees. Social determinants of health, including limited health literacy and finances, complicate refugees' access to treatment for conditions, such as chronic hepatitis B (CHB). Understanding the strategies utilised by a specialised general practice for refugees can offer guidance for treating this population. The aim of this study was to explore how primary care is currently managing CHB care tailored to refugees and to identify areas for potential improvements. METHODS: Between August and December 2024, we conducted 15 semi-structured interviews with nine general practitioners, four nurses, one pharmacist and one infectious disease specialist. We used a convenience sample and snowballing; most participants worked at a refugee-focused general practice in the west of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. All interviews were recorded and transcribed; data were analysed descriptively. RESULTS: Primary healthcare providers in our study recognised the challenges of treating refugees with CHB, including low health literacy, and the cost of providing and seeking care. However, when compared with hospital services, the benefits of primary care include community integration and location, rapport development, and the availability of interpreter services. Subsidising primary care provider training and other costs were recommended. CONCLUSIONS: Primary care may be better positioned than hospital services to treat refugees with CHB. These findings support funding and improving CHB management in primary care to meet the needs of refugees, which will lead to better health outcomes for this disadvantaged population.

title: Tislelizumab-induced immune-mediated hepatotoxicity combined with two episodes of hepatitis B virus reactivation: a case report
abstract: Immune-mediated hepatotoxicity (IMH) is a typical immune-related adverse event associated with the use of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), while hepatitis B virus reactivation (HBVr) is an infectious complication that may also occur during ICI therapy. However, these two conditions are usually independent and rarely co-occur in the same individual. Herein, we describe a patient with lung squamous cell carcinoma who developed HBVr and IMH simultaneously after receiving tislelizumab, and the co-existence of two episodes of HBVr brings challenges to the diagnosis and treatment of IMH. In the diagnosis of IMH, the co-existence of HBVr masked the underlying IMH, resulting in a delay in IMH treatment. In the treatment of IMH, the re-occurrence of HBVr led to a dilemma of continuing to use glucocorticoids (GCs) or stopping them. In such a clinical scenario, the multidisciplinary approach, close monitoring of liver function and HBV-DNA, and a carefully balanced treatment strategy combining GCs with intensified antiviral therapy are essential to realize the optimal management for IMH. In conclusion, medical staff should be alert to the coexistence of HBVr and IMH in patients receiving ICIs, so as to avoid missed diagnosis and treatment delay.

title: Prevalence and risk factors of hepatitis B infection in rural communities: a cross-sectional analysis
abstract: Objective Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a highly contagious preventable liver disease with high mortality rates across the world. HBV is endemic in Ghana, yet screening for early detection and treatment of the condition is a challenge. This study assessed the prevalence and associated risk factors of HBV infection in rural communities in the Upper East Region of Ghana. Subjects and methods This is a cross-sectional analysis of secondary data from 218 participants. The participants were classified into 2 groups—HBV negative and positive groups. Fisher Exact and Chi Square analysis were used to evaluate association between hepatitis B infection status and demographic and clinical characteristics. Binary logistic regression was used to evaluate for the risk factors associated with the HBV positive group. Results The mean (SD) age of the participants was 39.04(13.65) years, with majority 18–30 years old (30.28%), and 55.50% were farmers. The prevalence of HBV infection was 9.63%. Farmers were less likely associated with risk of HBV infections (OR = 0.17; 95% CI: 0.052–0.529; p = 0.002) than traders. After adjusting for other confounders, participants who had handwork were associated with lower risk of HBV infections (OR = 0.14; 95% CI: 0.028–0.738; p = 0.020) than traders. No family history of hepatitis B was associated with lower risk of HBV infections (OR = 0.09; 95% CI: 0.021–0.416; p = 0.002) than participants with family history of hepatitis B. Conclusion We found high prevalence of HBV infection among rural adults in this study. Associated risk factors identified for transmission of HBV infection in this population included occupation and family history of hepatitis B infection. There is urgent need for the development of context-specific prevention strategies that address both social and household transmission dynamics of HBV in rural communities in Ghana.

title: APRI and FIB-4 for Liver Fibrosis Assessment in Chronic Hepatitis B: Evidence from a Hyperendemic Andean Setting
abstract: Background/Objectives: The 2024 WHO guidelines incorporated the APRI index into treatment decisions for chronic hepatitis B, with thresholds of >0.5 for significant fibrosis and >1.0 for cirrhosis, because it can be computed when neither biopsy nor elastography is available. The evidence supporting those thresholds derives almost entirely from studies using liver biopsy as reference standard; how serological indices behave when the available comparator is elastography remains unknown, and no data exist for Andean populations. We aimed to quantify the agreement of APRI and FIB-4 with transient elastography, determine whether either discriminates better, and evaluate the 2024 WHO thresholds in this setting. Methods: Retrospective agreement study of patients in the Hepatitis B Elimination Plan of Huanta, Peru. APRI and FIB-4, computed from routine laboratory results, were compared against transient elastography (FibroScan 402, M+ probe) used as a reference standard given the unavailability of biopsy. Outcomes followed the 2024 WHO thresholds: >7.0 kPa for significant fibrosis and >12.5 kPa for cirrhosis. Only examinations meeting the pre-specified quality criterion (at least 10 valid measurements; IQR/median ≤ 30%) were analyzed. Diagnostic properties were estimated with exact confidence intervals and likelihood ratios, areas under the curve with bootstrap intervals, and the between-index comparison with DeLong’s test for paired curves. Reporting followed STARD 2015. Results: Of 92 patients, 73 had a valid elastography examination; APRI was computable in 60 and FIB-4 in 57. Prevalence was 23.3% (95% CI 14.2–34.6) for significant fibrosis and 12.3% (5.8–22.1) for cirrhosis. For significant fibrosis, APRI > 0.5 achieved 61.5% sensitivity (31.6–86.1) and 74.5% specificity (59.7–86.1), with a positive likelihood ratio of 2.41 (1.26–4.62) and a negative one of 0.52 (0.25–1.05). For cirrhosis, APRI > 1.0 yielded 71.4% sensitivity, 92.5% specificity and a positive likelihood ratio of 9.46 (3.30–27.11). Areas under the curve were 0.844 and 0.808 for significant fibrosis and 0.914 and 0.874 for cirrhosis; DeLong’s test detected no statistically significant difference between indices at either level (p = 0.47 and 0.53); however, the limited number of outcome-positive cases (13 and 7, respectively) means that clinically important differences cannot be excluded and equivalence has not been established. Conclusions: APRI and FIB-4 identified cirrhosis with likelihood ratios large enough to act on but were only weakly informative at the threshold that governs treatment eligibility, where the negative likelihood ratios did not exclude unity. Neither index can be used as a stand-alone rule-out test at that threshold. The small number of outcome-positive cases limits precision throughout. Although the program intended both assessments to occur during the same session, individual dates were unavailable, preventing verification of the actual interval between elastography and blood sampling.

title: DISTRIBUTION OF FIVE HEPATITIS B VIRUS MARKERS IN HIV INFECTED AND UNINFECTED INJECTING DRUG USERS IN COASTAL KENYA
abstract: Aims: This study determined HBV sero-markers profile in HIV-1 infected (n=157) and uninfected (n=214) IDUs from Mombasa, Kenya HIV-1 diagnosis was performed using DetermineTM and UnigoldTM rapid tests. Methodology: The CD4+ T cells were enumerated using the FacsCalibur flow cytometer and categorized according to the Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) immunological staging criteria. HBV seroprofile was determined using HBV-5 panel rapid test cassettes. Clinical staging was based on serological profile of the five HBV markers. Results: HBsAg (P=0.004) and HBcAb-IgM (P=0.008) positivities were higher in the HIV-1 infected compared to the uninfected individuals while the opposite was observed for HBsAb positivity (P=0.019). Rates of acute (P=0.033) and chronic (P=0.021) clinical stages were higher in the HIV-1 infected compared to the uninfected individuals but the inverse was noticed for vaccine type response rate (P=0.008). Only genotype A, sub-genotype A1 was detected with higher frequencies noted in the HIV-1 infected (n=12) compared to the uninfected (n=4) individuals. Conclusion: HBsAg and HBcAb-IgM sero-markers and acute and chronic clinical categories are higher while HBsAb sero-marker and vaccine type response stage are lower in HIV-1 infected compared to uninfected IDUs at Mombasa, Kenya. Taken together, HIV infected injection drug users are at risk of acquiring HBV and progressing to chronic infection.
journal: Global Journal of Research in Medicine and Dentistry

title: Why Outcomes Diverge in Chronic Hepatitis B with Steatotic Liver Disease: Lessons from Within-Study Contrasts
abstract: Background and Objectives: The “friend or foe” debate in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) with steatotic liver disease (SLD) partly arises from treating hepatic fat, metabolic burden, and steatohepatitis as one exposure and interpreting different outcomes together. Materials and Methods: This narrative review applies an exposure–stage–context framework to literature identified in PubMed and Web of Science through 21 September 2026. We synthesized outcome evidence from 119 reports, including 14 detailed examples, using within-study comparisons of exposures, outcomes, and patient subgroups. Results: Within individual cohorts, associations with the same outcome could diverge: steatosis or an SLD diagnosis was associated with lower hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) or mortality risk, whereas greater metabolic burden was associated with higher risk. Favorable antigen-related associations also coexisted with adverse fibrosis trajectories. Steatohepatitis was associated with more severe fibrosis and liver-related events, while metabolic abnormalities and prolonged glycemic exposure were associated with adverse hepatic outcomes. Studies of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) reported greater cardiovascular risk, and a study of hepatitis B virus-positive patients with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) reported more prevalent kidney disease. Baseline fibrosis, patient selection, and antiviral treatment shape these associations; lower relative risks can coexist with a high absolute event burden. Conclusions: Current hepatic fat, cumulative metabolic exposure, and established injury therefore carry different prognostic meanings. Their separate assessment helps explain part of the apparent paradox, while adverse steatosis findings and discrepancies in similar settings remain unresolved. The evidence is predominantly observational.

source_records.title: Why Outcomes Diverge in Chronic Hepatitis B with Steatotic Liver Disease: Lessons from Within-Study Contrasts
source_records.abstract: Background and Objectives: The “friend or foe” debate in chronic hepatitis B (CHB) with steatotic liver disease (SLD) partly arises from treating hepatic fat, metabolic burden, and steatohepatitis as one exposure and interpreting different outcomes together. Materials and Methods: This narrative review applies an exposure–stage–context framework to literature identified in PubMed and Web of Science through 21 September 2026. We synthesized outcome evidence from 119 reports, including 14 detailed examples, using within-study comparisons of exposures, outcomes, and patient subgroups. Results: Within individual cohorts, associations with the same outcome could diverge: steatosis or an SLD diagnosis was associated with lower hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) or mortality risk, whereas greater metabolic burden was associated with higher risk. Favorable antigen-related associations also coexisted with adverse fibrosis trajectories. Steatohepatitis was associated with more severe fibrosis and liver-related events, while metabolic abnormalities and prolonged glycemic exposure were associated with adverse hepatic outcomes. Studies of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) reported greater cardiovascular risk, and a study of hepatitis B virus-positive patients with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) reported more prevalent kidney disease. Baseline fibrosis, patient selection, and antiviral treatment shape these associations; lower relative risks can coexist with a high absolute event burden. Conclusions: Current hepatic fat, cumulative metabolic exposure, and established injury therefore carry different prognostic meanings. Their separate assessment helps explain part of the apparent paradox, while adverse steatosis findings and discrepancies in similar settings remain unresolved. The evidence is predominantly observational.

title: Macrophage Activation Syndrome Secondary to Hepatitis B in a Kidney Transplant Recipient: A Case Report and Regional Literature Review
abstract: Background: Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS), also known as hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), is a rare but potentially fatal hyperinflammatory disorder characterized by excessive activation of macrophages and cytotoxic lymphocytes, leading to a cytokine storm and multiorgan failure. Kidney transplant recipients are particularly vulnerable due to chronic immunosuppression and increased susceptibility to systemic infections. Viral infections, including hepatitis B and C, are recognized triggers of MAS in this population. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 21-year-old male kidney transplant recipient who developed MAS secondary to hepatitis B and C coinfection. The patient presented with fever, cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and pancytopenia. Laboratory findings revealed hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, elevated LDH, and hepatic cytolysis. Bone marrow aspiration confirmed hemophagocytosis. Six of the eight HLH-2004 diagnostic criteria were met, establishing the diagnosis of MAS. Hepatitis B PCR was >8 log10, and the patient was treated with entecavir, with favorable clinical and biological improvement. Conclusion: MAS should be suspected in any kidney transplant recipient presenting with fever and cytopenia, particularly in the presence of viral triggers. Early diagnosis and prompt etiological treatment are essential to improve prognosis, which remains poor in this population.

title: Resolution of viral R-loop by DHX9 promotes hepatitis B virus replication
abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a hepatotropic DNA virus with a compact 3.2 kb genome that replicates via reverse transcription. HBV covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) transcription shares molecular features with R-loop. DExH-box helicase 9 (DHX9) has been shown to be associated with R-loop accumulation, genome instability, and HBV replication. However, the role of DHX9-mediated R-loop homeostasis in HBV transcription has not yet been elucidated. In this study, we identified a critical role of DHX9 in resolving R-loops at transcription termination during HBV transcription. We demonstrate that HBV replication promotes viral R-loop accumulation. DHX9 promotes HBV R-loop resolution, HBV cccDNA transcription termination, and subsequent nuclear export of the 3.5 kb HBV RNA, facilitating HBV DNA replication. These findings reveal DHX9-mediated R-loop resolution as a potential therapeutic target for antiviral intervention. IMPORTANCE The persistence of HBV cccDNA poses a major challenge to achieving a cure for chronic hepatitis B. While R-loop structures have been implicated in the life cycles of viruses, their formation and functional significance in HBV replication have remained largely unexplored. This study provides the first evidence that the cellular helicase DHX9 resolves transcription-replication conflicts by dissolving R-loops formed during HBV replication. Our findings also identify DHX9-mediated R-loop resolution as a critical mechanism supporting the HBV life cycle. Consequently, targeting DHX9 presents a promising therapeutic strategy to silence the persistent HBV cccDNA reservoir.

title: Biological interpretation of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis in determining interferon treatment duration
abstract: The recent identification of baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and cirrhosis as independent predictors of extended interferon therapy provides a valuable clinical framework, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these associations require further elucidation. In this opinion review, we interpret these factors not merely as statistical covariates but as pathological surrogates for the virus-host equilibrium. We propose that high baseline hepatitis B surface antigen may reflect a deeply entrenched intrahepatic viral reservoir and may create an antigen-rich environment that impairs effective antiviral immunity. Concurrently, cirrhosis may be better understood as a spectrum of architectural remodeling in which vascular changes and sinusoidal defenestration could limit immune surveillance and affect local therapeutic access. Consequently, treatment durations exceeding 48 weeks may be required, at least in part, to overcome these profound immunological and structural barriers. We advocate shifting future predictive modeling from binary clinical definitions to a granular integration of viral kinetics and histological morphology to refine precision medicine in chronic hepatitis B.

title: Prevalence of hepatitis B surface antigen and associated factors among long-distance truck drivers at the Tunduma One-Stop Border Post, Tanzania: a cross-sectional study at Tunduma, Tanzania
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global public health concern and a leading cause of liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Sub-Saharan Africa bears a disproportionately high burden of HBV infection. Long-distance truck drivers may be exposed to factors associated with HBV transmission because of prolonged periods away from home, sexual behaviours, and limited access to healthcare services. Despite this, evidence on hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity and associated factors among this occupational group in Tanzania is limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of HBsAg positivity and associated factors among long-distance truck drivers at Tunduma Border Post, Tanzania. An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 396 long-distance truck drivers aged 18 years and above at Tunduma One-Stop Border Post, Songwe Region, southwestern Tanzania. Data on sociodemographic, behavioural, occupational, and health-related characteristics were collected using a structured questionnaire administered through Kobo Toolbox. Blood samples were tested for HBsAg using Abbott DetermineTM HBsAg rapid diagnostic tests. Bivariate and multivariable logistic regression assessed factors associated with HBsAg positivity. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% CIs were reported. Among the 396 participants, the median age was 37.5 years (IQR: 13), and 308 (77.8%) were married. A total of 26 (6.6%; 95% CI: 4.3–9.5%) participants were HBsAg-positive. In multivariable analysis, reporting more than five sexual partners in the previous 12 months was independently associated with higher odds of HBsAg positivity compared with reporting five or fewer partners during the same period (AOR 2.780, 95% CI: 1.120–6.901; p = 0.028). Transit time exceeding 60 days was also independently associated with higher odds of HBsAg positivity compared with transit time of 0–30 days (AOR 4.624, 95% CI: 1.707–12.520; p = 0.003). HBsAg positivity was observed among long-distance truck drivers at Tunduma Border Post. Reporting more than five sexual partners in the previous 12 months and longer transit time were independently associated with HBsAg positivity. Strengthening hepatitis B vaccination, screening, confirmatory testing, and linkage to appropriate care at border posts and other major transport points may improve prevention and early detection among this mobile occupational population.

title: Exploring the effect of ensemble size and technique on predictive accuracy of hepatitis B outcome
abstract: Machine learning (ML) models for hepatitis B virus (HBV) outcome prediction must address high variance, bias, and class imbalance. Previous ensemble-learning studies have commonly combined only two models or considered a limited set of ensemble techniques. This study evaluates how ensemble size, from two to five models, affects performance across voting, bagging, boosting, and stacking approaches. Experiments evaluated ten machine learning models on the UCI Hepatitis dataset using 5-fold cross-validation, with performance assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Among individual models, the support vector machine (SVM) achieved the highest accuracy (84.52%) and an AUC of 0.873, while CatBoost and random forest (RF) achieved accuracies of 83.87% and 83.23%, respectively; K-nearest neighbors (KNN) and naïve Bayes (NB) produced comparatively high recall. The five-model soft-voting ensemble achieved 91.84% accuracy, 0.960 AUC, 92.16% F1-score, and 95.92% recall. These findings indicate that multi-model ensembles can improve outcome prediction and high-risk patient identification. The results also suggest that performance depends on strategic model selection rather than ensemble size alone. The proposed 2 + n framework provides a structured approach to flexible model combination across ensemble techniques. Validation using larger, independent clinical datasets is required before broader application.
journal: Journal of the Nigerian Society of Physical Sciences

source_records.abstract: Machine learning (ML) models for hepatitis B virus (HBV) outcome prediction must address high variance, bias, and class imbalance. Previous ensemble-learning studies have commonly combined only two models or considered a limited set of ensemble techniques. This study evaluates how ensemble size, from two to five models, affects performance across voting, bagging, boosting, and stacking approaches. Experiments evaluated ten machine learning models on the UCI Hepatitis dataset using 5-fold cross-validation, with performance assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Among individual models, the support vector machine (SVM) achieved the highest accuracy (84.52%) and an AUC of 0.873, while CatBoost and random forest (RF) achieved accuracies of 83.87% and 83.23%, respectively; K-nearest neighbors (KNN) and naïve Bayes (NB) produced comparatively high recall. The five-model soft-voting ensemble achieved 91.84% accuracy, 0.960 AUC, 92.16% F1-score, and 95.92% recall. These findings indicate that multi-model ensembles can improve outcome prediction and high-risk patient identification. The results also suggest that performance depends on strategic model selection rather than ensemble size alone. The proposed 2 + n framework provides a structured approach to flexible model combination across ensemble techniques. Validation using larger, independent clinical datasets is required before broader application.

title: Ayurvedic Management of Chronic Hepatitis B: A Case Report
abstract: Background: Chronic hepatitis B is a viral infection associated with serious complications, including liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, highlighting the need for effective management strategies. Case Presentation: A 31-year-old male with a one-year history of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity presented with intermittent anorexia and no other significant symptoms. The patient was monitored over a period of 16 months. Intervention: The patient was managed with an Ayurvedic treatment regimen aimed at supporting liver health. The interventions included Phalatrikādi Kvātha, A combination of Tamālakī, Bhṛṅgarāja, Madhuka, and Trikaṭu Cūrṇa, Mustā Ghana Vaṭī, Bhūmyāmalakī Svarasa, Bhṛṅgarāja Cūrṇa, and Āmalakī Rasāyana. Liver function tests (LFTs) and HBV DNA quantitative polymerase chain reaction (PCR) were used to assess the response to treatment. Outcome: HBV DNA levels decreased from 6318 IU/mL in June 2023 to Conclusion: This case describes observed improvement in laboratory parameters during Ayurvedic management of chronic hepatitis B. However, findings from a single case cannot establish treatment efficacy or causality, and controlled clinical studies are required to determine the therapeutic efficacy and clinical relevance of Ayurvedic interventions in chronic hepatitis B. Keywords: Chronic hepatitis B, Case report, Ayurvedic herbal treatment, HBV DNA PCR

title: Pegylated interferon α-2b add-on to nucleos(t)ide analogues reduces hepatocellular carcinoma and decompensation in advanced fibrotic chronic hepatitis B
abstract: BACKGROUND The current therapeutic strategy of adding pegylated interferon (Peg-IFN) α-2b to nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) is primarily aimed at achieving functional cure. However, its value in improving prognosis and the suitable candidates for this combination strategy in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis remain to be further explored. AIM To evaluate the long-term prognosis benefit of add-on Peg-IFNα-2b therapy in patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. METHODS This retrospective cohort study enrolled patients diagnosed with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or compensated cirrhosis. Participants were divided into two groups: (1) Those receiving combination therapy (Peg-IFNα-2b add-on to ongoing NA treatment); and (2) Those receiving NA monotherapy. A 1:1 propensity score matching approach was applied to balance baseline characteristics between groups. In survival analysis, the outcomes of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and decompensated cirrhosis were stratified by baseline clinical features and established HCC risk scores. RESULTS The analysis included 302 matched pairs, with a median follow-up duration of 220 weeks. Combination therapy was associated with a significantly lower risk of developing HCC (hazard ratio = 0.22; 95%CI: 0.11-0.48) and decompensated cirrhosis (hazard ratio = 0.39; 95%CI: 0.20-0.77) than NA monotherapy. These benefits were particularly pronounced among patients classified as intermediate-to-high risk by validated HCC prediction models and in those with persistent biochemical abnormalities lasting > 12 months. CONCLUSION Add-on therapy with Peg-IFNα-2b to NAs is significantly associated with reduced HCC and decompensation in high-risk patients with HBV-related advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis, supporting its use in this population.

title: The Relationship between Serum Hepatitis B Virus DNA Level and Liver Fibrosis Status among Patients with Chronic HBV Infection in Chumphon: Findings from the National Surveillance Program
abstract: Objective: To determine the prevalence and screening coverage of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, examine the relationship between HBV DNA level and liver fibrosis, and assess antiviral treatment among patients with chronic HBV infection in Chumphon Province. Materials and Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study included individuals born before 1992 and high-risk groups screened between October 2024 and June 2025 across all 11 districts of Chumphon Province. Data included HBV serology, HBV DNA level, liver fibrosis assessed by the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and ultrasonography, and antiviral treatment. Results: Among 23,040 individuals screened (99.9% of the target), 462 were newly HBsAg-positive, yielding a prevalence of 2.0%, comparable with the national prevalence of 1.7%. Of these, 408 continued follow-up; median age was 54 years, and females predominated. HBV DNA ≥2,000 IU/mL was present in 48.3%. Higher viral load was significantly associated with greater fibrosis: APRI >0.5 occurred in 62.7% versus 37.3%, and APRI >1.0 in 94.3% versus 5.7% (p<0.001). Overall, 36.3% had significant fibrosis and 10.1% had cirrhosis, predominantly in the high-viral-load group. Among 149 patients who underwent ultrasonography, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma were detected in 11.5% and 1.3%, respectively, exclusively in the high-viral-load group. Tenofovir alafenamide was prescribed to 37.2% overall and 72.6% of patients with high viral loads. Conclusion: Higher HBV DNA levels were associated with greater liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. These findings support proactive HBV screening and improved access to antiviral therapy. Combining HBV DNA measurement, APRI, and liver ultrasonography may facilitate risk stratification and early detection of advanced liver disease, supporting efforts toward viral hepatitis elimination.

source_records.title: The Relationship between Serum Hepatitis B Virus DNA Level and Liver Fibrosis Status among Patients with Chronic HBV Infection in Chumphon: Findings from the National Surveillance Program
source_records.abstract: Objective: To determine the prevalence and screening coverage of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, examine the relationship between HBV DNA level and liver fibrosis, and assess antiviral treatment among patients with chronic HBV infection in Chumphon Province. Materials and Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study included individuals born before 1992 and high-risk groups screened between October 2024 and June 2025 across all 11 districts of Chumphon Province. Data included HBV serology, HBV DNA level, liver fibrosis assessed by the aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio index (APRI) and ultrasonography, and antiviral treatment. Results: Among 23,040 individuals screened (99.9% of the target), 462 were newly HBsAg-positive, yielding a prevalence of 2.0%, comparable with the national prevalence of 1.7%. Of these, 408 continued follow-up; median age was 54 years, and females predominated. HBV DNA ≥2,000 IU/mL was present in 48.3%. Higher viral load was significantly associated with greater fibrosis: APRI >0.5 occurred in 62.7% versus 37.3%, and APRI >1.0 in 94.3% versus 5.7% (p<0.001). Overall, 36.3% had significant fibrosis and 10.1% had cirrhosis, predominantly in the high-viral-load group. Among 149 patients who underwent ultrasonography, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma were detected in 11.5% and 1.3%, respectively, exclusively in the high-viral-load group. Tenofovir alafenamide was prescribed to 37.2% overall and 72.6% of patients with high viral loads. Conclusion: Higher HBV DNA levels were associated with greater liver fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. These findings support proactive HBV screening and improved access to antiviral therapy. Combining HBV DNA measurement, APRI, and liver ultrasonography may facilitate risk stratification and early detection of advanced liver disease, supporting efforts toward viral hepatitis elimination.

title: Hepatocellular carcinoma in the hepatitis B likely vaccinated and likely unvaccinated age groups in The Gambia: a prospective cohort study
abstract: The Gambia started Hepatitis B vaccination in July 1986 and achieved nationwide coverage in February 1990. However, not much is known about its effect on Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in The Gambia. We assess the differences in the features of HCC in both the Hepatitis B likely vaccinated and likely unvaccinated age groups in The Gambia. The study was a prospective cohort study that recruited patients with suspected HCC referred to the Medical Research Council liver clinic, Gambia Unit (MRC) from June 2012 to September 2019. Clinical, radiological, fibroscan and laboratory data were collected in all patients. Five hundred and forty two patients were recruited into the study. The majority (91.3%) of the patients were in the likely unvaccinated age group and most (88.8%) were born in The Gambia. Those born outside The Gambia were mostly Senegalese, Sierreleonean, and Guineans. The HCC patients in the hepatitis B likely unvaccinated age group were likely to be born in The Gambia 448 (90.5%) vs. 33 (70.2%) (p = < 0.001) as compared to the likely vaccinated age group. They were also less likely to have a positive HBsAg 332 (67.9%) vs. 40 (86.9%) ( p = 0.007) but had a lower AFP levels3897 (1.07-135000) vs. 9969 (3- 80000) ( p = 0.007) and a higher FIB4 score 5.2 (0.4–69.9) vs. 1.9 (0.5–57.9) (p = < 0.001) as compared to those HCC patients in the likely vaccinated age group. There were no differences in clinical manifestations, liver function tests and median survival. The majority of the HCC patients were in the likely unvaccinated age group and were also born in The Gambia. This suggest that the early introduction of nationwide Hepatitis B vaccination in 1990 into the EPI program in The Gambia may have had a positive effect in the incidence of Hepatocellular Carcinoma in the vaccinated age group. To strengthen these gains, a nationwide screening and treatment program needs to be implemented for those in the unvaccinated age groups.

title: NK cell reconfiguration and cytokine dynamics during pegylated interferon-α and nucleos(t)ide analogs combination therapy in chronic hepatitis B
abstract: HBsAg loss remains a major challenge in chronic hepatitis B (CHB). This study aimed to characterize the dynamic changes in NK cell phenotypes, receptor expression, and cytokine profiles during pegylated interferon-α (PEG-IFNα) and nucleos(t)ide analogs (NAs) combination therapy and their association with clinical outcomes. Twenty-seven CHB patients receiving PEG-IFNα and NAs combination therapy were stratified into on-treatment HBsAg loss group (HBsAg < 0.05 IU/mL, n = 10) and non-HBsAg loss group ( n = 17) at week 48. Flow cytometry assessed NK cell subsets (CD56 bright , CD56 dim ) and receptor expression (NKG2D, NKp30, NKp46, KIR, NKG2A, TIM3). Serum cytokines (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-10) were measured by ELISA. Correlations of virological markers with NK cell subsets/receptors or cytokines were analyzed. PEG-IFNα and NAs combination therapy expanded CD56 bright NK cells while reducing CD56 dim subsets in both on-treatment HBsAg loss and non-HBsAg loss groups. In the on-treatment HBsAg loss group, persistent KIR upregulation was observed in CD56 bright NK cells, whereas CD56 dim NK cells maintained elevated NKG2A expression. Cytokine analysis showed that the on-treatment HBsAg loss group exhibited significantly lower serum levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-2), while maintaining higher levels of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10. Correlation analysis revealed significant inverse correlations between HBsAg and CD56 bright NK cell proportion/ receptor expression, whereas HBsAg correlated positively with CD56 dim NK cell frequency in on-treatment HBsAg loss group. Moreover, HBsAg was positively correlated with pro-inflammatory cytokine levels in both treatment groups. PEG-IFNα and NAs combination therapy is associated with on-treatment HBsAg loss at week 48, potentially through optimizing cytokine responses, regulating NK cell balance (CD56 bright /CD56 dim ) and related receptors. Study limitations include the single-center design and moderate sample size. MR-53-26-076931 Date of registration: 31 August 2026. title: Resolved hepatitis B is associated with higher reactivation risk than chronic infection after chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: BACKGROUND Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a cornerstone treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation risk, particularly among patients with prior infection, remains incompletely characterized, with international guidelines providing discordant risk classifications. We hypothesized that patients with resolved HBV infection undergoing TACE face a higher reactivation risk than currently estimated by international guidelines. AIM To determine the incidence and risk factors of HBV reactivation in patients undergoing TACE for HBV-related HCC. METHODS We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent TACE for HBV-related HCC at a tertiary hospital during 2007-2025. Patients receiving baseline antiviral therapy were excluded. Patients with definitive serostatus (n = 774) were stratified into chronic-infection [hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive, n = 727] and resolved-infection (HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive, n = 47) groups. Cumulative incidences and risk factors were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression, with robustness evaluated through multiple imputation, competing-risks, and antiviral-naive sensitivity analyses. RESULTS During a median follow-up of 16.7 months, HBV reactivation occurred in 60 patients (6.1% overall). Patients with resolved HBV status had a higher reactivation rate (21.3% vs 6.9%; P CONCLUSION HBV reactivation occurred in approximately 6% of patients undergoing TACE, with resolved infection status conferring > 3-fold higher risk and reactivation incidence exceeding 20%. These findings support prophylactic antiviral therapy rather than monitoring alone for HBsAg-negative/anti-hepatitis B core antibody-positive patients undergoing TACE.

title: A cost-effective SYBR Green based Real-Time PCR platform for reliable detection of Hepatitis B virus: Establishment and clinical validation
abstract: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a major global health challenge, and accurate, rapid, and affordable molecular diagnostics are essential for timely detection, particularly in resource-limited settings where commercial molecular assays are often inaccessible. This study aimed to establish and validate an in-house SYBR Green-based real-time PCR assay for qualitative detection of HBV DNA in serum and plasma as a reliable and cost-effective alternative to commercial assays. An in-house SYBR Green real-time PCR assay targeting the HBV S gene was developed and validated. Analytical specificity was evaluated using clinically relevant pathogens, while analytical sensitivity was determined by serial dilutions of HBV DNA. Clinical performance was assessed using 112 patient samples and compared with a commercial real-time PCR assay. The assay demonstrated 100% analytical specificity and a limit of detection of 10 IU/mL. Diagnostic sensitivity and specificity were 95.74% (95% CI: 85.75–98.83) and 100% (95% CI: 94.42–100.00), respectively, with a positive predictive value of 100% and a negative predictive value of 97.01%. Agreement with the commercial assay was significant (Pearson’s χ2 = 104.03, *p* < 0.001), and inter-assay variability was < 1%. The in-house assay reduced reagent costs by approximately 78% (US$5.32 vs. US$24.69 per test) while maintaining diagnostic performance comparable to the commercial reference assay, supporting its application for routine HBV diagnosis in resource-limited settings.

title: ANTENATAL HEPATITIS B TESTING GAPS IN NIGERIA: SECONDARY ANALYSIS OF AGGREGATE ESTIMATES FROM THE 2024 NIGERIA DEMOGRAPHIC AND HEALTH SURVEY.
abstract: Nigeria carries one of the world’s largest hepatitis B burdens, and mother-to-child transmission is a major route of new infection. Routine antenatal hepatitis B screening has been a national policy for years, but nationally representative household-survey evidence on reported antenatal hepatitis B testing was previously unavailable. This is a descriptive secondary analysis of published aggregate estimates from the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) report and does not use individual-level survey records. We report hepatitis B awareness and recent testing among women, antenatal hepatitis B testing, and reported positive test results among women represented in the relevant recent-pregnancy population. The 2024 NDHS reported that 53.4% of women aged 15–49 had heard of hepatitis B, among whom 12.9% reported testing in the preceding year. Table 19.13 (FMoHSW et al., 2025), reported that 16.4% (N = 8,236) of the women represented in the table were tested for hepatitis B during antenatal care and that 0.6% reported a positive test result; however, the table described its denominator inconsistently. Reported antenatal testing was lower among women in rural areas and lower wealth and education categories and varied substantially across states, particularly in the North East and North West. These findings highlight substantial gaps and variation in reported antenatal hepatitis B testing and support consideration of integrated hepatitis B screening within existing antenatal services, consistent with the WHO triple-elimination framework.

title: Clonorchis sinensis co-infection potentiates polymorphonuclear-myeloid-derived suppressor cells expansion and metabolic reprogramming in chronic hepatitis B patients
abstract: BACKGROUND Clonorchis sinensis (C. sinensis ) co-infection is known to accelerate disease progression and induce immune tolerance in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV), particularly in regions where both infections are endemic. Metabolic reprogramming has emerged as a key driver of immunosuppression. These metabolic shifts are often orchestrated by myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), which expand during chronic infections to promote immune tolerance. sinensis co-infection reprograms metabolism to favor MDSC-linked suppression and how this process relates to normal liver enzyme levels remains unclear. AIM To investigate whether C. sinensis co-infection induces MDSC- linked metabolic reprogramming in patients with HBV and normal liver enzyme levels. METHODS In this cross-sectional study, a total of 117 participants were enrolled and assigned to four groups: Healthy controls (n = 30), C. sinensis mono-infected participants (n = 29), HBV mono-infected participants (n = 28), and co-infected participants (n = 30). Serum cytokine profiles were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassay, amino acid metabolites using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and MDSC subsets using flow cytometry. Spearman correlation and mediation analyses were performed to explore the relationships among inflammation, metabolism, and immunity. RESULTS HBV mono-infected and co-infected patients showed no statistically significant differences in liver enzyme and HBV DNA levels. However, compared with the HBV mono-infected group, the co-infected group had higher levels of the inflammatory cytokine: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), accompanied by markedly lower interferon-γ (IFN-γ) levels. Flow cytometric assay revealed that polymorphonuclear MDSCs (PMN-MDSCs) showed the greatest expansion in the co-infected group, and their proportion correlated strongly with IL-6 and TNF-α levels. Metabolically, the co-infected group had a significantly higher ornithine-to-arginine ratio. Mediation analysis suggested that PMN-MDSCs accounted for approximately 45% of the total effect of IL-6 on IFN-γ suppression. sinensis co-infection was associated with immunosuppression through IL-6/TNF-α-linked PMN-MDSC expansion and elevated ornithine-to-arginine ratio, resulting in suppressed IFN-γ production despite normal liver enzyme levels.

title: Prevalence of markers of hepatitis B, C and HIV infection among patients of pediatric oncohematology departments
abstract: The aim of the study was to conduct a retrospective analysis of the prevalence of markers for hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV), and HIV infection among patients in pediatric onco-hematology departments at the Dmitry Rogachev National Medical Research Center of Pediatric Hematology, Oncology and Immunology (hereinafter referred to as the Center) between 2013 and 2025, and to compare these findings with general population prevalence rates for chronic HBV, chronic HCV, and HIV infection. Materials and methods. A retrospective analysis was performed on the detection rates of markers for HBV, HCV, and HIV infection among onco-hematology patients aged 0—19 years treated at the Center between 2013 and 2025. A comparative analysis was conducted against the prevalence of these infections in the country's pediatric population during the period from 2013 to 2024. Testing for HBV markers was performed in 17,816 patients, for HCV markers in 17,762 patients, and for HIV infection markers in 17,741 patients. HBV markers were identified via HBsAg and/or HBV DNA testing; HCV markers via anti-HCV and/or HCV RNA testing; and HIV infection via immunoblotting results. The mean detection rates for HBV, HCV, and HIV infection markers were 1.1%, 0.1%, and 0.1%, respectively, of all patients tested. A comparison of the detection rates of HBV, HCV, and HIV markers among pediatric patients in onco-hematology units with the prevalence of these infections in the country's pediatric population revealed rates that were 6, 45, and 3 times higher ( p < 0.001), respectively. Pediatric patients in onco-hematology units constitute a high-risk group for HBV, HCV, and HIV infections.

title: Tenofovir Alafenamide in Chronic Hepatitis B: Real-World Outcomes
abstract: Objectives: Long-term viral suppression with nucleos(t)ide analogues is the cornerstone for preventing disease progression in chronic hepatitis B (CHB).Tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) provides comparable antiviral efficacy to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) with improved bone and renal safety.This study aimed to evaluate the real-world efficacy and safety of TAF in CHB patients. Materials and Methods:Patients aged ≥18 years receiving TAF for ≥6 months between January 2019 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed.Coinfected patients and those with decompensated cirrhosis were excluded.Virological suppression was defined as hepatitis B virus (HBV)-DNA <20 IU/mL, and biochemical response was defined as alanine aminotransferase (ALT) <40 U/L.Results: Among 100 patients (mean age 59.39±12.67years; 69% male), 91% had previously received TDF, with osteopenia/osteoporosis being the most common switching reason (67%).At one year, significant reductions were observed in aspartate aminotransferase (p=0.001) and ALT (p=0.004)levels, while serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate remained stable with no significant changes (p=0.088 and p=0.571, respectively).The ALT normalization rate remained stable during follow-up (91% at baseline vs. 94% at one year; p=0.687).HBV-DNA suppression was 77.3% at baseline and 97.2% at month 36, with complete virological response achieved in 98.8% of patients.Fibrosis-4 index and aspartate aminotransferase to platelet ratio index scores remained stable throughout follow-up.Hepatic steatosis was present in 39.6% of patients at baseline.Conclusion: TAF therapy maintained high, sustained virological suppression and demonstrated a favorable renal safety profile in predominantly TDF-experienced patients with CHB.

Materials and Methods:Patients aged ≥18 years receiving TAF for ≥6 months between January 2019 and December 2025 were retrospectively analyzed.Coinfected patients and those with decompensated cirrhosis were excluded.Virological suppression was defined as hepatitis B virus (HBV)-DNA <20 IU/mL, and biochemical response was defined as alanine aminotransferase (ALT) <40 U/L.Results: Among 100 patients (mean age 59.39±12.67years; 69% male), 91% had previously received TDF, with osteopenia/osteoporosis being the most common switching reason (67%).At one year, significant reductions were observed in aspartate aminotransferase (p=0.001) and ALT (p=0.004)levels, while serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate remained stable with no significant changes (p=0.088 and p=0.571, respectively).The ALT normalization rate remained stable during follow-up (91% at baseline vs. 94% at one year; p=0.687).HBV-DNA suppression was 77.3% at baseline and 97.2% at month 36, with complete virological response achieved in 98.8% of patients.Fibrosis-4 index and aspartate aminotransferase to platelet ratio index scores remained stable throughout follow-up.Hepatic steatosis was present in 39.6% of patients at baseline.Conclusion: TAF therapy maintained high, sustained virological suppression and demonstrated a favorable renal safety profile in predominantly TDF-experienced patients with CHB.

title: Prevalence and Molecular Detection, and Characterization of Hepatitis A and B Viruses and Their Public Health Implication in Maiduguri Metropolis, Borno State, Nigeria
abstract: Background: Hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) remain important public health concerns in developing countries due to inadequate sanitation, unsafe water, and poor hygiene. This study determined the prevalence of HAV-specific antibodies and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) among patients attending selected health facilities in Maiduguri Metropolis, Borno State, Nigeria. Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 440 participants recruited from four major health facilities. Blood samples were screened for HAV immunoglobulin G (IgG), immunoglobulin M (IgM), and HBsAg using standard serological methods. Sociodemographic characteristics and potential risk factors were obtained using structured questionnaires. Associations between infection status and selected variables were analyzed using appropriate statistical tests at a significance level of p 0.05). Significant associations were observed between educational level and HAV IgM seropositivity (p = 0.0158), occupation and HAV/HBV co-infection (p = 0.0326), age and HAV IgM seropositivity (p = 0.0062), and access to water supply, hand-washing practices, and travel history with HAV seropositivity (p < 0.0001). Of the 34 HBsAg-positive samples identified, three had insufficient volumes for molecular analysis, leaving 31 samples for PCR amplification. Multiplex PCR successfully amplified 12 samples, revealing the circulation of HBV genotypes B and E. HBV genotype B was detected at an expected amplicon size of 281 bp using Mix A, while genotype E was amplified at 167 bp using Mix B. The remaining samples tested negative for genotypes A, C, D, and F. The findings confirm the endemic circulation of HBV genotype E and the presence of the relatively uncommon genotype B within the study population, highlighting the genetic diversity of HBV strains in Maiduguri. No participant had received hepatitis vaccination. Conclusion: HAV and HBV remain endemic in Maiduguri, with environmental and behavioural factors playing significant roles in transmission. Strengthening health education, improving water, sanitation and hygiene, expanding HBV screening and vaccination, introducing targeted HAV vaccination, and enhancing routine surveillance are essential to reduce the burden of viral hepatitis in the study area.

source_records.title: Prevalence and Molecular Detection, and Characterization of Hepatitis A and B Viruses and Their Public Health Implication in Maiduguri Metropolis, Borno State, Nigeria
source_records.abstract: Background: Hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) remain important public health concerns in developing countries due to inadequate sanitation, unsafe water, and poor hygiene. This study determined the prevalence of HAV-specific antibodies and hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) among patients attending selected health facilities in Maiduguri Metropolis, Borno State, Nigeria. Methods: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 440 participants recruited from four major health facilities. Blood samples were screened for HAV immunoglobulin G (IgG), immunoglobulin M (IgM), and HBsAg using standard serological methods. Sociodemographic characteristics and potential risk factors were obtained using structured questionnaires. Associations between infection status and selected variables were analyzed using appropriate statistical tests at a significance level of p 0.05). Significant associations were observed between educational level and HAV IgM seropositivity (p = 0.0158), occupation and HAV/HBV co-infection (p = 0.0326), age and HAV IgM seropositivity (p = 0.0062), and access to water supply, hand-washing practices, and travel history with HAV seropositivity (p < 0.0001). HBV genotype B was detected at an expected amplicon size of 281 bp using Mix A, while genotype E was amplified at 167 bp using Mix B. The remaining samples tested negative for genotypes A, C, D, and F. The findings confirm the endemic circulation of HBV genotype E and the presence of the relatively uncommon genotype B within the study population, highlighting the genetic diversity of HBV strains in Maiduguri. No participant had received hepatitis vaccination. Conclusion: HAV and HBV remain endemic in Maiduguri, with environmental and behavioural factors playing significant roles in transmission. Strengthening health education, improving water, sanitation and hygiene, expanding HBV screening and vaccination, introducing targeted HAV vaccination, and enhancing routine surveillance are essential to reduce the burden of viral hepatitis in the study area.

title: Estimating new viral hepatitis infections from reported acute cases in the United States
abstract: Abstract Background New viral hepatitis infections may go unreported because many infections are asymptomatic, some people with symptoms do not seek testing, and gaps in surveillance capacity limit identification of acute cases. We present an updated approach to estimate the burden of new viral hepatitis infections from reported acute cases. Methods We estimated the proportion of new viral hepatitis infections expected to be symptomatic from the literature and the proportion of symptomatic patients expected to seek testing from a national survey. We estimated reporting proportions for new hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) infections from the literature and developed a Poisson regression model to estimate the proportion of new hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections reported as acute cases based on predictors of jurisdictional surveillance capacity. Results Overall multipliers to adjust reported acute cases in 2022 ranged from 1.7 (95% uncertainty interval [95% UI] 1.4–2.3) to 2.7 (2.1–3.9) across jurisdictions for hepatitis A, 5.7 (3.0–20.7) to 9.1 (4.7–33.4) for acute hepatitis B, and 2.8 (2.2–3.9) to 67.3 (30.5–152.8) for acute hepatitis C. Applying these multipliers, estimated numbers of new HAV, HBV, and HCV infections in 2022 nationally were 4,982 (95% UI 4,010–5,052), 15,725 (11,095–31,144), and 39,734 (26,740–50,075), respectively. Conclusions Reported cases might substantially underestimate new viral hepatitis infections, and adjustment factors vary widely by jurisdiction. Our updated approach enables public health officials to estimate the burden of new viral hepatitis infections more accurately for program planning and evaluation.

title: Investigating the Seroprevalence of HBV and HCV infection in Potential Donors: Study from Iranian Tissue Bank and Research Center (2014-2021)
abstract: Background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections are major contributors to liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), affecting millions worldwide. Transmission routes and clinical outcomes vary between the two viruses, with both posing significant challenges in transplantation. Understanding the seroprevalence of HBV and HCV is crucial for effective pre-transplant screening and post-transplant management to prevent disease transmission and recurrence. The present study aimed to investigate the prevalence of HBV and HCV in potential donors referred to the Iranian Tissue Bank and Research Center (ITBRC). Methods: The study population was potential donors referred to ITBRC between 2014 and 2021, including two groups: brain death donors and forensic donors referred from the Iranian Legal Medicine Organization. For HBV, HBsAg and HBsAb; and for HCV, HCV-Ab were detected by ELISA. Results: A total of 3862 individuals were studied (32.4% female and 67.6% male), including 1349 (34.9%) brain death and 2513 (65.1%) circulatory death donors. Analysis showed 1.19 times higher rates of HCV infection in women than in men, but this was not statistically significant. Logistic regression showed no significant effects of donor type on HCV infection rates. For HBV, brain death subjects had over three times higher odds of HBsAg-positive tests compared to circulatory death (OR = 3.06, p-value < 0.05). Additionally, female cases had lower odds of an HBsAg- positive test compared to males (OR = 0.56). The odds of a positive HBsAg test in brain death cases were 2.7 times higher than in circulatory death, with 3.49% of cases being positive for HBsAg and HBsAb test results. Conclusion: In conclusion, this retrospective study demonstrated a higher prevalence of HBV-positive tests in brain death donors compared to circulatory death donors, with female donors showing lower odds of HBsAg-positive tests compared to males.

title: A dual recombinant strategy to quantify PreS1 antibody in hepatitis B patients with genotype B or C virus by ELISA
abstract: Elevated levels of anti-preS1 antibodies in patients correlate with faster hepatitis B virus (HBV) clearance, since preS1 is vital for viral entry. However, accurate quantification of preS1 antibodies is hindered by the variation of HBV genotypes. Herein, a quantitative preS1 antibody assay was developed for Chinese patients with predominant HBV genotypes B and C. First, to address genotype diversity, we constructed a dual recombinant protein combining genotype B and C preS1. Second, a mouse-human chimeric antibody with high and comparable affinity for both B and C preS1 is developed as the standard for quantification by screening and cloning. An optimized ELISA kit using these components demonstrated good specificity, accuracy, reproducibility and stability, with a linear range of 10–100 ng/mL. This approach extends the patient coverage in China to over 95%, providing a valuable diagnostic tool. This work demonstrates a proof-of-concept model for developing broad-coverage assays for other multi-genotype viral diseases.

source_records.title: A dual recombinant strategy to quantify PreS1 antibody in hepatitis B patients with genotype B or C virus by ELISA
source_records.abstract: Elevated levels of anti-preS1 antibodies in patients correlate with faster hepatitis B virus (HBV) clearance, since preS1 is vital for viral entry. However, accurate quantification of preS1 antibodies is hindered by the variation of HBV genotypes. Herein, a quantitative preS1 antibody assay was developed for Chinese patients with predominant HBV genotypes B and C. First, to address genotype diversity, we constructed a dual recombinant protein combining genotype B and C preS1. Second, a mouse-human chimeric antibody with high and comparable affinity for both B and C preS1 is developed as the standard for quantification by screening and cloning. An optimized ELISA kit using these components demonstrated good specificity, accuracy, reproducibility and stability, with a linear range of 10–100 ng/mL. This approach extends the patient coverage in China to over 95%, providing a valuable diagnostic tool. This work demonstrates a proof-of-concept model for developing broad-coverage assays for other multi-genotype viral diseases.

title: Mechanisms and Research Progress of LncRNA-Mediated Regulation of Viral Infections
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), a class of RNA molecules whose transcripts exceed 200 nucleotides in length and typically lack protein-coding capacity, were once widely regarded as “transcriptional noise.” However, recent studies have shown that lncRNAs can encode small peptides and play critical roles in biological processes, including gene expression regulation, cell differentiation, and immune response. Viral infections, as a common disease, can reshape the transcriptome of host cells, in which the differential expression of lncRNAs is a core link in host–virus interactions. This review aims to deeply analyze the multidimensional regulatory mechanisms of lncRNAs in the host antiviral innate immune response. It elaborates in detail on how lncRNAs construct the host antiviral defense by regulating pattern recognition receptor (PRR) signaling pathways, the production and signal transduction of interferons (IFNs), as well as the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs). Additionally, we conducted an in-depth analysis of the complex functions of lncRNAs in regulating programmed cell death (PCD), including key processes such as pyroptosis, autophagy, and apoptosis, and integrated specific research cases in infections caused by multiple significant viruses, including influenza A virus (IAV), human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). We aim to provide novel strategies for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of viral diseases.

title: Hospital-linked and community-based viral hepatitis screening among Romanian migrants in Seville: A feasibility study
abstract: Introduction Romanian migrants may be at increased risk of viral hepatitis because many originate from countries with intermediate or high endemicity. Targeted, culturally adapted screening strategies are therefore needed to improve case finding and prevention. Our aim was to explore the feasibility of two sequential viral hepatitis screening strategies among Romanian migrants living in Seville, Spain. Methods We conducted a two-phase opportunistic screening study. Phase 1 was a Consulate-facilitated, hospital-based program using venipuncture and comprehensive serological testing. Phase 2 was a community-based program delivered at an Orthodox church using rapid diagnostic tests. Demographic characteristics, recruitment output, serological findings, fibrosis markers, and linkage to care were recorded. Results Of the total participants ( n = 54), the number of individuals screened was higher in the community-based intervention ( n = 39) than the hospital-based program ( n = 15). Median age was 48.5 (39.5–58) years, and 74.1% were women. No active viral hepatitis infections were identified. In phase 1, 66.7% of participants (10/15) lacked hepatitis B immunity and were candidates for vaccination, while 6.7% (1/15) had non-invasive markers compatible with intermediate fibrosis and required further assessment. In phase 2, 2.6% of participants (1/39) had antibodies against hepatitis C virus with documented prior cured infection. Conclusions In this pilot study, community-based screening in a familiar religious setting appeared more productive and operationally feasible for short-term recruitment than a hospital-based approach. These findings support the feasibility of decentralized strategies to improve engagement and may inform future micro-elimination programs in migrant populations.

title: Predictors of immunological non-response despite virological suppression in people living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Immunological Nonresponse (INR) in people living with HIV (PLWH) is characterized by inadequate CD4+ T-cell recovery despite effective viral suppression through antiretroviral therapy (ART). This systematic review and meta-analysis identify key clinical, demographic, and molecular predictors of INR to optimize immune recovery strategies. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, yielding 59 eligible studies, with a total of 19,511 individuals with INR. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), and pooled effect estimates were calculated as odds ratio (OR), mean difference (MD), or standardized mean difference (SMD). Significant predictors of INR included male sex [OR 1.33 (1.12-1.58)], older age [MD 2.61 (1.42-3.81)], intravenous drug use [OR 1.67 (1.15-2.42)], hepatitis B coinfection [OR 1.30 (1.08-1.57)], hepatitis C coinfection [OR 1.85 (1.50-2.28)], tuberculosis [OR 1.77 (1.41-2.21)], advanced HIV stage [OR 2.66 (2.34-3.02)], and lower baseline and nadir CD4+ counts [SMD -3.82 (-4.94-(-2.70)), SMD -1.69 (-2.69-(-0.68))], respectively. Additionally, 57 biomarkers were identified as potential predictors of INR, implicating several immunological pathways. These findings underscore the multifactorial nature of INR and the need for personalized approaches among ART-treated individuals.

title: Vaccination for girls and women across the life course: Evidence-based recommendations for clinical practice and policy.
abstract: Vaccination across the life course is a cornerstone of preventive health care for girls and women. Although WHO recommends completion of essential vaccines by adolescence, global coverage remains suboptimal. Vaccine-preventable diseases-including HPV-related cancers, vaginal, vulvar, anal, oropharyngeal, influenza, pertussis, hepatitis B, herpes zoster, and pneumococcal disease-continue to impose a disproportionate burden on girls and women, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and migrant populations. Key life stages, such as childhood (early and middle), adolescence, preconception, pregnancy, postpartum, midlife, and beyond, offer critical opportunities for immunization. Obstetricians, gynecologists, midwives, and other women's healthcare providers are uniquely positioned to integrate vaccination into routine care in all settings and influence vaccine acceptance. Strengthening vaccine advocacy within women's health care is essential to reduce preventable morbidity and mortality and advance health equity for girls and women globally. This paper presents evidence-based recommendations for equitable vaccination across the life course of girls and women, synthesizing guidance from WHO, the Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization (SAGE), the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and national immunization technical advisory groups. Vaccines reviewed include HPV, tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis (Tdap), influenza, hepatitis B, measles-mumps-rubella (MMR), varicella, herpes zoster, pneumococcal, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and COVID-19. A life-course framework is proposed, emphasizing maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and integration of regular and opportune vaccination into routine obstetric and gynecologic services. Practical implementation strategies and policy recommendations are outlined to support FIGO member societies.

title: Harm reduction services in female prisons: a scoping review exploring the situation in the MENA region.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study aims to explore and map the existing evidence on HR services, specifically NSP and OST, available to women in prison settings across MENA countries where such services are reported to exist, assessing their availability, accessibility, and gender responsiveness while identifying gaps in research, policy, and practice. Harm reduction (HR) is a public health and human rights approach aimed at reducing drug-related harms through interventions such as Opioid Substitution Therapy (OST) and needle and syringe programs (NSPs). People who use drugs (PWUDs) in prison face elevated risks of HIV, Hepatitis B and C, Tuberculosis and overdose. Women who use drugs (WWUDs) experience additional gender-specific vulnerabilities, yet little is known about its availability and gender responsiveness of prison-based HR in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. DESIGN/METHODOLOGY/APPROACH: This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Full-text peer-reviewed and grey literature published, in English, between 2014 and 2024 were retrieved from PubMed, Cochrane Library, JSTOR, Google Scholar and key organizational reports. Studies addressing NSP and/or OST in prison settings within MENA countries were included. Data were synthesized narratively focusing on service availability, accessibility and gender responsiveness. FINDINGS: Of 4,238 records identified, 27 studies met inclusion criteria (14 peer-reviewed articles and 13 grey literature sources). Evidence was concentrated in Iran, with limited data from Afghanistan, Morocco and Lebanon, and none from Algeria. OST was reported in several prison settings, while NSP was limited to Iran. Most studies lacked sex-disaggregated data, and where women were included, they were frequently underrepresented and rarely analyzed separately. Evidence on gender-responsive services, post-release care and monitoring and evaluation systems was limited. ORIGINALITY/VALUE: To the best of the authors' knowledge, this study provides the first regional synthesis of evidence on gender-responsive HR services for WWUD in MENA prisons, identifying substantial gaps in service provision, gender-disaggregated evidence and evaluation.

title: Perception of virus effects and vaccination among people with multiple sclerosis in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Background People with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) are at increased risk of infection due to immune dysregulation and exposure to disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Despite this risk, real-world vaccine uptake remains inconsistent. This study evaluated vaccination readiness, counseling practices, and infection-related perceptions among pwMS in Saudi Arabia. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among adults with MS ( n = 204) recruited using non-probability (convenience) sampling from tertiary-care clinical and community-based sources. The survey assessed demographic characteristics, vaccination attitudes and uptake, counseling experiences, perceptions of infection risk related to MS and DMTs, and awareness of Epstein–Barr virus (EBV). Internal consistency of multi-item measures was acceptable (Cronbach's α = 0.72). Descriptive statistics were used to summarize outcomes. Results The cohort was relatively young (mean age 35.7 years), with two-thirds aged 25–44 years (25–34 years: 38.2%; 35–44 years: 36.8%). Most participants held a bachelor's degree (66.7%). Attitudes toward routine vaccination were frequently non-committal: 47.6% were somewhat or very likely to vaccinate, 33.8% were neutral, and 18.6% were somewhat or very unlikely; separately, 60.8% agreed or somewhat agreed that routine vaccines might be harmful for pwMS. COVID-19 vaccination uptake was high (72.5%), whereas influenza vaccination was low (30.9%). Uptake of other adult vaccines, including hepatitis B, meningococcal, herpes zoster, and human papillomavirus vaccines, was < 10% for each. Perceived infection vulnerability was substantial, with 62.7% expressing concern about viral infections due to MS and 71.1% believing that DMTs increased susceptibility, consistent with 59.4% receiving high-efficacy DMTs. Awareness of EBV was limited: 26.5% had heard of EBV, 16.6% perceived an MS–EBV association, and 21.1% were aware of possible causality. Nearly half of participants (49.0%) were undecided about a hypothetical EBV vaccine, while approximately 44% expressed willingness to receive it. Counseling gaps were evident, as only 32.8% reported any discussion about vaccination with clinicians; counseling prior to DMT initiation and during ongoing treatment was reported by 16.2% and 19.1%, respectively. Conclusions In a young and highly educated cohort of pwMS in Saudi Arabia, vaccine hesitancy and counseling gaps persist despite high perceived infection risk. These findings highlight the need for structured and routine vaccine counseling, particularly at MS diagnosis and before initiating high-efficacy DMTs, to improve uptake of influenza and other recommended adult vaccines in MS clinics.
