title: Medical Quackery in India: A Multidisciplinary Patient-Safety Challenge
abstract: Informal, unqualified and unauthorized healthcare practice remains an important feature of India's pluralistic healthcare environment. The literature uses heterogeneous terminology, including quackery, informal healthcare providers and unqualified practice, which can obscure the patient-safety dimension of the problem. To map Indian evidence concerning informal, unqualified and unauthorized healthcare practice; identify documented patient-safety, antimicrobial, specialty-specific and health-system risks; characterize drivers of continued use; and propose a practical prevention framework. A structured open-evidence scoping search was conducted through 17 August 2026 using PubMed/MEDLINE, PubMed Central and targeted searches of publicly accessible scholarly and Indian regulatory sources. Thirty-five unique records were screened independently by two reviewers. A 10-record calibration exercise showed 9/10 (90%) agreement; one disagreement was resolved by consensus. Ten records proceeded to full-text assessment and all ten were included. During revision, a supplementary dermatology-focused search was undertaken to contextualize dermatology, venereology and leprosy (DVL)-specific safety risks; eight sources were selected for contextual synthesis. This targeted, non-systematic exercise was kept separate from the original PRISMA denominator. Data were synthesized narratively and thematically using the PRISMA-ScR reporting framework. The ten included sources covered informal-provider access and expenditure, neonatal care, abortion services, infectious-disease transmission, antibiotic prescribing, pharmacy dispensing, dental quackery, dermatology quackery and unlicensed antidepressant prescribing. The evidence demonstrates that informal providers may be deeply embedded in underserved communities because of accessibility, affordability and social context, while also documenting important safety risks. In a rural Ujjain study, 11,336 of 15,322 prescriptions (74%) contained antibiotics; 14,620 of the 15,472 antibiotics prescribed (95%) were broad-spectrum. A neonatal study of 830 informal providers identified important knowledge gaps in evidence-based neonatal care. A Gujarat hepatitis B outbreak was linked to inadequately sterilized needles and syringes used by an unqualified practitioner. Supplementary DVL evidence additionally documented non-physician and non-dermatologist pathways for topical corticosteroid misuse and highlighted qualification and training requirements for hair transplantation, botulinum toxin and laser procedures. Medical quackery should be addressed as a patient-safety and health-system problem rather than solely as professional misconduct. Prevention should combine credential verification, accessible formal care, antimicrobial stewardship, risk-based enforcement, public education, coordinated reporting and digital accountability. The SAFE-MED framework—Screening, Accreditation/verification, Fast reporting, Enforcement, Monitoring, Education and Digital surveillance—provides a practical structure for coordinated action. Keywords: Medical quackery; Informal healthcare providers; Unqualified practitioners; Patient safety; India; Antimicrobial resistance; Dental quackery; Dermatology; Medical misinformation; Health regulation

title: Single Jaundice in Cirrhosis: A Neglected Acute Decompensation of Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure and Mortality.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare the risk of acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) and short-term outcomes among cirrhotic patients with single jaundice, acute decompensation (AD) (including ascites, variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, and/or bacterial infection), and non-AD non-jaundice. METHODS: We analyzed cirrhotic inpatients without obstructive jaundice enrolled from two large multicenter prospective cohorts. Patients were divided at admission into classical AD, single jaundice, or non-AD non-jaundice groups. Baseline characteristics, ACLF development, and short-term outcomes were compared between groups. RESULTS: Among 2645 cirrhotic patients, classical AD, single jaundice, and non-AD non-jaundice were observed in 2163 (81.78%), 267 (10.09%), and 215 (8.13%), respectively. The 90-day liver transplant (LT)-free mortality was comparable between single jaundice patients and classical AD patients (15.09% vs. 17.81%, p = 0.266), but significantly higher than non-AD non-jaundice patients (2.45%; p < 0.01). The prevalence of ACLF (16.10% vs. 16.09%, p = 1.000) and pre-ACLF (9.36% vs. 6.43%, p = 0.094) were comparable between the single jaundice and classical AD groups. Intrahepatic precipitants, particularly hepatitis B flare with hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation (odds ratio [OR] 2.69; p = 0.002), spontaneous hepatitis B flare with high HBV-DNA load (OR 23.75; p < 0.001), superimposed hepatitis A/E virus infection on HBV infection (OR 13.40; p < 0.001) and hepatotoxic drug usage (OR 3.64; p < 0.001) were associated with single jaundice. CONCLUSIONS: Cirrhotic inpatients with single jaundice show comparably high short-term mortality and ACLF risk to those with classical AD. Single jaundice shall be considered as an AD event and is predominantly triggered by intrahepatic insults, warranting surveillance equivalent to classical AD and prioritized management of the precipitants.
authors: Chinese (Acute on) Chronic Liver Failure Consortium (Ch‐CLIF.C)

title: Potential Risks and Benefits of Low-barrier Access and Monitoring for HIV Pre-exposure Prophylaxis: A Modeling Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) prevents HIV acquisition, but its population-level impact is limited by access barriers. Low-barrier delivery of daily oral tenofovir disoproxil fumarate/emtricitabine (TDF/FTC), such as over-the-counter (OTC) availability, could improve access by eliminating clinic visits, though reduced monitoring may increase risks including drug resistance, renal toxicity, and hepatitis B virus (HBV) reactivation. We estimated the benefits and risks of OTC PrEP. METHODS: Using a stochastic network-based model of HIV/STI transmission among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM) in Atlanta, we simulated 2 delivery pathways: clinic-based PrEP and OTC PrEP with simplified initiation and reduced monitoring. We modeled 10%-50% increases in PrEP coverage over 10 years. Outcomes included HIV infections averted, STI incidence, contraindicated PrEP use (GFR 90% without reducing prevention benefits, and frequent renal-monitoring reduced renal risk. CONCLUSIONS: OTC PrEP could produce population-level HIV prevention benefits if it expands coverage beyond clinic-based care. However, its net public health impact depends on implementation choices that preserve safety functions, particularly HIV testing at initiation and renal monitoring, without undermining access gains.

title: Circulation and recombination-driven diversity of duck hepatitis B virus in domesticated geese in Guangdong, southern China
abstract: Duck hepatitis B virus (DHBV) is a valuable comparative model for human hepatitis B virus (HBV) due to its shared genomic organization and reverse transcription-based replication, despite having only ∼40% nucleotide identity. Infection is generally asymptomatic in adult birds but causes reduced hatchability, impaired embryo development, and growth retardation in young waterfowl, leading to economic losses. As a major waterfowl producer, China faces risks from this endemic virus. This study analyzed 901 deceased domesticated geese liver samples from five regions in Guangdong province, southern China. Nested PCR screening revealed an overall infection prevalence of 34.1% (307/901). Amino acid analysis of the preS domain of the large envelope protein showed extensive variability, including the G133E mutation in 47.7% (21/44) of strains and genotype-associated substitutions at residues 117 and 120. Genetic characterization of 44 complete genomes revealed exclusive circulation of genotypes I and II (DHBV-I and DHBV-II), with no detection of the Western-associated DHBV-III. Phylogenetic analysis indicated frequent duck-goose host-switching and viral circulation between provinces, likely facilitated by the live-poultry trade. We identified 20 recombination events, six of which involved our sequences as parental strains, demonstrating that active recombination among co-circulating strains drives viral heterogeneity in Guangdong. These findings highlight the ongoing circulation and evolutionary complexity of DHBV in southern China and underscore the need for longitudinal genomic surveillance to detect emerging variants.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨鸭乙型肝炎病毒(DHBV)在家鹅中的传播及其由重组驱动的多样性,因为DHBV由于其共享的基因组结构和基于逆转录的复制机制,尽管仅有约40%的核苷酸同源性,仍是人类乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)的重要比较模型。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究分析了从广东省五个地区收集的901例死亡家鹅肝脏样本,以评估DHBV的患病率及其遗传多样性。
elements_zh.methods: 采用嵌套PCR筛查检测DHBV感染,结果显示总体感染患病率为34.1%(307/901)。对大包膜蛋白preS结构域的氨基酸分析以及44个完整基因组的遗传特征分析被用于评估变异性和传播模式。
elements_zh.main_results: 对preS结构域的氨基酸分析显示存在广泛的变异,包括47.7%(21/44)的菌株中出现的G133E 突变,以及在第117和120位残基中与基因型相关的取代。遗传特征分析显示仅存在基因型I和II(DHBV-I和DHBV-II)的特异性传播,未检测到与西方相关的DHBV-III。鉴定了20个重组事件,其中6个涉及本研究序列作为亲本株。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现突显了DHBV在华南地区持续传播及其进化复杂性,强调了共循环菌株之间活跃重组在驱动病毒异质性中的作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果突出了需要长期的基因组监测监测以检测新兴的DHBV变种,并为在家鹅种群中监测和管理该病毒提供策略依据。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于横断面设计,可能无法全面捕捉DHBV传播随时间的变化动态。证据强度中等,基于患病率和单一地理区域的遗传分析。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the circulation and recombination-driven diversity of duck hepatitis B virus (DHBV) in domesticated geese in Guangdong, southern China, as DHBV is a valuable comparative model for human hepatitis B virus (HBV) due to its shared genomic organization and reverse transcription-based replication, despite having only ∼40% nucleotide identity.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed 901 deceased domesticated geese liver samples collected from five regions in Guangdong province, southern China, to assess the prevalence and genetic diversity of DHBV.
analysis_en.methods: Nested PCR screening was used to detect DHBV infection, revealing an overall infection prevalence of 34.1% (307/901). Amino acid analysis of the preS domain of the large envelope protein and genetic characterization of 44 complete genomes were conducted to evaluate variability and circulation patterns.
analysis_en.main_results: Amino acid analysis of the preS domain showed extensive variability, including the G133E mutation in 47.7% (21/44) of strains and genotype-associated substitutions at residues 117 and 120. Genetic characterization revealed exclusive circulation of genotypes I and II (DHBV-I and DHBV-II), with no detection of the Western-associated DHBV-III. Twenty recombination events were identified, six of which involved the study sequences as parental strains.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the ongoing circulation and evolutionary complexity of DHBV in southern China, emphasizing the role of active recombination among co-circulating strains in driving viral heterogeneity.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results underscore the need for longitudinal genomic surveillance to detect emerging DHBV variants and inform strategies for monitoring and managing the virus in domesticated geese populations.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its cross-sectional design, which may not capture the full dynamics of DHBV circulation over time. The evidence is moderate, based on prevalence and genetic analysis of a single geographic region.

title_zh: 广东地区家鹅中鸭乙型肝炎病毒的传播与重组驱动的多样性
source_body_en: Duck hepatitis B virus (DHBV) is a valuable comparative model for human hepatitis B virus (HBV) due to its shared genomic organization and reverse transcription-based replication, despite having only ∼40% nucleotide identity. Infection is generally asymptomatic in adult birds but causes reduced hatchability, impaired embryo development, and growth retardation in young waterfowl, leading to economic losses. As a major waterfowl producer, China faces risks from this endemic virus. This study analyzed 901 deceased domesticated geese liver samples from five regions in Guangdong province, southern China. Nested PCR screening revealed an overall infection prevalence of 34.1% (307/901). Amino acid analysis of the preS domain of the large envelope protein showed extensive variability, including the G133E mutation in 47.7% (21/44) of strains and genotype-associated substitutions at residues 117 and 120. Genetic characterization of 44 complete genomes revealed exclusive circulation of genotypes I and II (DHBV-I and DHBV-II), with no detection of the Western-associated DHBV-III. Phylogenetic analysis indicated frequent duck-goose host-switching and viral circulation between provinces, likely facilitated by the live-poultry trade. We identified 20 recombination events, six of which involved our sequences as parental strains, demonstrating that active recombination among co-circulating strains drives viral heterogeneity in Guangdong. These findings highlight the ongoing circulation and evolutionary complexity of DHBV in southern China and underscore the need for longitudinal genomic surveillance to detect emerging variants.
abstract_zh: 鸭乙型肝炎病毒(DHBV)由于其共享的基因组结构和基于逆转录的复制机制,尽管仅有约40%的核苷酸同源性,仍是人类乙型肝炎病毒(HBV)的重要比较模型。成年鸟类感染通常无症状,但在幼年水禽中会导致孵化率降低、胚胎发育受损和生长迟缓,从而造成经济损失。作为主要的水禽生产国,中国面临这种地方性病毒带来的风险。本研究分析了广东省五个地区收集的901例死亡家鹅肝脏样本,通过嵌套PCR筛查发现总体感染患病率为34.1%(307/901)。对大包膜蛋白preS结构域的氨基酸分析显示存在广泛的变异,包括47.7%(21/44)的菌株中出现的G133E 突变,以及在第117和120位残基中与基因型相关的取代。对44个完整的基因组进行遗传特征分析,结果显示仅存在基因型I和II(DHBV-I和DHBV-II)的特异性传播,未检测到与西方相关的DHBV-III。系统发育分析表明鸭与鹅之间存在频繁的宿主交换,以及病毒在省际间的传播,这可能由活禽贸易所促进。我们鉴定了20个重组事件,其中6个涉及本研究序列作为亲本株,表明在广东地区共循环的菌株之间活跃的重组驱动了病毒的异质性。这些发现突显了DHBV在华南地区持续传播及其进化复杂性,并强调了需要长期的基因组监测监测以检测新兴的DHBV变种。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果突出了需要长期的基因组监测监测以检测新兴的DHBV变种,并为在家鹅种群中监测和管理该病毒提供策略依据。

title: Metabolic-epigenetic regulation of the HBV cccDNA reservoir: pathways underpinning viral persistence
abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a global public health burden, and functional cure represents the primary goal of clinical management. The nuclear covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) minichromosome stably maintained in infected hepatocytes constitutes the major barrier to HBV cure. Clinically, functional cure is defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance with undetectable serum HBV DNA after finite treatment, a definition that does not require complete cccDNA elimination. At the molecular level, functional cure is thought to be associated with stable transcriptional silencing of cccDNA and integrated HBV DNA, a state biologically distinct from physical cccDNA depletion. Accumulating data demonstrate that the persistence and transcriptional homeostasis of the cccDNA reservoir are controlled by viral proteins and dynamically shaped by host metabolic signaling and epigenetic remodeling. Here, we first outline key steps of the HBV life cycle to establish the mechanistic context for cccDNA formation and replenishment, and then focus our synthesis on the integrated host metabolic-epigenetic network that governs cccDNA establishment, transcriptional activity, stability, and clearance. We dissect how central carbon metabolites, bile acid signaling, histone post-translational modifications, and immune cytokines converge to modulate cccDNA reservoir homeostasis, and critically evaluate the strength of evidence supporting their physiological relevance in the chronically infected human liver. We also discuss mechanisms of HBV immune evasion, including hepatitis B virus X protein (HBx)-driven epigenetic reprogramming and subviral particle-associated immune tolerance. We summarize preclinical and clinical therapeutic strategies targeting the metabolic-epigenetic microenvironment, viral assembly, antigen secretion, and cccDNA modulation to achieve a functional cure for HBV infection. Finally, we outline key unresolved challenges in the field, including the undefined in vivo cccDNA turnover kinetics, the poorly characterized physiological relevance of cell-to-cell transmission, the inherent limitations of gene-editing technologies, and the urgent need for specific non-invasive biomarkers reflecting intrahepatic cccDNA activity.

source_records.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a global public health burden, and functional cure represents the primary goal of clinical management. The nuclear covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) minichromosome stably maintained in infected hepatocytes constitutes the major barrier to HBV cure. Clinically, functional cure is defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance with undetectable serum HBV DNA after finite treatment, a definition that does not require complete cccDNA elimination. At the molecular level, functional cure is thought to be associated with stable transcriptional silencing of cccDNA and integrated HBV DNA, a state biologically distinct from physical cccDNA depletion. Accumulating data demonstrate that the persistence and transcriptional homeostasis of the cccDNA reservoir are controlled by viral proteins and dynamically shaped by host metabolic signaling and epigenetic remodeling. Here, we first outline key steps of the HBV life cycle to establish the mechanistic context for cccDNA formation and replenishment, and then focus our synthesis on the integrated host metabolic-epigenetic network that governs cccDNA establishment, transcriptional activity, stability, and clearance. We dissect how central carbon metabolites, bile acid signaling, histone post-translational modifications, and immune cytokines converge to modulate cccDNA reservoir homeostasis, and critically evaluate the strength of evidence supporting their physiological relevance in the chronically infected human liver. We also discuss mechanisms of HBV immune evasion, including hepatitis B virus X protein (HBx)-driven epigenetic reprogramming and subviral particle-associated immune tolerance. We summarize preclinical and clinical therapeutic strategies targeting the metabolic-epigenetic microenvironment, viral assembly, antigen secretion, and cccDNA modulation to achieve a functional cure for HBV infection. Finally, we outline key unresolved challenges in the field, including the undefined in vivo cccDNA turnover kinetics, the poorly characterized physiological relevance of cell-to-cell transmission, the inherent limitations of gene-editing technologies, and the urgent need for specific non-invasive biomarkers reflecting intrahepatic cccDNA activity.

title: Hepatitis Delta in Spain: A Nationwide Prospective Characterization of Active Infection and Liver Disease Severity.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Hepatitis delta virus (HDV) infection is associated with rapid progression to cirrhosis and liver-related complications. We aimed to characterize the clinical and virological profile of anti-HDV-positive individuals in Spain and identify factors associated with active infection and advanced fibrosis. METHODS: This nationwide, multicentre, prospective observational study included adults with positive anti-HDV serology enrolled between April 2024 and March 2026 across 72 hospitals in 15 Spanish Autonomous Communities. Demographic, virological, laboratory and clinical data were collected in a centralized database. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with active HDV infection and advanced liver fibrosis. RESULTS: Among 1,112 anti-HDV-positive individuals, 670/1,112 (60%) were male, median age was 54 years (IQR 43-61), and 457/926 (49%) were born in Spain. HIV co-infection and anti-HCV positivity were present in 189/944 (20%) and 217/1,112 (21%), respectively. HDV-RNA was detectable in 436/1,047 patients (42%), with a median viral load of 4.1 log IU/mL (IQR 2.9-5.1). Genotype 1 accounted for 108/121 (89%) genotyped infections. Advanced fibrosis was present in 222/536 (41%) evaluable patients and was more frequent in those with active infection than in non-viremic individuals (155/261, 59% versus 59/256, 23%; p<0.001). Active HDV infection was independently associated with younger age, hepatitis B virus (HBV) antiviral therapy, lower platelet count and lower albumin levels, whereas African origin was associated with lower odds of detectable HDV-RNA. Advanced fibrosis was independently associated with active HDV infection, HBV antiviral therapy and higher gamma-glutamyltransferase levels, while higher platelet count and haemoglobin levels were associated with lower odds of advanced fibrosis. CONCLUSIONS: Active HDV infection and advanced liver disease remain common in Spain. These findings support systematic HDV-RNA testing, standardized fibrosis assessment and close clinical follow-up of anti-HDV-positive individuals.

title: Assay-Dependent Variability in HBV DNA Quantification: An Illustrative Case Report
abstract: Abstract Introduction Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection affected approximately 254 million people worldwide in 2022 and remains a major cause of liver-related morbidity and mortality according to the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Hepatitis Report 2024. Regular monitoring of serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels and HBV DNA viral load is essential in patients who do not meet criteria for antiviral therapy, as it helps assess disease activity and guide future treatment decisions. Case Description A 29-year-old female, six months postpartum, with chronic HBV infection, presented for routine follow-up. Serial monitoring showed fluctuating HBV DNA levels despite normal liver function tests. To confirm this trend, HBV viral load testing was performed on the same blood sample using two different platforms: a semi-automated assay and a fully automated assay. The results showed a discrepancy between the two methods. Conclusion Our case highlights the potential importance of standardised laboratory methods and consistent testing platforms for reliable interpretation of HBV viral load during long-term monitoring. It also supports findings from existing literature regarding semi-automated and automated assay performance.

title: Haemovigilance and Epidemiological Surveillance of Transfusion-Transmitted Infections in Greece, 1996-2023: National Donor Screening Data and Recipient Investigations.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Surveillance of transfusion-transmitted infections (TTIs) supports blood safety, particularly for multi-transfused patients such as those with haemoglobinopathies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective descriptive analysis of aggregated national surveillance data from Greece. We report aggregate infectious-marker positivity values from national surveillance summaries for 1996-2009. We also report NAT yields in 2007-2023, the transmission categories of HIV-positive donors in 2010-2019 and recipient investigations reported to the national haemovigilance system in 2005-2023. RESULTS: More than 14 million donations were tested in 1996-2023. For 1996-2009, the surveillance summaries reported aggregate positivity of 0.39% for HBsAg, 0.09% for anti-HCV, 0.017% for syphilis and 0.008% for anti-HIV1/2. In 2007-2023, NAT detected 1,393 serology-negative infectious donations among 8,389,862 donations reported as tested (estimated 16.6 per 100,000; 95% CI 15.7-17.5), of which 1,321 were HBV. In 2010-2019, 56.9% of HIV-positive donors were men who have sex with men and 25.3% were heterosexual. Fifteen recipient investigations were reported among 13.6 million issued components; transmission was excluded in one. CONCLUSION: In 2007-2023, NAT detected infectious donations that serology missed, mostly HBV. Reported recipient infections were rare but included emerging pathogens. Annual data are needed to assess trends.

title: Sexually Transmitted Infections in the Third Age: Rising Risk Among over 65-Year-Old Persons in Southern Sardinia
abstract: Background/Objectives: Population ageing and the persistence of sexual activity in later life are reshaping sexual health needs. Older adults are often overlooked in STI surveillance and prevention, and data on infections among those aged ≥65 years remain limited. This study describes the epidemiological and clinical profile of STIs in older adults in Southern Sardinia. Our aim was to describe the epidemiological and clinical characteristics of sexually transmitted infections in adults aged 65 years and older attending a specialist STI outpatient clinic in Southern Sardinia over a 15-year period. Methods: We conducted a retrospective longitudinal study of all new STI diagnoses in patients aged ≥65 years attending the Dermatology STI outpatient clinic at the University Hospital of Cagliari between 2010 and 2024. Demographic, behavioural, clinical, and laboratory data were extracted from medical records and analysed descriptively. Results: Among 2378 new STI cases, 69 (2.9%) occurred in patients aged ≥65 years (median age 74 years; range 65–83), predominantly men (85.5%) and mostly heterosexual. Most patients reported limited or no condom use, with 84.1% stating that they never used condoms. The most frequent diagnoses were condylomata acuminata (52.2%) and syphilis (31.9%), followed by molluscum contagiosum and other viral and bacterial infections. Relevant co-infections were observed: hepatitis B virus in 17.4%, HIV in 5.8%, and hepatitis C virus in 1.4% of cases. Follow-up ranged from 1 month to 5 years; 46.4% achieved complete clinical resolution, 33.3% required ongoing treatment, and 20.3% were lost to follow-up. Conclusions: Although they represent a small proportion of all STI cases, infections in older adults constitute a meaningful and likely underestimated public health issue. Low risk perception, limited condom use, and diagnostic delays contribute to underdiagnosis. Integrating systematic sexual health assessment, counselling, and targeted prevention into geriatric and primary care is essential to improve the early detection and management of STIs in this growing age group.

title: Pre-Transplant Laboratory Parameters and Early Outcomes in HBV-Related Deceased Donor Liver Transplantation
abstract: Background: Early postoperative outcomes after deceased donor liver transplantation (DDLT) are influenced by recipient, donor, and perioperative factors. Routinely available pre-transplant laboratory tests may provide complementary information for risk assessment. This study aimed to explore associations between routine pre-transplant laboratory parameters and early postoperative outcomes after DDLT. Methods: This retrospective single-center descriptive pilot study included 32 adult recipients who underwent DDLT for hepatitis B virus-related liver disease between 2004 and 2019. Pre-transplant biochemical and hematologic parameters were evaluated in relation to in-hospital mortality, biliary complications, infectious complications, bleeding, and hospital stay. Descriptive group comparisons and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed. Results: In-hospital mortality occurred in 6/32 recipients (18.8%), biliary complications in 5/32 (15.6%), infectious complications in 9/32 (28.1%), and postoperative bleeding in 2/32 (6.2%). Routine laboratory parameters did not significantly discriminate mortality. Among 28 recipients with available potassium measurements, four developed biliary complications. Potassium showed exploratory discrimination for biliary complications (AUC = 0.818, p = 0.048), based on only four biliary events. Bilirubin and GGT did not significantly discriminate mortality. Conclusions: Routine pre-transplant laboratory parameters showed no consistent association with in-hospital mortality after DDLT. The potassium association is hypothesis-generating and requires validation in larger cohorts before clinical application.

title: Rapid, reversible RNA/DNA precipitation using rare earth ion coordination
abstract: Efficient recovery and removal of nucleic acids remain major challenges in molecular biology, diagnostics, and viral-vector manufacturing. Conventional precipitation methods often require organic solvents, low temperatures, and extended centrifugation, while nuclease-based contaminant removal can be incomplete and/or is incompatible with downstream workflows. Here, we evaluate NADA, a trivalent rare earth-based reagent, for rapid, solvent-free precipitation of RNA and DNA, and ALGO-mediated recovery of the full range of properties of unmodified RNA. Using hepatitis B virus pre-genomic RNA, lambda bacteriophage DNA, and the HBV nucleocapsid as model systems, we show that NADA rapidly sequesters both ssRNA and dsDNA from solution, reducing Midori Green nucleic acid fluorescence and UV absorption to baseline levels. The NADA complex prevents HBV core protein binding to the HBV pgRNA, and therefore triggering of nucleocapsid formation, even when added simultaneously with core protein, suggesting that lanthanide ion coordination, out-competes the cognate Cp for viral RNA-binding interactions. Recovery with ALGO restores pgRNA integrity and functionality, enabling subsequent assembly of the expected T=4/T=3 nucleocapsids. In contrast, pre-assembled nucleocapsids resist NADA-ALGO treatment, demonstrating coat protein capsid-mediated protection of encapsidated pgRNA. Similar outcomes for lambda dsDNA establish NADA/ALGO as a rapid, reversible, and selective alternative platform for nucleic acid precipitation, with potential applications in viral particle purification, contaminant removal, and RNA handling workflows.

title: Evaluation of Vaccination Coverage and Compliance Among Medical Students: A Cross-Sectional Documentary Analysis
abstract: Introduction: Vaccination is a cornerstone of primary healthcare, particularly critical for medical students and healthcare professionals due to constant occupational exposure to infectious agents.This study aimed to evaluate the vaccination status of medical students at a private higher education institution in the Federal District, Brazil, comparing their self-perceived protection with actual immunization records.Methods: A cross-sectional, descriptive study was conducted between August 2024 and July 2025, involving 90 medical students from various semesters.Data collection utilized structured online questionnaires and documentary analysis of digital vaccination cards submitted via the "Meu SUS Digital" platform or physical records.Evaluated immunizations included hepatitis A, hepatitis B (HBV), measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR), tetanus/dT, yellow fever, meningococcal C and ACWY, influenza (2024 campaign), and COVID-19.Data were analyzed using absolute and relative frequencies.Results: Although 75 (83.3%)participants self-reported having an up-to-date vaccination card and 85 (94.4%) felt protected for clinical practice, documentary analysis revealed severe gaps.Only 16 (19.3%)participants possessed a completely up-to-date occupational schedule for all analyzed immunogens.Significant deficits included 56 (67.5%) lacking hepatitis A doses, 77 (92.8%) lacking meningococcal ACWY records, and 22 (26.5%)lacking the 2024 influenza vaccine.The primary reasons cited for missing vaccines were lack of availability at the appropriate age (n = 10, 43.5%) and unknown causes (n = 10, 43.5%).Descriptively, students with parents in the healthcare field and those in advanced internship semesters showed proportionally higher completeness rates, although overall coverage remained insufficient.Furthermore, 57 (63.3%) respondents recognized a lack of information regarding occupational infection risks during their academic training.Conclusions: A profound discrepancy exists between medical students' perceived immunological protection and their actual immunization status.These findings highlight an urgent need for institutional interventions, curriculum enhancements, and mandatory vaccination verification protocols to safeguard students and patients in clinical learning environments.

title: Integrated Antigen-DNA Co-Detection Using Digital Microfluidics for Improving Diagnostic Accuracy in POCT Analysis.
abstract: Simultaneous detection of protein and nucleic acid (NA) provides complementary information essential for accurate analysis of complex samples. Conventional approaches for the analysis of protein and NA typically rely on separate workflows and instruments, limiting the reliability of point-of-care testing. Here, we present a digital microfluidics-based dual-mode molecular assay for simultaneous detection of both protein and NA from the same microscale sample. The protein is captured by a gold nanoparticle-antibody conjugate, while NA is enriched by magnetic beads. Magnetic manipulation separates the protein-containing fraction from NA, enabling separate analysis of the two molecular classes within an automated workflow. By integrating the analysis of protein and NA, the platform enables more accurate analysis than either modality alone. In 56 clinical samples, the combined analysis of hepatitis B surface antigen and DNA reduces the false-negative rate to 1.79%, compared with 12.5% for HBsAg alone. In food safety assays, simultaneous detection of Staphylococcus aureus-associated toxins and PMA-treated bacterial NA provides information not only on protein-based toxins, but also the presence and viability of bacteria within milk. This automated DMF-based dual-mode molecular assay provides a highly integrated strategy for multimodal POCT and public health risk assessment.

title: Proteome wide Mapping reveals a Neutralizing Epitope at the N-terminus of Hepatitis E Virus Capsid Protein with Implications for Vaccine Design
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis E virus (HEV) causes acute viral hepatitis (AVH), fulminant hepatitis and community-level outbreaks. Chronic HEV infection is observed in many solid organ transplantation patients. The disease worsens during pregnancy, with ~ 30% mortality rate. Earlier studies using different fragments of the purified viral capsid protein have identified the region encompassing major neutralizing epitopes in HEV capsid. However, there is no systematic study regarding repertoire of B-cell epitopes in HEV. This study aimed at unbiased identification of B-cell epitopes in the human-infecting genotypes of HEV, with the goal of designing a more potent HEV vaccine. Proteome-wide mapping of B-cell epitopes present in human-infecting HEV genotypes by cyclic peptide microarray using HEV patient sera reaveled the repertoire of B-cell epitopes in HEV. Importantly, HEV patient sera show highest reactivity against an epitope located between 116–126 aa of g1-HEV ORF2 protein. Synthetic peptides corresponding to the above epitope react with HEV-positive human sera. Recombinant 112–608 ORF2 protein immunized mice sera display higher anti-ORF2 IgG titre, virus neutralization titre (NT50) and memory T-cell response compared to that of the 368–606 ORF2. Furthermore, immunodepletion of the 112–608 ORF2 antigen immunized mice sera with synthetic peptide corresponding to 116–126 aa of g1-HEV ORF2 considerably reduces its anti-ORF2 antibody level and NT50 titres. In summary, we report a comprehensive data of B-cell epitopes in HEV and characterize a new neutralizing epitope at the N-terminus of 112–608 ORF2 protein, which contributes to its superior virus neutralization efficacy. These findings pave the way for development of next generation, more potent HEV vaccine.

Earlier studies using different fragments of the purified viral capsid protein have identified the region encompassing major neutralizing epitopes in HEV capsid. However, there is no systematic study regarding repertoire of B-cell epitopes in HEV. This study aimed at unbiased identification of B-cell epitopes in the human-infecting genotypes of HEV, with the goal of designing a more potent HEV vaccine. Proteome-wide mapping of B-cell epitopes present in human-infecting HEV genotypes by cyclic peptide microarray using HEV patient sera reaveled the repertoire of B-cell epitopes in HEV. Importantly, HEV patient sera show highest reactivity against an epitope located between 116–126 aa of g1-HEV ORF2 protein. Synthetic peptides corresponding to the above epitope react with HEV-positive human sera. Recombinant 112–608 ORF2 protein immunized mice sera display higher anti-ORF2 IgG titre, virus neutralization titre (NT50) and memory T-cell response compared to that of the 368–606 ORF2. Furthermore, immunodepletion of the 112–608 ORF2 antigen immunized mice sera with synthetic peptide corresponding to 116–126 aa of g1-HEV ORF2 considerably reduces its anti-ORF2 antibody level and NT50 titres. In summary, we report a comprehensive data of B-cell epitopes in HEV and characterize a new neutralizing epitope at the N-terminus of 112–608 ORF2 protein, which contributes to its superior virus neutralization efficacy. These findings pave the way for development of next generation, more potent HEV vaccine.

title: Hepatitis in the Shadow of Tuberculosis: Analysis of Morbidity among Staff of a Specialized Hospital
abstract: The article presents the results of a retrospective epidemiological analysis of the incidence of viral hepatitis B and C among healthcare workers at the Jalal-Abad Regional Tuberculosis Control Center (Kyrgyz Republic) over a ten-year period (2016–2025). The study revealed an increase in the detection rate of bloodborne infections from 4.5 to 10.6 per 100 employees by 2023, followed by a decline to 7.9 in 2025, which was attributed to organizational changes, such as staff and bed capacity reduction. It was established that the largest proportion of cases (61.5%) occurred among nursing staff, with the peak incidence observed in the 40–59 age group (69.2%). Two critical periods of occupational tenure risk were identified: 1–5 years (predominance of hepatitis B) and 11–15 years (predominance of hepatitis C). Dental interventions were identified as the most probable source of infection (53.8%). Vaccination coverage against hepatitis B among personnel reached 84.0%; however, a group of unvaccinated employees remains, necessitating enhanced control measures. Gender differences in incidence were nullified after adjustment for staff composition (p = 0.622). Recommendations were developed for optimizing vaccine prophylaxis, infection control, and dispensary follow-up in tuberculosis hospitals.

title: Virological Events During Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Therapy: A Multi-Source Evaluation
abstract: Background/Objectives: Virological findings during immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy may represent viral loss of control, pre-existing infection, tumour biomarkers, or infection after immune-related adverse event (irAE)-directed immunosuppression. Distinguishing these possibilities is important for treatment and diagnostic decisions. We evaluated virus-specific patterns across complementary data sources. Methods: We evaluated HBV, HCV, HIV, EBV, CMV, HSV, and VZV using FAERS disproportionality analysis (2011Q1–2026Q1), PubMed evidence mapping and appraisal, EBV endpoint verification, and review of ClinicalTrials.gov protocols by start era. Findings were interpreted in relation to prevention, monitoring, endpoint interpretation, and infectious mimic evaluation. Results: Among 200,699 primary suspect ICI reports, only HBV reactivation met the prespecified reporting criterion (226 reports; reporting odds ratio 1.20, 95% CI 1.06–1.37); this estimate did not persist with an oncology-restricted comparator (0.81, 0.71–0.94). Same report overlap of HBV with hepatic events and CMV with enterocolitis or pneumonitis identified diagnostically ambiguous settings without establishing event sequence. EBV DNA reflected viral inflammatory activity in some conditions but tumour burden in EBV-associated cancers. The evidence map included 198 publications, with design-specific appraisal of 84. Among 164 trials, conditional viral eligibility appeared in 49.0–57.1% across start eras, whereas longitudinal monitoring appeared in 8.2–19.6%. Conclusions: Reporting patterns were virus-specific and comparator-sensitive. The findings support HBV prevention, confirmation of HCV and HIV control, disease-specific interpretation of EBV markers, and CMV evaluation when inflammation or irAE-directed immunosuppression raises concern for infection. Context-specific assessment may help avoid unnecessary ICI interruption while identifying viral loss of control and infectious mimics.

title: Discovery of Thiazolamide-based PI4KIIIβ/HDAC Dual Inhibitors with Potent Activity against Hepatitis C Virus
abstract: Abstract Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains a critical global public health burden affecting hundreds of millions of people worldwide. The emergence of antiviral resistance persistently undermines the long-term clinical efficacy of current direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, creating an urgent need for therapeutics with different mechanisms of action. Host-directed multi-target therapy offers a promising avenue to overcome DAA resistance, yet dual inhibitors targeting HCV-essential host kinase phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase IIIβ (PI4KIIIβ) and epigenetic regulator histone deacetylases (HDACs) have not been reported for HCV treatment to date. Herein, we describe the rational design, chemical synthesis, and comprehensive biological evaluation of a series of novel thiazolamide-based dual PI4KIIIβ/HDAC inhibitors. Lead compounds displayed potent dual-target enzymatic inhibition, robust in vitro anti-HCV activity and excellent in vivo tolerability. This work establishes a novel host-directed dual-target therapeutic paradigm for HCV, providing a viable strategy to address the unmet clinical challenge of DAA resistance.

title: Synthesis of comparisons of multiple interventions in infectious diseases research: a scoping review
abstract: Abstract Background Evidence synthesis in infectious diseases research often involves comparing multiple interventions to assess relative efficacy or safety, usually through pairwise or network meta-analyses. However, the statistical methods used and whether they are applied appropriately in practice are frequently unclear. This scoping review provides an overview of how comparisons of multiple interventions are synthesised in infectious diseases research. Methods A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews using search terms related to meta-analyses and infectious diseases. Systematic reviews were included if they quantitatively compared three or more interventions for the prevention or treatment of infectious diseases. Results Of the 8160 records identified, 420 systematic reviews were eligible after full text screening. A random sample of 200 systematic reviews was selected for data extraction: 100 each from 2015–2019 and 2020–2024, to ensure representation of pre- and post-COVID infectious diseases. Systematic reviews of interventions for COVID-19 (n = 32), HIV/AIDS (n = 22), and hepatitis B (n = 22) were most common. Therapeutic interventions were assessed in 153 (76.5%) systematic reviews and preventive treatments in 47 (23.5%). For statistical comparison of interventions, 34 (17.0%) systematic reviews used only pairwise meta-analyses, 88 (44.0%) used only network meta-analyses, and 78 (39.0%) used both. Of the 166 network meta-analyses, 83 (50.0%) were implemented using a Bayesian framework. Only 41 (24.7%) assessed transitivity, that is, whether it is appropriate to combine evidence from direct and indirect comparisons of interventions, and 112 (67.5%) evaluated consistency, which quantifies the agreement between the effect estimates from direct and indirect comparisons. Conclusion Network meta-analysis is widely adopted in infectious diseases research. However, the key assumption of transitivity is rarely assessed. Improved adherence to publicly accessible protocols, thorough evaluation of assumptions, and transparent reporting is needed to improve the validity and reproducibility of evidence synthesis in infectious diseases research.

title: Trends in Hepatitis D Virus Prevalence Among HBsAg-Positive Individuals With and Without HIV in Italy: A Converging Epidemiology.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection has historically been more prevalent among people with HIV (PWH) due to shared transmission routes. Whether HIV status still identifies a subgroup at higher risk of HDV in contemporary settings remains unclear. METHODS: We performed two cross-sectional analyses assessing anti-HDV prevalence among HBsAg-positive PWH enrolled in the ICONA cohort in 2009-2012 and 2019-2023, compared with HIV-negative individuals from the MASTER and PITER cohorts. RESULTS: Anti-HDV prevalence among PWH declined from 19.1% to 12.5%, converging with that observed in HIV-negative individuals (12.7%). Injection drug use markedly decreased over time among PWH and remained the strongest determinant of HDV infection. In multivariable analyses, HDV seropositivity was associated with age, injection drug use, and birth outside Italy, but not with HIV infection in the contemporary period. CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that HIV infection is no longer independently associated with HDV infection in this setting and support universal HDV screening strategies.

title: Bone health trajectories following regimen optimization in male people living with HIV receiving TDF: a prospective, observational, cohort study
abstract: TDF exposure is associated with reduced bone mineral density (BMD) in people living with HIV (PLWH). Data remain limited evaluating changes in BMD and bone turnover markers (BTMs) after switching to tenofovir alafenamide (TAF), TDF/TAF-free regimens such as dolutegravir/lamivudine (DTG/3TC), or receiving treatment with zoledronic acid (ZOL). In this prospective cohort study, 223 virologically suppressed male PLWH with low BMD on TDF-based regimens were evaluated across four groups: (1) continuing TDF ( n = 48); (2) TDF plus intravenous ZOL 5 mg at baseline ( n = 37); (3) switching to BIC/FTC/TAF(bictegravir/emtricitabine/TAF) ( n = 70); or (4) switching to DTG/3TC ( n = 68). Primary outcomes were multivariable-adjusted absolute BMD change from baseline to week 48 across the femoral neck (FN), total hip (TH), and lumbar spine (LS), estimated using ANCOVA with 2,000 bootstrap resamples. Secondary outcomes included percent BMD changes and unadjusted BTM changes (β-CTX and P1NP) as median (IQR). Sensitivity analyses using 20 imputed datasets under the intention-to-treat principle were also conducted. A total of 189 participants completed the 48-week follow-up. Persistent BMD loss occurred at week 48 in the TDF group [median change: FN -0.01 (-0.04, 0.01)g/cm2; TH -0.01 (-0.06, 0.01)g/cm2; LS -0.02 (-0.05, 0.00)g/cm2]. In multivariable-adjusted models, all three intervention regimens were associated with significantly greater absolute BMD gains compared with TDF across all sites ( P < 0.05). At LS, adjusted mean differences were 0.09 g/cm2 (95% BCa CI: 0.07 to 0.12) for TDF + ZOL, 0.07 g/cm2 (95% BCa CI: 0.04 to 0.11) for BIC/FTC/TAF, and 0.11 g/cm2 (95% BCa CI: 0.07 to 0.14) for DTG/3TC (all P ≤ 0.001). No significant pairwise differences were found among the three intervention regimens. Regarding BTMs, TDF + ZOL was associated with the greatest percentage reduction in P1NP compared with both switch groups (both P < 0.001), as well as in β-CTX versus DTG/3TC ( P < 0.001). Conversely, the TDF group exhibited a significant increase in BTMs from baseline. Multiple imputation sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings. In relatively young male PLWH with low BMD and without chronic hepatitis B co-infection, switching from TDF to BIC/FTC/TAF or DTG/3TC, as well as ZOL co-administration, were associated with favorable 48-week BMD recovery. ZOL co-administration was characterized by the strongest suppression of bone turnover among all evaluated strategies. These findings reflect the overall benefits of diverse regimen-switching strategies in this specific population, supporting individualized bone management for PLWH receiving TDF.

title: Study on the Effects of Combined Exposure to a High-Fat, High-Sugar Diet and a High-Temperature, High-Humidity Environment on Adaptive Immunity in CHB Mice Based on Multi-Omics Analysis
abstract: (1) Background: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is a widely prevalent chronic liver disease, with a particularly high incidence in China. Recent studies indicate that external influences like a high-fat, high-sugar diet and high temperature and humidity may alter the hepatic immune microenvironment in CHB and hasten liver injury progression in patients. Nonetheless, the cumulative effect of these combined factors on liver damage and the immune remodeling process, along with its regulatory mechanisms, remains uncertain. (2) Objective: This research seeks to clarify the impact of simultaneous exposure to a high-fat, high-sugar diet and a high-temperature, high-humidity environment on CHB liver injury and its primary immunometabolic pathways. (3) Methods: This research employed recombinant adenovirus AdrcccDNA to establish a CHB mouse model (M group), and subsequently developed a combined exposure model through intervention with a high-fat, high-sugar diet and a high-temperature, high-humidity environment (NWS group). Subsequently, multi-omics analysis, WGCNA, immune infiltration analysis, and in vivo and in vitro experiments were employed to evaluate the effects of a high-fat and high-sugar diet combined with high-temperature and high-humidity exposure on the progression of CHB. (4) Results: HE staining, virology, and other results showed that combined exposure worsened liver injury and increased viral replication in CHB mice. WGCNA and immune infiltration analysis revealed CD4+ T cells as the key differential immune cells and identified 36 associated core mRNAs. Combined analysis revealed that miR-340-5p was significantly negatively correlated with Psat1 expression and highly associated with the proliferation and function of memory CD4+ T cells. In vivo validation indicated that in the NWS group, Psat1 levels were reduced, miR-340-5p levels were elevated, and the percentage of memory CD4+ T cells was diminished. After in vitro transfection with miR-340-5p mimics, Psat1 levels were downregulated in AML12 and primary CD4+T cells, indicating that miR-340-5p negatively influences Psat1. (5) Conclusions: This study demonstrates that combined exposure to a high-fat, high-sugar diet and a high-temperature, high-humidity environment may worsen CHB liver injury through miR-340-5p/Psat1-mediated immunometabolic regulation.

title: Development of a support tool for hepatitis C virus treatment decision making
abstract: Abstract Background: Timely initiation of treatment for hepatitis C virus (HCV) is essential for reducing both transmission and long-term health impacts. Decision support tools can assist patients by enhancing understanding, clarifying personal priorities, and guiding treatment selection. Methods: This exploratory, sequential mixed-methods study aimed to identify the key priorities for an HCV treatment decision aid and to co-create the tool with expert HCV nurses and people with lived and living experience. In phase 1, three focus groups with HCV nurse providers identified several central needs, while in phase 2, 30 participants with HCV experience reviewed the prototype tool using a questionnaire. Results: Phase 1 findings described the need for the tool to include support for newer providers; strategies to manage limited time, to address health literacy, and to tackle stigma and confidentiality concerns; and preferences related to layout, narrative elements, reminders, autonomy in treatment choices, side-effect information, provider communication, and linkage to care. In phase 2, Likert scale ratings (median scores range: 4–5) reflected strong endorsement, and qualitative responses emphasized four main areas: efficiency, clarity, content relevance, and visual design. Conclusions: Overall, the findings demonstrate that combining clinical expertise with lived experience can lead to the development of a meaningful patient-centred decision aid that supports informed choices about HCV treatment.

title: Hepatitis E Virus Genotype 3 in Quindío, Colombia: One Health Surveillance and First Genomic Characterization Reveal Cryptic Regional Divergence
abstract: Hepatitis E virus genotype 3 (HEV-3) is a zoonotic pathogen whose burden in Latin America remains underestimated. We conducted a cross-sectional One Health surveillance study (2019–2024) in Quindío, Colombia, testing 42 pig fecal, 8 farm runoff, 4 tributary water samples, and 5 clinical serum samples from patients with hepatitis of undetermined etiology by reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Positive and selected clinical/environmental samples underwent Oxford Nanopore MinION sequencing targeting the open reading frame 2 and 3 (ORF2/ORF3) junction, k-mer fingerprinting (k = 25), consensus generation, phylogenetic analysis, and Sanger confirmation. HEV RNA was detected in 8/42 pig fecal samples (19.0%), 4/8 runoff samples (50.0%), 1/4 tributary samples (25.0%), and 4/5 serum samples (80.0%). K-mer analysis identified strong HEV signals in two clinical samples (44.5% and 39.5% of reads) and wastewater (97.2%). Phylogenetic analysis classified Colombian isolates within HEV-3 (bootstrap 83%), while Sanger sequencing confirmed HEV-specific motifs. Two sequences were deposited in GenBank (PZ262436, PZ262437), representing the first Colombian HEV-3 genomic records. These findings demonstrate HEV-3 circulation across porcine, environmental, and human compartments and highlight substantial genomic divergence, supporting locally calibrated molecular approaches and strengthened One Health genomic surveillance in Colombia and Latin America.

title: Rat Hepatitis E Virus ( RHEV ) in Mus musculus and Rattus norvegicus in Northwestern Italy
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Hepatitis E virus (HEV) represents a major public health concern. Beyond the main zoonotic genotypes HEV‐3 and HEV‐4, with pigs and wild boars recognized as the primary reservoirs of infection, a genetically distinct hepevirus of rodent origin (species Rocahepevirus ratti, genotype C1) (rat HEV, RHEV) has recently been implicated in human hepatitis cases worldwide. Although several risk factors have been proposed, contact with rats has been documented in one human case only, and the sources and transmission routes of RHEV remain largely unclear. Of interest, RHEV RNA has recently been detected in farmed pigs, highlighting livestock environments as potential interspecies transmission interfaces. In light of these findings, we performed a molecular investigation for RHEV in rodents captured on farms raising different livestock species in Northwestern Italy (Piemonte region). Methods A total of 98 rodents, collected on 32 livestock farms, were tested for RHEV by a combined molecular approach based on RHEV specific real‐time reverse transcription (RT)‐PCR assay and a pan‐hepevirus heminested RT‐PCR. Positive samples were further processed to attempt full‐genome amplification. Results RHEV RNA was identified in a Norway rat ( Rattus norvegicus ) and in house mice ( Mus musculus ) , with detection rates of 16.6% (1/6; 95% CI: 0.41–64.1) and 7.0% (6/86; 95% CI: 2.6–14.5), respectively. The positive rodents were captured in five livestock farms, raising cattle, goats, and poultry, located across three municipalities. The nearly full‐length genome of a rat strain (RHEV/ Rattus norvegicus /38129‐22/ITA) was reconstructed. Pairwise nucleotide alignment showed high genetic relatedness of RHEV/ Rattus norvegicus /38129‐22/ITA with sequences previously identified in rodents and human patients, including those from European countries. Conclusions The identification of infected rodents in livestock farms highlights RHEV circulation in rural environments, where interactions among rodents, domestic animals, and humans may be facilitated. Additional studies are necessary to elucidate RHEV transmission dynamics and assess public health implications.

title: Immunization with an Escherichia coli-Produced Hepatitis E Virus Genotype 3 Virus-like Particle (HEV-3_p495) Confers Protection Against HEV-3 and HEV-4 Challenge in Pigs
abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) genotypes 3 and 4 are major zoonotic pathogens, with domestic pigs serving as an important reservoir. Vaccination of pigs may therefore help reduce HEV circulation and zoonotic transmission. We evaluated the protective efficacy of an Escherichia coli-produced HEV-3 virus-like particle (VLP), HEV-3_p495, against homologous HEV-3 and heterologous HEV-4 challenge in pigs. Juvenile pigs vaccinated three times with either 80 or 400 μg of HEV-3_p495 remained negative for HEV RNA in serum and feces during prolonged cohabitation with naturally HEV-3-infected pigs, whereas all non-vaccinated controls became infected. At market age, vaccination also provided strong protection against intravenous HEV-3 challenge, with complete protection against detectable infection in the four-dose group and in two of three pigs in the three-dose group. Importantly, HEV-3_p495 conferred cross-protection against HEV-4 following cohabitation exposure. Two-dose vaccination prevented detectable infection in two of three young pigs and delayed fecal virus detection without viremia in the remaining pig. At market age, all vaccinated pigs remained negative for HEV RNA in serum and feces following HEV-4 exposure, whereas all non-vaccinated controls became infected. These findings provide proof-of-concept evidence for homologous and cross-genotype protection by HEV-3_p495 and support its further evaluation as a candidate swine vaccine for reducing HEV infection and shedding.

title: Seroprevalence and risk factors of hepatitis E virus infection in a rural Argentine community: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is a leading cause of acute viral hepatitis worldwide. Rural populations and pig production systems in Argentina may be at increased risk of HEV exposure; however, epidemiological data from these settings remain scarce. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among residents of a rural community. Serum samples from 90 residents were tested for anti-HEV immunoglobulin G. Participants completed structured questionnaires and residential addresses were georeferenced to evaluate exposures and spatial distribution. Results Rural residents reported greater exposure to homemade pork and wild boar sausages, wastewater, untreated well water, agricultural settings, livestock, rodents and flood-prone areas compared with levels previously documented in the urban population of the same region. The overall seroprevalence was 23.3% (95% confidence interval 14.0 to 32.6). Age and history of constipation were related with seropositivity. Rodent presence was more frequent in households of seropositive individuals, while feline contact coincided with reduced rodent occurrence. Spatial analysis identified one high-risk cluster (71.4% [5/7], p>0.05) of seropositivity and one low-risk cluster (0% [0/14], p>0.05), the latter corresponding to areas where contact with felines is greater. Conclusions HEV exposure may be substantial in this Argentine rural community, supporting the need for integrated One Health surveillance targeting sanitation, reservoirs and food safety. Larger studies are warranted to validate these findings and better define transmission pathways.

title: Neonatal outcomes and immune reprogramming induced by prenatal opioid and hepatitis C exposure
abstract: Introduction Prenatal opioid exposure (POE) is an escalating public health concern. However, its impact on neonatal immune development remains poorly defined. This study examined how POE, with or without maternal hepatitis C (hepatitis C virus, HCV) infection, shapes neonatal immunity. Methods Umbilical cord blood was collected from pregnancies included uncomplicated term controls (n=38) and deliveries in patients with severe opioid use disorder on medication-assisted treatment, with (n=41) or without HCV (n=34) infection. Flow cytometry was used to characterize cell phenotype and functional response to stimulation. Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to investigate transcriptomics changes. Results POE was associated with smaller birth size, higher rates of congenital anomalies, and longer intensive care admissions. Immune profiling showed a proinflammatory milieu, reduced circulating levels of neuroprotective factors, expanded memory/effector T and B cells, blunted T-cell responses, and markedly reduced natural killer (NK) cell frequency and cytotoxicity, especially in POE HCV+ newborns. Monocytes exhibited inflammatory reprogramming with impaired antiviral and tissue repair pathways and disrupted lymphoid–innate immune cell communication. Discussion These findings suggest that POE-driven immune disequilibrium may underlie adverse early-life outcomes and highlight monitoring and intervention targets.

title: Modern possibilities of antiviral therapy for chronic viral hepatitis C in children aged 3 to 17 in the Moscow Region
abstract: Aim to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir (GLE/PIB) in two dosage forms and velpatosvir/sofosbuvir (VEL/SOF) in children 317 years old with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) in the Moscow region. Material and methods. We analyzed the results of treatment of 108 children over 3 years old with chronic hepatitis C who received in routine practice: GLE/PIB 50 mg/20 mg in granules (34 patients 3—12 years old) or GLE/PIB 300 mg/120 mg tablets (55 patients 12—17 years old) for a course of 8 weeks (with no experience in treating 88 children) and 16 weeks (with experience in treatment with interferon, 1 patient) or VEL/SOF 100 mg/400 mg tablets (19 patients 7—13 years old) for a course of 12 weeks. In 62.3% of children with HCV were diagnosed with concomitant diseases (including cancer), in 35.2% liver disease, in 3.7% extrahepatic manifestations, in 22.2% a high viral load (106—107 IU / ml) and in 23.1% social burden. To ensure compliance, communication technologies were used (keeping patient diaries, weekly communication with the attending physician and patient reporting). The rate of sustained virological response 12 weeks after GLE/PIB or VEL/SOF (SVR12) did not depend on the dosage form of DAAs, age, viral load, concomitant diseases and in children with HCV GT1, GT2, GT4 and untyped GT was 100% (95% CI 94.5—100), GT3 97.6% (95% CI 87.7—99.6). Lack of effectiveness in one teenager with a socially burdened history was associated with irregular use of the drug. 24 weeks after the end of DAA, the incidence of liver fibrosis grade 1—2 according to the METAVIR scale decreased from 24.1% to 8.3% ( p < 0.001). Adverse events (25%) were mild, consistent with the seasonal disease spectrum (88.9%), and in most cases were not related to DAA use. In 2.8% of cases, when taking GLE/PIB, a temporary and asymptomatic increase in total bilirubin was recorded. The high efficacy and safety profile of the pangenotypic DAA regimens GLE/PIB (in two dosage forms) and VEL/SOF for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C in children 3 years of age and older has been proven using communication technologies and substantiates the possibility of a simplified regimen for the management of children with HCV.

title: Temporal dissection of hepatitis C virus and orthoflavivirus infections by continuous luminescence monitoring
abstract: ABSTRACT Virus infection is a dynamic process consisting of rapidly evolving viral and host events, yet conventional endpoint assays provide only fragmented snapshots of these processes. Here, we established a unified temporal framework for dissecting virus–host interactions by integrating continuous bioluminescence monitoring with molecular and functional analyses. Real-time monitoring of hepatitis C virus (HCV) single-round infectious particles (SRIPs) revealed a biphasic replication profile consisting of an initial transient phase, followed by replication-dependent amplification. This transition was independently validated by similar HCV RNA kinetics observed after infection with HCV SRIPs or fully infectious HCV. Extension of this approach to dengue, Zika, and yellow fever virus SRIPs demonstrated that infection kinetics are determined by virus-specific replication programs and are modulated by the combination of viral replicons/capsids and prM/E proteins. This temporal framework enabled the identification of virus–host interactions that are difficult to resolve by conventional endpoint analyses. Early-phase cytoplasmic proteomics, combined with functional screening, identified the dynein light chain component DYNLRB2 as a previously unrecognized negative regulator of early HCV infection. Continuous monitoring also distinguished phase-specific antiviral activities, revealing distinct kinetic inhibition profiles for daclatasvir, acetylsalicylic acid, and interferon-α. Furthermore, delayed activation of the ER stress sensor ATF6 was first detected 40–47 h after HCV infection, and transcriptomic analysis at reporter-defined time points characterized the accompanying transition in host gene expression. Together, our study establishes continuous temporal monitoring as a general strategy for resolving dynamic virus–host interactions and for uncovering molecular events that remain obscured by conventional endpoint analyses. IMPORTANCE Viral infection is a dynamic process in which entry, genome amplification, host-factor requirements, antiviral effects, and cellular responses occur on different timescales. Conventional endpoint assays can identify changes in these processes but provide limited information about when they emerge or transition from one stage to another. Here, we show that continuous monitoring, when combined with direct molecular and functional measurements, can place these otherwise separate observations within a common temporal framework. Using HCV and related orthoflavivirus SRIPs, we resolved early and replication-associated phases, identified host factors with stage-dependent effects, and distinguished profiles of antiviral inhibition. We further showed that ATF6-mediated ER stress activation emerged later than early HCV infection and viral RNA amplification. Thus, continuous temporal monitoring provides a general strategy for resolving dynamic virus–host interactions by defining the temporal relationships among viral processes, pharmacological effects, and host responses that remain obscured by conventional endpoint analyses.

Thus, continuous temporal monitoring provides a general strategy for resolving dynamic virus–host interactions by defining the temporal relationships among viral processes, pharmacological effects, and host responses that remain obscured by conventional endpoint analyses.

title: Occurrence of Norovirus and Hepatitis A Virus RNA in Agricultural Soil from Produce Farms in Ohio and Georgia
abstract: Although foodborne viruses are considered ubiquitous in the environment, studies on their presence in soil are largely lacking. In this field study, 168 agricultural soil samples were collected from farms in Georgia and Ohio over seven and eight months, respectively. A total RNA isolation method was developed, and extracted genetic material was analyzed using reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) to detect human norovirus and hepatitis A virus (HAV) RNA. Nearly 6% of samples (n = 10) tested positive for HAV RNA, while norovirus genogroup I and II were detected in 1.2% (n = 2) and 0.6% (n = 1) of samples, respectively. Despite samples being stored at −20 °C for an average of two years prior to testing, viruses remained detectable, although in low levels. CrAssphage DNA and pepper mild mottle virus (PMMoV) RNA were assessed as indicators of human fecal contamination in positive samples; however, neither was detected, precluding any correlation with the viral pathogens—likely due to differing characteristics between the indicators and target viruses. These findings provide valuable insight into the prevalence and diversity of foodborne viruses in agricultural soil and highlight its potential as a vehicle for virus transport to other matrices within a fresh produce farm environment.

title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
abstract: Abstract Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions.

title: Acute hepatitis E presenting with fulminant myocarditis and cardiogenic shock: A case report from Nepal
abstract: Hepatitis E virus infection is endemic in Nepal and commonly presents as an acute self-limiting hepatitis. Cardiac involvement is extremely rare and may be life-threatening. We report a case of a young female who presented with fever, jaundice, progressive dyspnea and hypotension. Laboratory assessment confirmed acute hepatitis E infection. Chest radiography revealed cardiomegaly with bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated left ventricular dysfunction. Other infectious causes of myocarditis were excluded. The patient improved with inotropic support, heart failure treatment and other supportive management, with complete clinical recovery on follow-up. This case highlights the importance of early cardiac evaluation in patients with acute hepatitis E with features of heart failure.

title: Structural and biochemical insights into HCV envelope proteins for germline-targeting vaccines
abstract: Despite effective antivirals, Hepatitis C remains a global health burden, reflecting the difficulty of eliciting broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs). For the Hepatitis C virus, bnAb responses are biased toward VH1-69-encoded Abs targeting a conserved epitope on the E2 glycoprotein, suggesting that effective immunogens must engage the corresponding germline (GL) B cell receptors. However, the structural basis of GL recognition remains unclear. Here, we show that GL-reverted VH1-69 bnAbs recognize the E2 core domain in a manner closely resembling mature Abs binding. High-resolution structures reveal a conserved mode of engagement, indicating that key epitope features are accessible prior to affinity maturation. Guided by these insights, we engineered E2 variants to enhance GL Ab interactions and stability. Although these designs increased affinity, they did not improve engagement of naïve B cells, highlighting a key constraint in GL-targeting strategies. Together, our findings define principles governing GL recognition and inform the rational design of an HCV vaccine.

title: The Most Important Causes of Infection Transmission among Medical Healthcare and Laboratory Staff for Communicable Disease
abstract: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and bloodborne pathogen exposures present severe occupational hazards to frontline medical, health, and laboratory staff. While infection prevention and control (IPC) guidelines exist, behavioral and institutional barriers frequently compromise workplace safety. This study aimed to identify primary transmission pathways, assess infection control knowledge and post-exposure practices, and evaluate institutional training coverage among healthcare personnel at Azadi Teaching Hospital in Kirkuk, Iraq. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 110 medical, health and laboratory staff selected by random sampling. Data were collected with a structured self-administered questionnaire covering demographic and professional characteristics, recognised transmission routes, knowledge of bloodborne pathogen risks, post-exposure practices, hand hygiene and prior infection control training, and were analysed with descriptive statistics. Nurses (39.1%) and laboratory technicians (30.9%) formed the largest groups, and 32.7% of participants had never received formal infection control training. Direct contact with patients or contaminated materials was identified as the main transmission route by 55.5%. HIV was perceived as the highest-risk bloodborne pathogen by 66.1%, whereas only 15.6% each chose HBV and HCV. Only 46.4% correctly reported washing the wound as the first step after a needle-stick injury, while 40.0% reported squeezing the wound; 56.0% knew the recommended handwashing duration. Staff showed basic awareness of transmission pathways but substantial gaps in training coverage, bloodborne risk perception and post-exposure practice. Mandatory continuous infection prevention and control training, standardised post-exposure protocols and curricula emphasising viral hepatitis are recommended.

title: Suspected fibrosing cholestatic hepatitis in an immunocompetent child with hepatitis C: Case report
abstract: Abstract A 12‐year‐old boy presented to our center with elevated aminotransferases, jaundice, right upper quadrant tenderness, and hepatomegaly. Evaluation revealed a highly elevated blood hepatitis C virus (HCV) ribonucleic acid (RNA) level, and liver biopsy showed canalicular and intrahepatic cholestasis, feathery degeneration of hepatocytes, and periportal/perisinusoidal fibrosis. Though there were atypical biopsy features, including absence of bile ductular reaction, we diagnosed suspected fibrosing cholestatic hepatitis (FCH). FCH secondary to HCV infection has been reported exclusively in immunosuppressed adults. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of suspected FCH in a child, and the first reported case of suspected HCV‐related FCH in any immunocompetent patient. Our patient was successfully treated with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with sustained virologic response at 12 weeks. We conclude that FCH should be considered on the differential whenever any child with HCV infection presents with evidence of worsening liver injury including new hepatomegaly or jaundice.

title: FAKTOR-FAKTOR YANG BERHUBUNGAN DENGAN PEMERIKSAAN TRIPLE ELIMINASI PADA IBU HAMIL: LITERATURE REVIEW
abstract: Triple eliminasi merupakan program kesehatan nasional yang bertujuan mencegah penularan HIV, sifilis, dan hepatitis B dari ibu ke anak melalui pemeriksaan skrining selama kehamilan. Meskipun telah menjadi bagian dari pelayanan antenatal terpadu, cakupan pemeriksaan triple eliminasi di Indonesia masih belum mencapai target yang ditetapkan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis faktor-faktor yang berhubungan dengan pemeriksaan triple eliminasi pada ibu hamil melalui pendekatan literature review. Penelusuran literatur dilakukan melalui database Google Scholar dan Garuda dengan kriteria artikel penelitian original berdesain cross sectional yang dipublikasikan tahun 2023–2026. Sebanyak sepuluh artikel dianalisis menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif naratif. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa pengetahuan, sumber informasi, motivasi, dan sikap ibu hamil merupakan faktor yang paling konsisten berhubungan dengan pemeriksaan triple eliminasi. Dukungan suami, peran tenaga kesehatan, akses layanan kesehatan, serta karakteristik sosiodemografi juga memiliki hubungan terhadap pelaksanaan pemeriksaan, meskipun hasilnya bervariasi antarwilayah. Penguatan edukasi kesehatan, peningkatan keterlibatan keluarga, dan optimalisasi peran tenaga kesehatan diperlukan untuk meningkatkan cakupan pemeriksaan triple eliminasi pada ibu hamil secara merata dan berkelanjutan.

title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model integrating ctDNA methylation and clinical features for diagnosing hepatocellular carcinoma in HBV-infected patients with intrahepatic nodules
abstract: Distinguishing hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) from non-HCC nodules remains challenging in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. We developed an interpretable machine-learning model that integrates baseline circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) methylation readouts with clinical variables for this specific diagnostic setting. The cohort included 586 patients, with 217 adjudicated HCC outcomes. The existing 411-patient training and 175-patient internal-validation partition was retained. Eleven baseline predictors previously selected by Boruta and LASSO were used. Ten algorithms underwent nested stratified cross-validation with 10 outer and five inner folds, regularized candidate settings, and a one-standard-error selection rule. Model selection and classification thresholds used training data. Frozen models were evaluated internally, and SHAP was used to explain CatBoost predictions. After feature selection using both Boruta and LASSO, eleven features were retained: age, cirrhosis, maximum intrahepatic nodule diameter, AFP-L3%, AFP, DCP, ALBI grade, AST, HIST1H3G/ACTB, OTX1/ACTB, and NLR. SHAP analysis was subsequently performed to quantify and visualize the contribution of each feature to the model predictions. Among the evaluated machine learning models, CatBoost achieved the highest observed area under the receiver operating characteristic curve in the internal validation set (AUC = 0.903). The sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), F1 score, and Youden’s index were 0.800, 0.818, 0.811, 0.722, 0.874, 0.759, and 0.618, respectively. The integrated CatBoost model demonstrated strong diagnostic performance for identifying HCC among HBV-infected patients with intrahepatic nodules by integrating clinical characteristics, laboratory indicators, and ctDNA methylation markers. The model provided an interpretable framework for distinguishing HCC from non-HCC nodules and showed potential as an auxiliary tool for individualized assessment of HCC likelihood after nodule detection. However, the use of historically derived feature selection and the reuse of the internal validation set may limit the robustness of the validation.
